summaries.title: Getting to know Sami: home, work, family, running
summaries.text: Sami introduced himself: he lives in Porto and works as a structural engineer at Aurelia Bridges. He has a lazy four-year-old greyhound called Pixel, is allergic to shellfish, and his partner Noor teaches chemistry at a secondary school. Kazma drew up a 12-week plan for the Lisbon half marathon on March 22 (three easy runs a week, a Sunday long run growing from 8 to 18 km, a two-week taper) and suggested Cantinho do Avillez for Noor's birthday dinner: seafood for her, a meat menu for him. Left open: booking the dinner.

summaries.title: Passport renewal, the Tagus retrofit, Maya's new school
summaries.text: Sami's passport expires on 14 March 2031; Kazma will remind him in September 2030 to renew it. At work he now leads the Tagus footbridge retrofit, due at the end of June, under his manager Ines Carvalho, who likes detailed status reports; Kazma offered a milestone plan. His daughter Maya, seven, started at Escola Azul: school begins at 8:40, so they leave home by 8:10 and a 7:30 alarm leaves time for breakfast.

summaries.title: Lisbon trip bookings and a laptop battery fix
summaries.text: For the Lisbon half marathon trip the hotel is booked (reference ZX4-91Q) and the flight is TP1352 on March 20 at 07:15; Kazma advised being at the airport by 05:45. Separately, Sami's ThinkPad X1 Carbon battery was draining fast: Kazma suggested an 80 percent charge threshold in Lenovo Vantage and the Better Battery power mode.

summaries.title: Keep the Octavia or buy an electric car
summaries.text: Sami considered selling the 2019 Skoda Octavia estate and buying an electric car, probably a Kia EV6; Kazma noted its good range and said to check home charging first. A few days later he decided to keep the Octavia for another year.

summaries.title: Half marathon training: week one
summaries.text: Week one of the 12-week plan for the Lisbon half marathon: three easy 5 km runs and an 8 km Sunday long run. Kazma: keep the easy runs truly easy.

summaries.title: Half marathon training: first check-in
summaries.text: Sami's long run this week was 10 km at an easy pace, knees fine. Kazma advised keeping long runs conversational and adding 1-2 km a week toward the Lisbon half marathon.

summaries.title: Half marathon training: 12 km and a tight calf
summaries.text: Sami ran 12 km on Sunday for the Lisbon half marathon, and his left calf was tight afterwards. Kazma suggested stretching and foam-rolling, and cycling instead of one easy run if it stayed tight. Left open: whether the calf recovers.

summaries.title: Half marathon training: 13 km, calf recovered
summaries.text: The calf recovered. Sami ran 13 km at 5:40 per km, a good steady pace for his half marathon goal.

summaries.title: Half marathon training: a missed long run
summaries.text: Sami skipped this week's long run because of work on the Tagus retrofit. Kazma said one missed week is fine: pick the plan up again without making up the distance.

summaries.title: Half marathon training: 14 km and intervals
summaries.text: Back on track with a 14 km long run and one interval session added. Kazma: keep intervals to once a week so the long run stays fresh.

summaries.title: Half marathon training: 16 km, felt strong
summaries.text: Sami ran 16 km and felt strong at the end; two more build weeks, then the taper before the Lisbon half marathon.

summaries.title: Half marathon training: longest run, 18 km
summaries.text: Sami's longest run ever: 18 km at an average 5:35 per km. Kazma said race day is well within reach; the taper starts next week.

summaries.title: Half marathon training: taper week
summaries.text: Taper week: only 10 km on Sunday and fresh legs. Sami's goal for the Lisbon half marathon is under two hours, which Kazma judged realistic from his long runs.

summaries.title: Half marathon training: last long run and a massage
summaries.text: The last long run before the Lisbon half marathon: 8 km easy. Sami booked a sports massage for Thursday, which Kazma judged well timed.

summaries.title: Lisbon half marathon: finished in 1:56:40
summaries.text: Sami finished the Lisbon half marathon in 1:56:40, under his two-hour goal, on his first attempt.

Fewer slides with more visual weight usually outperform dense decks); What is accreditation and why does it matter for online courses (Accreditation is official recognition that an institution meets quality standards set by an external body, and it matters because it affects credit transfer, financial aid, and employer trust); Quiz me on Spanish irregular verbs (Conjugate 'ir' in the present tense: yo voy, tú vas, él va, nosotros vamos, ellos van).

summaries.title: Money questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Give me a quick formula for break-even in units (Divide total fixed costs by the contribution margin per unit (price minus variable cost per unit)); What's the difference between a budget and a spending plan (They are largely the same thing, though 'spending plan' is often used to sound less restrictive and to emphasize intentional allocation); Write a short checklist for setting up a budget (List income, total fixed costs, estimate variable costs, set savings goals, then assign limits and track for a month); Compare a certificate of deposit and a savings account for parking cash (A CD typically locks in a fixed rate for a set term but charges penalties for early withdrawal, while savings accounts stay flexible with variable rates); Give an example of a regressive tax (A sales tax on basic groceries is often regressive because it takes a larger share of income from lower earners); Is a 6% rate good for a mortgage right now (That depends on current market benchmarks, but 6% is generally considered moderate by recent historical standards).

summaries.title: Tool runs: tests, disk, files, servers
summaries.text: The user asked: check this command for errors: npm test -- --watch (The command is valid; it runs the test script and passes `--watch` to the underlying runner if supported); What does high CPU usage actually mean (It means the processor is spending most of its cycles doing work rather than sitting idle. Sustained near-100% usage usually points to a busy or stuck process); Is cloud sync a backup (No — sync services replicate deletions and ransomware encryption across devices, so they only count as backup if versioning or an isolated copy exists); Why do sync conflicts happen (Two devices edit the same file before either uploads the change, so the service can't tell which version wins and saves both or flags a conflict).

summaries.title: Travel questions
summaries.text: The user asked: What's the best time of year to visit Iceland (June to August for hiking, winter for the northern lights); What does travel insurance usually cover (Most policies cover medical emergencies, trip cancellation, lost baggage, and emergency evacuation, though specifics vary by plan); What's the difference between a bay and a gulf (A gulf is generally larger and more deeply indented into the coastline than a bay, though the terms are not strictly defined); What currency is used in Budapest (Hungary uses the forint (HUF), though many tourist spots accept euros. Cards are widely accepted, but keep some cash for markets); Do I need a visa for Japan (Visa requirements depend on nationality; many countries get visa-free stays of 90 days, so check your passport's rules); Compare downhill and cross-country skiing in two sentences (Downhill skiing uses gravity and lifts to descend steep groomed or off-piste terrain at speed. Cross-country skiing relies on self-propulsion over flatter trails, emphasizing endurance over adrenaline).

summaries.title: أسئلة متفرقة
summaries.text: سأل المستخدم: ليش تُعد معركة حطين مهمة؟ (لأنها انتصر فيها المسلمون بقيادة صلاح الدين واستعادوا القدس بعدها.)؛ ليش نقول كتبت بالقلم والباء هنا وش وظيفتها؟ (الباء حرف جر، والقلم اسم مجرور بالباء وعلامة جره الكسرة.)؛ عندي مساحة صغيرة في البلكونة، شنو أزرع فيها؟ (ازرع أعشاب مثل النعناع والريحان أو خضار صغير في أصص، وتناسب المساحات الضيقة.)؛ هل يحتاج الجوال برنامج حماية؟ (إذا تنزل تطبيقات من المتاجر الرسمية ما تحتاج غالباً، بس الحرص زين.)؛ كيف أسعّر منتجاتي عشان أربح وما أخسر العملاء؟ (احسب التكلفة الكاملة وزيد هامش ربح معقول، وقارن أسعارك بالسوق، وجرب تعدل السعر حسب رد فعل العملاء.)؛ ليش الحكم يطلع كرت أصفر؟ (يطلعه للإنذار على مخالفة أو سلوك غير رياضي، وإذا تكرر يتحول لأحمر ويُطرد اللاعب.)

summaries.title: Programming questions
summaries.text: The user asked: What does HTTP status 429 mean (Too Many Requests: you are being rate limited); Quick one: what does umask 022 set (It makes new files get 644 and new directories get 755 by default, masking out group and other write); Replace negative values in a numpy array with zero (Use np.where(arr < 0, 0, arr) or arr.clip(min=0) to set negatives to zero); Give me a one-liner to add a user to the sudo group on Debian (usermod -aG sudo username adds the user to the sudo group; they must log in again for it to take effect); Write a short example of a worker pool using channels (Create a jobs channel, start N goroutines ranging over it, send work items into jobs, and close it to let workers exit).

summaries.title: General knowledge questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Spot the fallacy: Everyone believes it, so it must be true (That's an appeal to popularity (argumentum ad populum); widespread belief doesn't establish truth); Why do we have different blood types (Blood types reflect different antigens on red blood cells, and immune antibodies against foreign types evolved partly as defense against infections); Write a two-line poem about Saturn's rings (Rings of ice in silent spin, a halo bound by gravity's thin. They stretch some 280,000 km wide yet are often just tens of meters thick); What is the pH of pure water at room temperature (Pure water has a pH of 7 at 25 °C, which is neutral); What's the tallest building in the world right now (The Burj Khalifa in Dubai, standing at 828 meters, has been the tallest since 2010); Write a one-sentence summary of the Baroque period in music (The Baroque era (roughly 1600–1750) emphasized ornate ornamentation, continuous bass lines, and dramatic expression, culminating in the works of Bach, Handel, and Vivaldi).

summaries.title: Home and garden questions
summaries.text: The user asked: How many boxes does a typical one-bedroom flat need (A one-bedroom flat usually needs roughly 20 to 30 medium boxes plus a few large ones for bedding and bulky items. Book boxes can be borrowed or rented to cut costs); How do I get ink out of a white cotton shirt (Blot the stain with isopropyl alcohol, then rinse in cold water and launder with oxygen bleach); How much can a smart thermostat actually save on heating bills (Typically 8–15% on heating costs, with larger savings when schedules vary a lot. Savings depend on climate, house insulation, and correct setup); What causes static cling and how can it be reduced (Static builds up from friction between fabrics in dry air; adding a dryer sheet or a damp cloth to the dryer helps reduce it).

summaries.title: Learning and study
summaries.text: The user asked: Write a short list of activities to build phonemic awareness (Try rhyming games, clapping syllables, sound blending, and identifying the first sound in words); How do I roll my Rs in Spanish (Practice tongue trills with 'butter' said fast, then try 'perro' while keeping the tongue tip relaxed near the ridge); Check this outline logic: notes on pricing, then notes on costs, then a conclusion (The order works if costs inform pricing; otherwise present costs first so the pricing notes can reference them); What's the difference between urgent and important (Urgent tasks demand immediate attention, while important ones advance long-term goals. Prioritize important-but-not-urgent work, since it prevents future crises).

summaries.title: Devices and software
summaries.text: The user asked: Explain why context length matters (It sets how much prior text the model can consider, so longer context helps with big documents and long chats); Is a 15-inch laptop too big for a backpack (No, most standard backpacks fit a 15-inch laptop if the sleeve is at least 15 inches deep); Why do sites ask for a backup code (Backup codes let you get in if your main 2FA device is lost or broken. Store them offline somewhere separate from the device); Is it safe to reuse a password across sites (No — one breach then exposes every account sharing it; generate a distinct password per site instead); List the main parts of a laptop keyboard (Keycaps, switches or domes, a membrane or PCB, and a backplate or frame).

summaries.title: Writing help
summaries.text: The user asked: How do I open a wedding speech without sounding cliché (Start with a specific shared moment or a dry observation rather than 'For those who don't know me.' One concrete detail beats three generic jokes); Explain enjambment using a tiny example (In "I held the door / open," the sentence runs past the line break, so meaning spills into the next line); What is the difference between assonance and rhyme (Assonance repeats vowel sounds inside words, as in "deep green," while rhyme matches sounds at the ends of words); Pull out the three most important statistics from this report (Global renewable capacity grew 50% in 2023, solar accounted for three-quarters of that, and costs fell 12% year over year).

summaries.title: أسئلة متفرقة
summaries.text: سأل المستخدم: اقترح لي أماكن سياحية في صلالة (جبل دربات وعين جرزيز والشاطئ، وأفضل وقت للزيارة في الخريف.)؛ اعطني ثلاثة أمثلة على الأفعال الناسخة. (من الأفعال الناسخة: كان، صار، ليس، وكلها ترفع الاسم وتنصب الخبر.)؛ شنو دور بيت الحكمة في بغداد؟ (كان مركز ترجمة وعلوم، نُقلت فيه كتب اليونان والفارسية وازدهرت فيه العلوم.)؛ عطني جدول بسيط للعشر الأواخر من رمضان. (خصص وقت للقرآن والدعاء والقيام، وقلل السهر، واجعل لك ورد يومي ثابت.)؛ كيف انظف البطارية من التآكل؟ (افصل الأطراف ونظفها بفرشاة وماء وصودا خبز. انتبه للعيون واليدين.)؛ متى يبدأ الشتاء عندنا؟ (عادةً يبدأ البرد الحقيقي في ديسمبر، وتكون أبرد الفترات في يناير.)

summaries.title: Programming questions
summaries.text: The user asked: After resolving conflicts, what's the exact command to continue an interrupted rebase (Stage the resolved files with git add, then run git rebase --continue); What's the difference between flexbox and grid in one sentence (Flexbox lays out items along a single axis, while grid handles rows and columns simultaneously in two dimensions); Write a mock for an HTTP client that returns a 404 once, then 200 (Use side_effect=[response_404, response_200] on the mock so successive calls return different responses); Explain Dijkstra's algorithm briefly (It repeatedly extracts the closest unvisited node from a priority queue and relaxes its edges, finding shortest paths on non-negative weighted graphs); What does the ? after a group do, like (abc) (It makes the whole group optional, so it matches zero or one occurrence of abc); Compare optimistic and pessimistic concurrency control briefly (Optimistic control checks for conflicts at commit and retries on failure, while pessimistic control locks rows upfront to prevent conflicts).

summaries.title: Cooking questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Explain the difference between vegetarian and vegan diets (Vegetarians avoid meat but may eat dairy and eggs; vegans avoid all animal products, including honey and gelatin); Check whether a banana and coffee counts as a real breakfast (It provides quick carbs and caffeine but little protein, so adding yogurt, nuts, or an egg would make it more balanced); What makes Emirati machboos distinct (Machboos is distinguished by its spiced rice, dried lime, and meat or fish, often finished with rose water or saffron); Write a short vegan Caesar dressing recipe (Blend silken tofu, lemon juice, Dijon mustard, garlic, capers, and a little miso until smooth); Explain tempering chocolate like it's a quick science lesson (Tempering heats and cools chocolate so cocoa butter crystals set in a stable form, giving a glossy snap and preventing bloom); What's the fastest way to bake a potato (Microwave it for 5 minutes, then finish in a 450°F oven for 10 minutes for crispy skin. Total time is about 15 minutes).

summaries.title: General knowledge questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Was Metropolis silent (Yes, Fritz Lang's Metropolis (1927) was a silent film, though later versions added scores and sound elements); Is 'Ulysses' by James Joyce worth reading (It's famously difficult but rewarding, celebrated for its stream-of-consciousness style and dense allusions to Homer's 'Odyssey.'); Is it true that lightning never strikes the same place twice (No, that's a myth—tall structures like the Empire State Building are struck many times each year); Describe why the sky is blue in two sentences (Air molecules scatter shorter blue wavelengths of sunlight far more than red ones. That scattered blue light reaches your eyes from all directions); Give me three inventions from ancient China (Paper, gunpowder, and the magnetic compass all originated in China, along with printing and the mechanical clock); Check this: the printing press was invented in 1543 (That date is off; Johannes Gutenberg's movable-type printing press in Europe dates to around 1440–1450).

summaries.title: Hobbies and sport
summaries.text: The user asked: Write one sentence describing the goal of chess (The goal of chess is to checkmate the opponent's king, putting it in a position where it cannot escape capture); Explain the rules of Catan in three sentences (Players collect resource cards from hexes based on dice rolls, then trade and spend them to build roads, settlements, and cities. Settlements and cities earn victory points, and the first to 10 points wins. The robber blocks a hex and steals a card when a 7 is rolled); Check this: is a throw-in goal allowed if it goes straight in without touching anyone (No, a goal cannot be scored directly from a throw-in; a corner kick or goal kick would be awarded instead); Explain how to fix a dropped stitch in knitting (Use a crochet hook to catch the dropped stitch and ladder it back up by pulling the horizontal bars through the loop one by one); Explain the difference between a pin and a skewer (A pin traps a piece in front of a more valuable one so moving it loses material; a skewer attacks the valuable piece first, forcing it to move and expose the piece behind); Recommend a mystery series with a detective who isn't a police officer (Sue Grafton's Kinsey Millhone series features a private investigator; start with *A Is for Alibi*).

summaries.title: Home and garden questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Compare front-load and top-load washers for fabric wear (Front-loaders use gentler tumbling and less water, generally causing less fabric abrasion than agitator top-loaders); Explain the four-box method for decluttering (Label four boxes keep, donate, store, and trash, then sort each item into exactly one box as you handle it once); What's the difference between a wrench and a spanner (In US English, a wrench and a spanner are often the same tool. In UK English, a spanner usually refers to a fixed-size tool, while a wrench may be adjustable); Suggest a color palette for a small living room (Use light neutrals like white, cream, and pale gray with a few darker accents to make the space feel larger and brighter).

summaries.title: Money questions
summaries.text: The user asked: What are Treasury bonds (Treasury bonds are long-term U.S. government debt, generally considered very low risk because they're backed by the federal government's taxing power); Which is usually cheaper, term or whole life (Term life is typically much cheaper because it has no cash value and covers a limited period); What records should be kept for business mileage (Log the date, destination, business purpose, and miles driven for each trip, plus total annual mileage for the vehicle); Draft a brief policy note on expense reimbursement (Require itemized receipts, manager approval, submission within 30 days, and reimbursement only for reasonable business-related costs).

summaries.title: Travel questions
summaries.text: The user asked: What does passport validity of six months mean (It means your passport must remain valid for at least six months beyond your planned entry or exit date); Give me three foods to try in the Levant (Try kibbeh, fattoush and knafeh — all staples across Lebanon, Syria, Jordan and Palestine); Is Petra worth two full days (Yes, two days lets you see the main monuments plus the Monastery and the High Place of Sacrifice without rushing); Write a short checklist for what to do if a passport is lost abroad (Report to local police, contact your embassy or consulate, get an emergency travel document, and notify your airline and insurer. Keep photocopies and digital scans); Compare the Caribbean and the Mediterranean for beach holidays (The Caribbean offers warmer water, white-sand beaches, and a tropical hurricane season, while the Mediterranean has cooler winters, calmer summer seas, and denser historic coastal towns); How can a traveler find cheap intercity bus tickets (Compare aggregator sites with the operator's own site, and book a few days ahead for early-bird fares).

summaries.title: Writing help
summaries.text: The user asked: Give me a formal way to say 'I'm sorry for the mistake.' (Write: 'I sincerely apologise for the error and any inconvenience it may have caused.'); Write a short poem about a lighthouse (Stone tower leaning into wind, / it keeps one bright eye on the dark); How do you pronounce 'croissant' (It's pronounced 'kwah-SAHN' with a silent 't'); Compare a chronological CV with a functional CV (A chronological CV lists work history in reverse order, emphasizing career progression, while a functional CV focuses on skills and competencies, downplaying dates and job titles); Check this for tense consistency: She walks in and sat down (Both verbs should match: "She walked in and sat down" or "She walks in and sits down."); Is a couplet always two rhyming lines (Not always; a couplet is any two-line stanza, though in English it usually rhymes and shares the same meter).

summaries.title: أسئلة متفرقة
summaries.text: سأل المستخدم: شنو الفرق بين التمارين الهوائية وتمارين المقاومة؟ (الهوائية ترفع نبض القلب مثل المشي والسباحة، والمقاومة تقوي العضلات مثل رفع الأثقال.)؛ هل ممكن تعطيني قاعدة بسيطة لعلامات الترقيم؟ (خلي كل جملة تامة تنتهي بنقطة، واستخدم الفاصلة للفصل بين المعاني، وعلامة الاستفهام للسؤال.)؛ كيف أقدر أشتري بضاعة بسعر أرخص؟ (قارن بين أكثر من مورد واطلب عينات قبل الشراء بالكمية. الشراء بالجملة يخفض السعر بس تأكد من الجودة أول.)؛ أبي أعرف طريقة أم علي بسرعة (افرك العجين المطهو مع الحليب والسكر، وحط فوقه مكسرات وزبيب وادخله الفرن لين يحمر.)؛ صوت طقطقة بالمكينة شنو يعني؟ (ممكن نقص زيت أو مشكلة بالمكينة نفسها. وقف السيارة وافحص الزيت فورًا.)؛ ليش القهوة تنشرب قبل التمرين؟ (القهوة تحسّن التركيز وترفع الأداء شوي، بس ما تكثر منها قبل الرياضة.)

summaries.title: Programming questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Explain a covering index simply (A covering index contains every column the query needs, so the database reads the index alone and never touches the table); Explain the difference between `interface` and `type` in TypeScript (Interfaces can be merged via declaration merging and are extendable; type aliases can represent unions, tuples, and other types, but cannot be merged); What does HTTP 404 mean (404 Not Found means the server can't locate the requested resource, though it may exist later); What is interior mutability and when is RefCell used (Interior mutability allows mutation through a shared reference; RefCell enforces borrow rules at runtime and panics on violations).

summaries.title: Cooking questions
summaries.text: The user asked: What temperature should leftovers be reheated to (Reheat to 165°F (74°C) and stir so it heats evenly throughout); Does a magnetic knife strip damage blades (No, it's fine for most knives as long as blades are dry before hanging. Avoid storing very brittle or delicate blades that could chip on contact); Give me a rule for how long eggs last (Refrigerated eggs typically keep 3–5 weeks from purchase; check the carton date); Explain umami and how to add it to plant dishes (Umami is a savory taste driven by glutamate; add it with miso, soy sauce, mushrooms, tomato paste, or nutritional yeast).

summaries.title: General knowledge questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Compare the difficulty of Sudoku and KenKen for beginners (Sudoku is usually easier for beginners because it only uses digit placement, while KenKen adds arithmetic constraints and cage rules); Did the Lumière brothers invent cinema, or was it Edison (Both contributed: Edison built the Kinetoscope for individual viewing, while the Lumières' 1895 Cinématographe projected films to paying audiences); Why do we yawn (Yawning likely helps regulate brain temperature and may serve a social bonding function, though the exact purpose is still debated); Give me three key figures of the Harlem Renaissance in music (Duke Ellington, Louis Armstrong, and Bessie Smith were central figures, though the movement also spanned literature and visual art); Do octopuses have three hearts (Yes, two pump blood to the gills and one pumps it to the rest of the body).

summaries.title: Hobbies and sport
summaries.text: The user asked: Can you explain how to read a knitting chart (Each square is one stitch, and each row is read bottom to top. Right-side rows read right to left; wrong-side rows read left to right, with symbols showing stitch type); Explain what bokeh means (Bokeh describes the quality of the out-of-focus areas, especially how highlights render as soft discs or harsh rings); How do I unlock the secret character in Super Smash Bros. Ultimate (Play versus matches or clear Classic mode to unlock characters like Luigi and Jigglypuff; each has specific conditions); Tell me about the history of the offside rule (The offside rule dates back to 19th-century English public school football, and FIFA has revised it several times, including the 1990 change allowing players to be level with the second-last defender); Check this: does a 35mm lens on a crop sensor give a wider field of view (No, it gives a narrower field of view, roughly like a 52mm lens on full frame with a 1.5x crop); Write a one-line caption for a sunrise landscape photo ("First light spills over the ridgeline, and the valley finally exhales.").

summaries.title: Home and garden questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Compare vinegar and bleach for killing mold in a shower (Vinegar works on light mold on tile and grout, while bleach is stronger for heavy growth on non-porous surfaces. Never mix the two, as it produces toxic gas); Can you check whether lemon juice damages granite countertops (Yes, lemon juice is acidic and can etch granite over time, so avoid leaving it on the surface. Use a pH-neutral stone cleaner instead); Is it cheaper to rent a truck and move yourself (Usually yes for short local moves, but factor in fuel, insurance, and time; full-service movers often win for long distances or stairs); List five ways to add warmth to a gray room (Add wood furniture, warm-toned textiles, brass accents, layered lighting, and a few plants).

summaries.title: Devices and software
summaries.text: The user asked: What's a quick way to remove extra spaces from text (Use =TRIM(A1) to strip leading, trailing, and repeated internal spaces); Explain the difference between VLOOKUP and INDEX MATCH (VLOOKUP searches only rightward from the lookup column, while INDEX MATCH can look in any direction and is more flexible when columns get inserted); Check this sentence for clarity: 'The bot, which was trained on data, responds to users quickly.' (It's grammatically fine and clear; consider trimming the commas if you want a tighter flow); How do I share my screen on Zoom (Click the green Share Screen button in the meeting toolbar, pick a window or tab, then click Share); Write a short checklist for setting up a new wireless printer (Unpack and remove tape, install ink or toner, power on, connect to Wi-Fi via the panel, then install drivers and print a test page); Which Wi-Fi standard is newer, Wi-Fi 6 or Wi-Fi 6E (Wi-Fi 6E is newer; it adds the 6 GHz band on top of the 2.4 and 5 GHz bands used by Wi-Fi 6).

summaries.title: Travel questions
summaries.text: The user asked: What does 'rail replacement bus' mean (It means buses replace trains on part of a route, usually during engineering work or disruptions); What's the difference between carry-on and personal item (A carry-on is the larger overhead-bin bag, while a personal item is a smaller bag that must fit under the seat in front of you); How high is the summit of Mount Rainier (The summit sits at 14,411 feet, the highest point in Washington state); Explain how maglev trains work (Maglev trains use magnetic levitation to lift the train above the track, eliminating friction, and linear motors to propel it forward).

summaries.title: Writing help
summaries.text: The user asked: Draft an opening sentence for a letter complaining about a delayed public service ("I am writing to express my concern regarding the significant delay in the service provided on 12 May."); Write a one-paragraph scene where two rivals must share one lantern (They set the lantern between them and said nothing, each counting the other's breaths. When the flame guttered, both reached at once, and the argument that followed was quieter than either expected); Shorten and soften: 'I demand an explanation for this error.' ('Could you help me understand what happened here?' is shorter and far less confrontational); Explain the key findings of this study like I'm in a hurry (Sleep under six hours correlated with a 20% higher risk of colds in the sample. The effect held after adjusting for age and exercise).

summaries.title: أسئلة متفرقة
summaries.text: سأل المستخدم: كيف أمنع نفسي من التسويف وقت المذاكرة؟ (حدد هدف صغير تخلصه في ١٥ دقيقة وابدأ فيه فوراً. البداية هي أصعب خطوة وبعدها تكمل.)؛ كيف أنشر موقع على GitHub Pages؟ (ارفع الملفات لمستودع واختار GitHub Pages من الإعدادات وحدد الفرع، وراح يطلع الرابط.)؛ فسر لي ظاهرة الكسوف والخسوف ببساطة (الكسوف يصير لما القمر يحجب الشمس عن الأرض، والخسوف لما الأرض تحجب ضوء الشمس عن القمر.)؛ شنو الفرق بين الدراسة الجماعية والفردية؟ (الجماعية تنفع للمناقشة وحل الأسئلة، والفردية أفضل للحفظ العميق. الأفضل تمزج بينهم.)؛ طلع لي أسئلة تدريبية عن موضوع الامتحانات (أسئلة مثل: شنو أفضل وقت للمراجعة؟ وشلون توزع وقتك في الامتحان؟ جاوب عليها بجملة قصيرة.)؛ عطني ملخص عن مناخ الخليج بشكل عام (مناخ الخليج حار صيفاً مع رطوبة عالية قرب الساحل، ومعتدل شتاءً مع أمطار قليلة. الفرق بين الليل والنهار يكون أوضح في الداخل.)

summaries.title: Programming questions
summaries.text: The user asked: How do I reverse a list in Python (Use my_list[::-1] for a copy or my_list.reverse() in place); How can I make a sticky footer layout with grid (Use grid-template-rows: auto 1fr auto on a full-height container so the middle row stretches and the footer stays at the bottom); What's the difference between useMemo and useCallback (useMemo memoizes a computed value; useCallback memoizes a function reference. useCallback(fn, deps) equals useMemo(() => fn, deps)); What are volumes and why use them (Volumes are Docker-managed storage that persists beyond a container's lifecycle and can be shared between containers; use them for databases and any data that must survive restarts).

summaries.title: Cooking questions
summaries.text: The user asked: What wood chips are best for smoking (Hickory and mesquite are strong, while apple and cherry are milder; choose based on the flavor intensity you want); How long do you cook dried penne (Dried penne usually cooks in 10 to 12 minutes; check the package for exact timing); Explain the pinch grip (Grip the handle with the last three fingers, pinch the blade's spine between thumb and index finger just ahead of the bolster, giving control and leverage); Why does my sourdough starter smell like nail polish remover (That acetone smell means the starter is starving and over-fermenting. Discard half, feed it at 1:1:1, and use it within a few hours of peaking); How long should chicken soup simmer (Simmer it for about 45 minutes to an hour so the chicken cooks through and the broth picks up flavor); How do I hold a chef's knife properly (Use a pinch grip: pinch the blade between thumb and forefinger just ahead of the bolster, with the remaining fingers wrapping the handle. This gives control and less wrist fatigue).

summaries.title: General knowledge questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Give me the capital of every country that starts with the letter K (Kabul (Afghanistan), Nur-Sultan (Kazakhstan), Nairobi (Kenya), Tarawa (Kiribati), Pristina (Kosovo), Kuwait City (Kuwait), and Bishkek (Kyrgyzstan)); What's the origin of the phrase 'bury the hatchet' (It refers to a Native American practice of burying weapons to signal peace, recorded in English since the 17th century); Check this fact: bats are blind (That is false; most bats can see, and many also navigate using echolocation); What's the origin of the phrase 'bite the bullet' (It likely refers to soldiers biting a lead bullet during surgery before anesthesia, though the exact origin is debated); Could you describe the structure of the Colosseum (It is an elliptical amphitheater with tiered seating, built from travertine, tuff, and concrete, and could hold over 50,000 spectators); Why do cats purr (Contentment mostly, but also to soothe themselves when stressed).

summaries.title: Devices and software
summaries.text: The user asked: Write a short checklist for cleaning a laptop keyboard safely (Power off and unplug, use compressed air at an angle, wipe with a lightly damp microfiber cloth, and avoid spraying liquid directly on the keys); Compare mesh systems and traditional routers (Mesh systems use multiple nodes for even coverage across large spaces, while a single router is cheaper and simpler but weaker at range); Convert a date in A1 to just the month name (Use =TEXT(A1,"mmmm") to display the full month name); Compare Outlook and Thunderbird for spam handling (Outlook has built-in Junk Email filtering with server-side rules, while Thunderbird relies on adaptive junk filters and third-party add-ons for advanced spam control); Rewrite 'the assistant gave a answer' correctly ("The assistant gave an answer.").

summaries.title: Tool runs: tests, disk, files, servers
summaries.text: The user asked: Give me a one-line command to run tests with coverage (Use pytest --cov=yourpackage tests/ if pytest-cov is installed); Give a command that counts commits on the current branch (Use git rev-list --count HEAD to get the number of commits reachable from HEAD. Add a branch name to count for another branch); Write a command to list all files in a directory on Linux (Use ls -a to list all files, including hidden ones, in the current directory); Quick way to see CPU load on macOS (Open Activity Monitor and check the CPU tab, or run `top -o cpu` in Terminal. Both show per-process CPU percentages live).

summaries.title: أسئلة متفرقة
summaries.text: سأل المستخدم: اكتب لي دعاء قصير ينقال وقت الإفطار. («اللهم إني لك صمت وعلى رزقك أفطرت»، وتقدر تضيف دعاء لنفسك بعدها.)؛ كم لتر ماي لازم أشرب في اليوم؟ (المعتاد من لترين لثلاثة، ويزيد إذا كان الجو حار أو فيه رياضة.)؛ اكتب لي رسالة شكر لمديري. (شكرا على دعمك المستمر وثقتك.)؛ صوت صفير عند التسريع شنو سببه؟ (ممكن سير المكينة مرتخي أو مضخة. يحتاج فحص عند ورشة.)؛ شنو ألعاب رمضان القديمة عند الخليجيين؟ (منها الكيرم وأم التسع، وكانوا يتجمعون بعد التراويح يلعبون ويسولفون.)؛ كيف تتنفس الأسماك تحت الماء؟ (عن طريق الخياشيم اللي تسحب الأكسجين من الماء وتطلقه للدم.)

summaries.title: Programming questions
summaries.text: The user asked: What does flex: 1 actually mean (It's shorthand for flex-grow: 1, flex-shrink: 1, and flex-basis: 0%, so the item grows to share free space equally); What does Promise.allSettled do (It returns a Promise that resolves after all input Promises settle, with an array of status objects for each); What's the difference between a stub and a mock (A stub returns canned data to make a test pass; a mock also records calls and lets you assert on interactions); What's the difference between microtasks and macrotasks (Microtasks (e.g., Promise callbacks) run before the next macrotask (e.g., setTimeout), and the event loop processes all microtasks after each macrotask); How to mock time in tests (Inject a clock interface or use a library like freezegun (Python) or Sinon fake timers (JS)); Explain the difference between &T and &mut T (&T is a shared reference allowing read-only access, while &mut T is an exclusive reference allowing mutation but no simultaneous aliases).

summaries.title: Cooking questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Quick check: does adding milk to tea reduce its antioxidants (It can bind some polyphenols, but the overall effect on antioxidant absorption is generally modest); Canned beans opened yesterday — still good (Yes if refrigerated in a sealed container; use within 3–4 days); Can you write a short poem about a simmering pot of stew (The pot hums low on winter's stove, / root and broth in slow embrace, / steam curls up like stories told, / warm as a hand upon the face); Does adding herbs at the start or end of cooking matter (Yes—hardy herbs like rosemary and bay release flavor slowly and go in early, while delicate ones like basil and cilantro lose aroma and are best added at the end); What spices go into garam masala (Cumin, coriander, cardamom, cloves, cinnamon and black pepper).

summaries.title: General knowledge questions
summaries.text: The user asked: What causes tides (The gravitational pull of the Moon and Sun, combined with Earth's rotation, raises and lowers the seas); What's the smallest number of coins that can't be made from 3s and 5s (1 can't be made, and also 2, 4, and 7; the largest impossible amount is 7); Give me a valid syllogism about birds ('All birds have feathers; all robins are birds; therefore all robins have feathers' is valid and sound); What causes the seasons on Earth (Earth's 23.4-degree axial tilt, which changes how directly sunlight strikes each hemisphere through the year); Check this statement: 'A trade deficit is always bad.' (That statement is not always true; trade deficits can reflect strong consumer demand and are not inherently harmful); What's the next number in the sequence 1, 4, 9, 16, 25 (36, since these are perfect squares: 1², 2², 3², 4², 5², 6²).

summaries.title: Health and fitness questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Compare caffeine and alcohol effects on sleep (Caffeine delays sleep onset and shortens deep sleep, while alcohol helps you fall asleep faster but fragments sleep and suppresses REM); Write a short script I can read while doing a breathing exercise ("Breathe in slowly through your nose... now out through your mouth, longer than the inhale... again, gently." Repeat those lines calmly for several cycles); Is it true that cold water is absorbed faster than warm water (No, absorption rates are similar; cold water may just feel more refreshing); Quick—what's the recovery position (Roll the person onto their side with the upper leg bent forward and the head tilted slightly back to keep the airway open); What is proper form for a deadlift (Keep the bar close to the shins, hinge at the hips with a flat back, drive through the heels, and stand tall without overextending); Explain how to treat a minor cut (Clean the wound with water, apply gentle pressure to stop bleeding, and cover it with a sterile bandage).

summaries.title: Hobbies and sport
summaries.text: The user asked: Is 'The Catcher in the Rye' still relevant today (Yes, its themes of alienation and identity resonate with modern readers, though some find the protagonist's voice dated); Compare monofilament and fluorocarbon leader for trout (Fluorocarbon sinks and is nearly invisible underwater, while monofilament floats and stretches more; trout in clear water favor fluoro leaders); Describe the layout of a Mahjong set (A Mahjong set typically includes 144 tiles: 36 each of bamboo, characters, and dots suits, plus winds, dragons, flowers, and seasons); How does the away goals rule work, and is it still used (The away goals rule once broke ties in two-legged matches by favoring the team that scored more away, but UEFA abolished it in 2021 for its competitions); Give me a quick tarp setup for rain (Rig an A-frame: tie a ridgeline between two trees, drape the tarp over it, and stake the corners low with taut lines to shed water); What's the best way to clean guitar strings (Wipe them with a dry microfiber cloth after playing, and use a small amount of string cleaner on a cloth rather than directly on the strings).

summaries.title: Home and garden questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Quick tip for decluttering paperwork (Handle paper once: file, scan, shred, or recycle on the spot, and keep only what has a legal or active use); Give me a checklist for securing a smart home network (Use a separate Wi-Fi network or VLAN for IoT, change default passwords, enable auto-updates, and disable unused remote access features); Does vinegar soften laundry (A half cup of white vinegar in the rinse cycle helps strip detergent residue and can soften fabrics mildly); Give me three ways to reduce smart home network congestion (Move devices to a separate Wi-Fi band or VLAN, prefer Thread or Zigbee for sensors, and limit cloud polling by using local integrations).

summaries.title: Travel questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Find cheap hostels near train stations in major cities (Search Hostelworld with the map view and filter by distance to the station, then compare ratings); Check whether an international driving permit is needed in Italy (Italy accepts a valid non-EU license with an official translation or an International Driving Permit, so carrying an IDP is the safest choice); What currency is used in Lebanon and can US dollars be used (The Lebanese pound is official, but US dollars are widely accepted and often preferred for larger payments); Suggest a short trip combining Jordan and Lebanon (Fly into Amman, see Petra and Wadi Rum, then fly to Beirut for a few days of coast and mountain villages); Which is easier to navigate without a car, Muscat or Manama (Manama is easier on foot and by taxi, while Muscat is spread out and car-dependent); Is Prague expensive for tourists (Cheaper than western Europe, especially outside the old town).

summaries.title: Writing help
summaries.text: The user asked: Is "living my best life" overused (Yes, it's widely considered a cliché and can read as generic. Fresher alternatives include "making the most of today" or something specific to the moment); What makes a good headline (A good headline is clear, specific, and promises value while using strong verbs and keywords to grab attention); Check this headline: 'Local Man Wins Award' (It's too vague; add specifics like the award name and man's field to make it compelling); What makes a good opening line (It raises a question the reader needs answered—specific, odd, or slightly wrong in a way that demands explanation); Give me a title for a blog post about remote work (Home Is Where the Standup Is); Give me three caption ideas for a coffee shop post (Try 'First sip, best sip,' 'Liquid motivation,' or 'Coffee: because mornings are a thing.').

summaries.title: أسئلة متفرقة
summaries.text: سأل المستخدم: ليش التطبيقات تستهلك بيانات وايد؟ (غالباً بسبب التحديثات التلقائية والفيديوهات، تقدر تحدد استهلاك البيانات لكل تطبيق من الإعدادات.)؛ عطني فكرة مشروع صغير. (مشروع توصيل وجبات صحية في الحي.)؛ اذكر لي أنواع الجموع في العربية (ثلاثة أنواع: جمع مذكر سالم، جمع مؤنث سالم، وجمع تكسير.)؛ ايش افضل طريقة للحفاظ على السيارة بالحر؟ (اركن بالظل وافحص السوائل والكفرات. شغل المكيف بعد التهوية شوي.)؛ أبي أزرع ريحان في أصيص، شنو لازم أعرف؟ (الريحان يحب الشمس والتصريف الزين، اسقيه لما يجف سطح التراب وقص الأطراف عشان يكثف.)؛ وش أحسن طريقة لحفظ القرآن؟ (التكرار اليومي والمراجعة المنتظمة.)

summaries.title: Programming questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Write the shorthand for grid-template-rows and columns in one line (Use grid-template: 'a a' 100px 'b c' 1fr / 200px 1fr;); Why do people say not to mock everything (Over-mocking couples tests to implementation details, so refactors break tests that never actually exercised real behavior); Give me a checklist for diagnosing a slow endpoint in a web backend (Measure latency at each layer, check database query plans and indexes, profile CPU and allocations, and look for blocking I/O or lock contention); What's the cleanest way to remove unused images (`docker image prune` clears dangling images; add `-a` to remove all unused ones, which is more aggressive); How can I paginate results efficiently on a big table (Use keyset pagination with WHERE id > last_id ORDER BY id LIMIT 20 rather than large OFFSET values); How do I range over a channel (Use for v := range ch, which receives until the channel is closed, then exits the loop).

summaries.title: Cooking questions
summaries.text: The user asked: How do I thicken a soup without cream (Use a cornstarch or flour slurry, puree some of the vegetables, or stir in mashed potato to add body without dairy); Compare pesto and tomato sauce (Pesto is uncooked, herb-based, and fresh, while tomato sauce is cooked and tangy-sweet); List the main ingredients in a traditional tiramisu (Ladyfingers, mascarpone, eggs, sugar, espresso, and cocoa powder, often with a splash of Marsala); Why does my French press coffee taste muddy (Fine grounds or over-steeping cause it; use a coarse grind and steep for about 4 minutes before pressing slowly).

summaries.title: General knowledge questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Name three films by Akira Kurosawa (Rashomon, Seven Samurai, and Ran are three well-known Kurosawa films); How long does a red blood cell live (A red blood cell circulates for about 120 days before being broken down and recycled, mostly in the spleen and liver); Compare Beethoven and Mozart briefly (Mozart was a Classical-era prodigy known for effortless melodic clarity, while Beethoven bridged into Romanticism with more dramatic, structurally ambitious works. Beethoven's career overlapped Mozart's only slightly, as Mozart died in 1791 when Beethoven was 20); What is chiaroscuro (Chiaroscuro is the strong contrast between light and dark used to model forms and create drama, as in Caravaggio's work); What's GDP (GDP, or Gross Domestic Product, is the total monetary value of all finished goods and services produced within a country's borders in a specific time period); Why do wolves howl (Wolves howl to communicate over long distances, coordinate pack hunts, and defend territory from rival packs).

summaries.title: Home and garden questions
summaries.text: The user asked: How high should pendant lights hang over a kitchen island (Hang pendants about 30 to 36 inches above the countertop for proper task lighting and visual balance); How much power does a smart plug use on standby (Most draw about 0.5 to 2 watts continuously, which is roughly 4 to 17 kWh per year per plug); Write a one-line reminder to unplug unused chargers ("Unplug idle chargers — they sip power even with nothing attached."); Write a short checklist for winterizing an outdoor faucet (1. Disconnect hoses. 2. Shut off the indoor valve. 3. Drain the pipe. 4. Open the outdoor spigot to let remaining water escape).

summaries.title: Learning and study
summaries.text: The user asked: List three common mistakes in algebra exams (Sign errors when distributing, forgetting to flip inequalities when multiplying by negatives, and dropping units or terms); Invent a fun game to practice letter sounds (Play 'sound hunt': call out a sound like /m/ and have the child race to find an object in the room starting with that sound); Should a speaker use a microphone in a room of 40 people (Usually yes if one is available — amplification lets you speak at a relaxed volume and keeps the back rows engaged); Draft a two-line rule for handling email without losing focus (Check email only at scheduled times, never first thing in the morning. Process each message once: reply, delegate, or schedule it); Is a nanodegree the same as a certificate (A nanodegree is a type of certificate offered by Udacity, focused on job-ready technical skills).

summaries.title: Money questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Check whether 100 Canadian dollars is more or less than 70 euros (100 Canadian dollars is worth about 68 euros, so slightly less than 70 euros); List three ways to improve a credit score (Pay bills on time, reduce credit card balances, and avoid opening too many new accounts); Write a short note asking a lender to correct an error on a credit report (Here's a draft: "I am writing to dispute an inaccurate item on my credit report and request that it be investigated and corrected under the Fair Credit Reporting Act."); Does a weaker currency help a country's exports (Generally yes, because goods become cheaper for foreign buyers, though import costs rise and the effect can take time).

summaries.title: Devices and software
summaries.text: The user asked: Draft a two-line meeting invite for a 30-minute video call about budget review ("Video call: Budget Review, 30 minutes. Agenda: review current figures and agree next steps. Join link and passcode below."); Summarize the main risks of deploying AI assistants (Key risks include inaccurate outputs, privacy leaks, bias, and overreliance without human review); Should recovery codes be stored offline (Yes, printing them or keeping them in an offline safe place prevents an attacker with email or cloud access from using them); Do power banks with higher mAh always charge phones more times (Not always, because conversion losses and voltage differences mean real output is lower than the rated mAh, often by 30-40%).

summaries.title: Tool runs: tests, disk, files, servers
summaries.text: The user asked: What does a detached HEAD mean in git status output (It means HEAD points directly at a commit rather than a branch, so new commits won't belong to any branch. git status warns about this and suggests checking out a branch); What does a TTL value in ping output tell you (TTL is the remaining hop count a packet can survive; its starting value hints at the remote OS. Values near 64, 128, or 255 suggest Linux, Windows, or network gear respectively); Compare ping and traceroute (Ping tests reachability and latency to one host, while traceroute maps the path and shows per-hop delays. Use ping first, then traceroute if latency or loss appears); ping the staging server (staging responded in 23 ms); What does git status show (It shows the working tree state: staged changes, unstaged modifications, and untracked files. It also notes the current branch and whether it's ahead or behind its upstream).

summaries.title: أسئلة متفرقة
summaries.text: سأل المستخدم: أبي أسمد النخلة، شنو الأنسب؟ (استخدم سماد عضوي متوازن حول الجذور، وضيفه في بداية الربيع وقبل الصيف.)؛ عطني معلومة عن صلاح الدين الأيوبي. (هو قائد أيوبي وحّد مصر والشام واستعاد القدس من الصليبيين سنة 1187.)؛ أبي حلى سهل ما يبي فرن (سوّ بسكويت مطحون مع زبدة في القالب، وفوقه خليط جبن وقشطة وحطّه بالثلاجة.)؛ أبغى أعرف كم سعرة يحرق الجري نص ساعة (حسب الوزن والسرعة، تقريباً من ٣٠٠ إلى ٤٠٠ سعرة في النص ساعة.)؛ شنو أفضل وقت أغير فيه زيت المكينة؟ (الأفضل كل ٥٠٠٠ إلى ١٠٠٠٠ كيلو حسب نوع الزيت، وتأكد من دليل السيارة.)؛ الفرق بين الضمة والفتحة وشو؟ (الضمة علامة الرفع وتنطق بضم الشفة، والفتحة علامة النصب وتنطق بفتح الفم.)

summaries.title: Programming questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Why does my Node app's memory keep climbing until it crashes (Likely a retained reference such as an unbounded cache, listener, or global array; take heap snapshots over time and diff them to find objects growing without release); What is optimistic concurrency control (Optimistic concurrency control lets transactions proceed without locks, checking for conflicts at commit time (e.g., using version numbers) and aborting if conflicts are detected); How do I read a CSV file with pandas (pandas.read_csv('file.csv') returns a DataFrame); Write a short JUnit test using Mockito (Create the mock with @Mock, inject via @InjectMocks, stub with when(repo.find(1)).thenReturn(user), and assert); How do I keep my branch up to date with main without a merge commit (Rebase your branch onto main with git rebase main, which applies your commits on top of the latest main); Why does my React component render twice (In development StrictMode renders twice on purpose to surface side effects).

summaries.title: General knowledge questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Why did the Ottoman Empire collapse (It dissolved after World War I, weakened by nationalist movements, economic strain, and defeat alongside the Central Powers; the sultanate was abolished in 1922); Write a short description of daily life in ancient Rome (Romans rose early, ate a light breakfast of bread and cheese, worked or attended the forum, and gathered for a main afternoon meal of grains, vegetables, and occasionally meat); Compare Gothic and Romanesque cathedrals (Gothic cathedrals feature pointed arches, flying buttresses, and large stained glass, while Romanesque ones have rounded arches, thick walls, and small windows); Give me a quick timeline of the New Hollywood movement (It ran roughly from the late 1960s to the early 1980s, when auteur-driven films like Bonnie and Clyde and The Godfather reshaped studio output); Summarize the story depicted in Botticelli's Primavera (It shows a spring allegory with Venus, the Three Graces, Flora, and Mercury in an orange grove, likely celebrating love and fertility); Write one sentence about why capital cities are often not the largest city (Capitals are sometimes chosen for central location or political compromise, like Canberra or Brasília, rather than for being the biggest city).

summaries.title: Health and fitness questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Quick trick to calm down fast (Try a physiological sigh: two short inhales through the nose, then one long exhale through the mouth. It's one of the fastest ways to reduce acute stress); What's the best way to remove a tick (Grip it close to the skin with fine tweezers and pull steadily upward, then clean the area); Does stretching prevent injury (Evidence is mixed; regular flexibility work may help, but gradual training and proper warm-ups are stronger injury-prevention factors); Can calcium supplements interfere with anything (Yes, calcium can reduce absorption of iron and some antibiotics, so timing matters); What's a good warm-up for a 10K run (Do 5–10 minutes of easy jogging, dynamic stretches like leg swings, and 3–4 short strides at race pace).

summaries.title: Home and garden questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Turn down the living room lights to 30 percent (I can't control devices directly, but that command fits standard dimmer syntax: "Set living room lights to 30 percent."); What do the laundry care symbols mean (A washtub means washing, a triangle means bleaching, a square means drying, an iron means ironing, and a circle means dry cleaning; dots and lines indicate temperature and cycle settings); What protocol does Matter use under the hood (Matter runs over IPv6 and typically uses Thread or Wi-Fi for transport, with Bluetooth Low Energy for initial commissioning); Give me three cheap ways to cut home energy use (Seal drafts, switch to LEDs, and lower the thermostat a few degrees. Each costs little and cuts energy quickly); Give me a step-by-step for hand-washing a delicate sweater (Fill a basin with cool water and mild detergent, gently squeeze the sweater through the water, rinse thoroughly, then roll it in a towel and lay flat to dry).

summaries.title: Money questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Does pet insurance cover routine checkups (Many pet policies focus on accidents and illness; routine checkups are often optional add-ons); Check whether $2,000 is enough for a three-month fund (That works only if essential monthly costs are about $667 or less; otherwise you'd need more); Check if flood damage is usually covered by standard homeowners insurance (Flood damage is typically not covered by standard homeowners insurance; separate flood insurance is needed); Check whether a bankruptcy stays on a report for seven or ten years (Chapter 7 bankruptcies generally stay ten years, while Chapter 13 typically stays seven years from the filing date).

summaries.title: Devices and software
summaries.text: The user asked: How can I estimate the cost of cloud storage (Estimate cost by multiplying stored data volume by the provider's per-GB rate, then add charges for operations, data transfer, and retrieval. Use provider calculators for accuracy); How do authenticator apps work (They generate time-based one-time codes from a shared secret, typically rotating every 30 seconds, and work without a network connection); How to combine first and last name columns with a space (Use =A2&" "&B2 or =CONCATENATE(A2," ",B2) to join them with a space); Explain why a long passphrase can beat a short complex password (Each added word multiplies the number of guesses needed, so a five-word random passphrase often has far more entropy than eight mixed characters); What does the Fn key actually do on a laptop (It activates secondary functions printed on other keys, like brightness, volume, or media controls, and often toggles with a Fn Lock setting); Briefly explain what channel bandwidth means for Wi-Fi (It's the width of the frequency range a channel uses; wider channels like 80 MHz carry more data but overlap more and are more prone to interference).

summaries.title: Travel questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Recommend a weekend itinerary for Seville (Alcazar, the cathedral, Triana and a flamenco show at night); How hot does Riyadh get in July (July highs in Riyadh average around 43°C, with nights rarely dropping below 30°C); Why do passports have different colors (Passport colors often reflect regional standards: red for many EU countries, blue for the Americas, and green for several Islamic nations); Check whether a Eurail Global Pass covers Italy and Switzerland (Yes, the Eurail Global Pass covers both Trenitalia and SBB services, though seat reservations are required on some high-speed and scenic routes); Why is the water at some beaches clearer than at others (Clear water usually means low sediment and nutrient levels, so places with little runoff or river input and calm wave action stay transparent); What time should I sleep on a flight to Tokyo from New York (Sleep during the last half of the flight so you wake near Tokyo morning, aligning your body with Japan time on arrival).

summaries.title: Writing help
summaries.text: The user asked: What's wrong with saying 'more unique' ("Unique" means one of a kind, so it can't logically be compared; write "unique" or "very unusual" instead); Check this sentence for grammar: 'I has extensive experience in project management.' (The sentence should be: "I have extensive experience in project management."); Translate "the cat is on the table" into French ("Le chat est sur la table."); Explain the rule of three in speechwriting (Grouping ideas in threes makes them memorable and rhythmic, like 'life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness.' Use it for lists, punchlines, and closing lines); What is a dangling modifier, with a quick example (It's a descriptive phrase that doesn't clearly attach to the subject, as in "Walking home, the rain started." Revise to "Walking home, I got caught in the rain."); Quick tip for captions on TikTok (Keep it brief and hooky, and use one or two trending hashtags. The first few words matter most).

summaries.title: أسئلة متفرقة
summaries.text: سأل المستخدم: ليش الناس يزورون الأهل أكثر في رمضان؟ (لأن الشهر يجمع الناس على الإفطار والتراويح، وتزيد فيه صلة الرحم.)؛ شنو الفرق بين المرق واليخنة؟ (المرق يكون أخف وأكثر سوائل، واليخنة أثقل وأسمك وتنطبخ على نار هادية.)؛ شكثر مدة الشوط الواحد في المباراة؟ (خمس وأربعون دقيقة، مع وقت بدل ضائع يضيفه الحكم.)؛ كم المسافة بين الكويت والرياض؟ (تقريبا ستمية كيلو بالسيارة.)؛ كيف أحمي كلمة المرور في قاعدة البيانات؟ (لا تخزنها كنص صريح، استخدم دالة تشفير مثل bcrypt مع ملح عشوائي.)؛ اذكر لي أسماء ثلاث صحاري كبيرة. (الصحراء الكبرى، صحراء الربع الخالي، وصحراء غوبي.)

summaries.title: Programming questions
summaries.text: The user asked: What does GROUP BY actually do (It collapses rows sharing the same values in the listed columns into one row each, usually for aggregate functions like COUNT or SUM); What is a race condition (Two operations on shared state whose result depends on timing); Can you check this test for problems: assert result is not None (That only proves it isn't None; assert something specific like the exact value or length so the test can actually fail); Compare a fast-forward merge and a three-way merge (A fast-forward just moves the branch pointer when there's no divergence, while a three-way merge creates a merge commit combining divergent histories); Is 100% coverage the goal (No — coverage shows untested code, not tested behavior; high coverage with weak assertions can still miss bugs); Write a quick Python snippet that prints the top growing object types using tracemalloc (Use tracemalloc.start(), take two snapshots, then compare them and sort statistics by size difference to print the top types).

summaries.title: Cooking questions
summaries.text: The user asked: What's a quick breakfast I can make in five minutes (Scrambled eggs on toast takes about four minutes total. Or microwave oatmeal with milk for two minutes); What is the difference between lasagne and lasagna ('Lasagne' is plural and refers to the sheets of pasta, while 'lasagna' is the singular dish; in Italy, the dish is called 'lasagne'); How do I tell if leftovers are unsafe (Discard them if they smell off, look slimy, or sat out over 2 hours; when in doubt, throw it out); What's a quick weeknight dinner with eggs (A frittata with spinach and cheese bakes in about 20 minutes. Sauté the spinach, pour in beaten eggs, and finish under the broiler).

summaries.title: General knowledge questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Give me one surprising fact about elephants (Elephants can communicate with low rumbles that travel through the ground and are felt by other elephants' feet); Explain the Hays Code and when it ended (The Hays Code was a set of self-censorship production rules enforced from 1934. It was effectively replaced in 1968 by the MPAA rating system); How is a blizzard different from a snowstorm (A blizzard requires sustained winds of 35 mph or more with blowing snow reducing visibility to a quarter mile for at least three hours, not just heavy snowfall); Write a two-line dialogue illustrating a straw man fallacy ('I favor some gun regulation.' 'So you want to ban all guns and leave people defenseless?' The second line misrepresents the first); Compare Mesopotamian and Egyptian writing systems (Mesopotamia used cuneiform wedge marks pressed into clay, while Egypt used hieroglyphs painted or carved, later developing hieratic script on papyrus); Why is the sky blue (Air scatters short blue wavelengths more than red ones).

summaries.title: Travel questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Name three documents usually needed for a visa application (A valid passport, proof of funds, and travel itinerary are commonly required for visa applications); Can tweezers go in a carry-on (Yes, tweezers are allowed in carry-on bags. Sharp objects like scissors are fine only if the blades are under 4 inches); Quick one: what ocean surrounds the Maldives (The Indian Ocean surrounds the Maldives); Does drinking water really help with jet lag (Hydration reduces fatigue and headaches that make jet lag feel worse, though it won't reset your body clock by itself); Compare strollers vs. baby carriers for travel (Carriers free your hands and handle stairs and crowds well, while strollers carry gear and let kids nap; many travelers bring a lightweight folding stroller plus a carrier); How can I save money on food while staying in hostels (Cook in the communal kitchen, shop at local markets, and take advantage of free hostel breakfasts).

summaries.title: Writing help
summaries.text: The user asked: How do you say 'thank you' in Japanese (The most common way is 'arigatou' (ありがとう). For a more polite form, use 'arigatou gozaimasu'); Write a haiku about a falling leaf (One leaf lets go, spins— / the whole afternoon turns gold / in a single fall); Give me a hook for a speech about volunteering (Open with a striking statistic or a single vivid story of one person helped. Concrete detail pulls an audience in faster than broad claims); How long should a formal letter be (Aim for one page; keep it to three or four concise paragraphs covering purpose, details and next steps); Do free verse poems need line breaks (Yes; in free verse the line breaks are the main rhythmic tool, so where lines end shapes pace and emphasis); What's a polite way to say excuse me in Turkish ("Affedersiniz" is the polite form; " pardon" is a casual alternative).

summaries.title: أسئلة متفرقة
summaries.text: سأل المستخدم: أبغى أعرف علامات تلف الفرامل (صوت صرير عند الفرملة أو اهتزاز بالدواسة أو مسافة وقوف أطول، كلها علامات تستاهل فحص.)؛ عطني نبذة قصيرة عن الخليفة عمر بن الخطاب. (هو ثاني الخلفاء الراشدين، اشتُهر بالعدل والفتوحات الواسعة وإنشاء الدواوين.)؛ أبي أعرف كمية القهوة لكل كوب (ملعقتين صغار بن مطحون لكل كوب ماي تقريبًا، وزيدها حسب القوة اللي تبيها.)؛ ليش تكتب الهمزة على واو في كلمة مؤمن؟ (لأن الهمزة ساكنة واللي قبلها مضموم، فتكسر على واو حسب قاعدة الهمزة المتوسطة.)؛ عدد لي ثلاث روايات أدبية عربية تستاهل القراءة. (أوصي بثلاثية نجيب محفوظ، وموسم الهجرة إلى الشمال، وذاكرة الجسد لأحلام مستغانمي.)؛ شنو الفرق بين الشاي الأحمر والأسود؟ (نفس الشي تقريباً، اللي نسميه أسود هو الأحمر المخمّر كامل. التسمية تختلف حسب البلد والطريقة.)

summaries.title: Cooking questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Give me three high-protein breakfast ideas (Greek yogurt with nuts, eggs with cheese, and cottage cheese with fruit all deliver roughly 20 grams of protein per serving); How hot is a vindaloo (Traditionally quite hot, built on vinegar, garlic, and chili; restaurant versions range widely but are usually among the spiciest options); Write a one-line rule for storing dried herbs (Keep dried herbs airtight, cool, dark, and dry, and replace them once their aroma fades); Best way to reheat pizza (In a hot pan with a lid for a few minutes); Is it okay to add cream to carbonara (Traditional carbonara does not include cream; the creaminess comes from eggs and cheese); Describe how to spatchcock a chicken for grilling (Cut out the backbone with kitchen shears, flip the bird breast-up, and press down on the breastbone until it lies flat for even, faster cooking).

summaries.title: General knowledge questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Give me a one-line summary of Citizen Kane's plot (A reporter investigates the dying words of newspaper tycoon Charles Foster Kane, piecing together his rise and lonely fall); How did 'nice' change meaning over time (It went from Latin 'nescius' (ignorant) to foolish, then precise, then pleasant, arriving at its current positive sense); Compare stoicism and existentialism briefly (Stoicism says virtue lies in accepting what's outside your control, while existentialism holds that meaning comes from choices you freely make); Describe the role of the oracle at Delphi (The oracle at Delphi was a priestess who delivered prophecies from the god Apollo, influencing political and personal decisions across ancient Greece); Check this: if 5 machines make 5 widgets in 5 minutes, 100 machines make 100 widgets in 100 minutes, right (No, it takes 5 minutes; each machine makes one widget every 5 minutes regardless of how many there are); Explain the trolley problem in one sentence (It asks whether it's right to redirect a runaway trolley to kill one person instead of five, testing whether outcomes or intentions justify harm).

summaries.title: Hobbies and sport
summaries.text: The user asked: Explain how tiebreaks work in tennis (In a tiebreak, players race to 7 points and must win by 2; the first server serves one point, then serves alternate every two points); What causes a mayfly hatch and why do trout key on it (Warm water and stable flows trigger mayfly emergences, and trout feed selectively on emerging nymphs and duns because they're easy, abundant prey); Write a short description of the plot of Halo: Combat Evolved (Master Chief fights the Covenant on a ringworld called Halo, uncovering the Flood and the ring's destructive purpose); How many players are on a basketball court per team (Five players per team are on the court at once, so ten total during play); What's the difference between a novella and a novel (Novellas are typically 20,000–50,000 words, shorter than novels but longer than short stories, often with a single focused arc); How do I stop acrylic paint from drying too fast (Use a retarder medium or a stay-wet palette, and mist the paint lightly with water).

summaries.title: Home and garden questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Check if vinegar is safe to use in the washing machine (Yes, a half-cup of white vinegar in the rinse cycle is safe for most fabrics and helps remove odors and detergent residue); Should I wash jeans inside out (Yes, turning jeans inside out reduces fading and wear on the outer surface during washing); How do I stop clutter from coming back (Give every item a fixed home and do a two-minute reset each evening. Prevention beats repeated purges); How do I handle sentimental items when decluttering (Box them separately and revisit later; limit keepsakes to one container so the pile stays bounded).

summaries.title: Learning and study
summaries.text: The user asked: Compare duolingo and a real tutor for learning a language (Apps build vocabulary and habit cheaply, while a tutor corrects pronunciation and conversation in real time. Many learners combine both); What formulas do I need for kinematics (v = u + at, s = ut + ½at², and v² = u² + 2as cover constant-acceleration problems); Explain the rule of three in speeches (Grouping ideas in threes is easy to remember and sounds rhythmic, which is why slogans and toasts so often use three-part lists); What should a course syllabus include (A syllabus should list learning objectives, weekly topics, required materials, assessment methods, and grading criteria).

summaries.title: Tool runs: tests, disk, files, servers
summaries.text: The user asked: Explain how to monitor CPU usage on a Linux server (Use top or htop for real-time monitoring, or vmstat 1 for periodic snapshots of CPU statistics); list the files in the downloads folder (12 files, the newest is invoice_0917.pdf); What's the difference between RPO and RTO (RPO is the maximum acceptable data loss measured in time; RTO is the maximum acceptable downtime before service is restored); How do I find a file by name on a computer (Use the search bar in the file manager or a command like find or dir /s with the filename).

summaries.title: Travel questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Describe the climate of Beirut in autumn (Beirut in autumn is warm and mild, around 20–28°C, with occasional rain starting late in the season); List the steps to replace a lost passport abroad (Report the loss to local police, contact your embassy, and apply for an emergency travel document or replacement passport); Explain the difference between a collision damage waiver and liability insurance (A collision damage waiver covers damage to the rental vehicle itself, while liability insurance covers harm or injury to others and their property. They address different risks and are often sold separately); Best route from Denver to Moab for scenic driving (Take I-70 west then US-191 south through Grand Junction, or detour via Colorado National Monument for extra scenery); Write a short packing checklist for a week-long road trip (Essentials: driver's license, insurance and rental papers, phone charger and car mount, water and snacks, first-aid kit, jumper cables, tire pressure gauge, map or offline GPS, sunglasses, and layers for changing weather).

summaries.title: أسئلة متفرقة
summaries.text: سأل المستخدم: كيف أتعامل مع مادة أحسها صعبة؟ (قسّمها لأجزاء صغيرة وابدأ بالأساسيات. واسأل عن النقاط الغامضة بدري ولا تتراكم عليك.)؛ كيف أتجنب شد العضلات بعد الرياضة؟ (سوي تمارين إطالة بعد التمرين واشرب ماي كافي وارتح نوم زين.)؛ كيف أطول عمر بطارية الجوال؟ (قلل سطوع الشاشة، وأغلق التطبيقات بالخلفية، وتجنب الشحن الكامل المتكرر.)؛ شنو أفضل طريقة لمراجعة ليلة الامتحان؟ (راجع النقاط الرئيسية والملخصات فقط ولا تحاول تتعلم شي جديد. ونم بدري عشان تكون صاحي.)؛ وش أفضل طريقة لكتابة رسالة نصية قصيرة وواضحة؟ (ابدأ بالهدف مباشرة، واستخدم جمل قصيرة، وابتعد عن الحشو.)؛ وش أفضل وقت لمشاهدة زخات الشهب؟ (أفضل وقت يكون بعد منتصف الليل في مكان مظلم بعيد عن أضواء المدينة.)

summaries.title: Programming questions
General knowledge questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Compare Heathcliff and Rochester as romantic figures (Heathcliff is a destructive, vengeful obsession in 'Wuthering Heights,' while Rochester in 'Jane Eyre' is a moody but ultimately redeemable Byronic hero); Did Nikola Tesla invent radio (Tesla held key early radio patents, but Marconi is generally credited with the first practical radio transmission); How do fish breathe underwater (They draw water over gills, where dissolved oxygen passes into their blood); Name a famous example of brutalist architecture (The Barbican Estate in London is a well-known example of brutalist architecture).

summaries.title: Hobbies and sport
summaries.text: The user asked: Check this: is a basketball worth 3 points if shot from beyond the arc (Yes, a successful field goal taken from behind the three-point line counts for 3 points); What's the difference between a sketch and a study (A sketch is a quick rough drawing capturing basic form, while a study is a focused work exploring one element like light or anatomy in depth); How many players are on a football team on the field (Each team fields 11 players, including the goalkeeper, and a match cannot continue if a team has fewer than seven players); What are the notes of a D major scale (D E F# G A B C# D); How do I read a river to find smallmouth (Look for seams where fast water meets slack, eddies behind boulders, and deep pools below riffles; smallmouth hold in the calmer pockets); How many stops brighter is f/1.4 than f/2.8 (Two stops, since each halving of the f-number admits twice the light).

summaries.title: Travel questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Is travel insurance worth it for a cheap domestic trip (It's often low value for inexpensive domestic trips unless cancellation risk is high. Check whether existing health coverage already applies); Suggest a scenic train route in Switzerland (The Glacier Express from Zermatt to St. Moritz is famous for its alpine scenery and panoramic windows); Write a short note explaining why a jar of peanut butter counts as a liquid at security (Peanut butter is a spreadable gel, and security rules treat gels like liquids, so it must follow the 100 ml container limit. Anything spreadable that can't hold its shape falls under the same rule); Summarize the dress expectations for visiting mosques in the Gulf (Women should cover hair, arms, and legs, and men should wear long trousers; shoes come off at the entrance).

summaries.title: أسئلة متفرقة
summaries.text: سأل المستخدم: عطني أسماء أشهر الأندية في إنجلترا. (من أبرزها مانشستر يونايتد وليفربول وتشيلسي وآرسنال ومانشستر سيتي.)؛ وش أفضل بهارات للمرق الخليجي؟ (الدارسين والهيل واللومي والكزبرة أساس، وضف شوية كركم للون.)؛ اكتب لي خطة مراجعة لأسبوع كامل (خصص أول خمسة أيام لمادة وحدة كل يوم، واليوم السادس مراجعة سريعة، والسابع حل نماذج أسئلة.)؛ هل كلمة ماء مذكر ولا مؤنث؟ (ماء مؤنث في الغالب، تقول ماء عذبة، بس بعض القبائل تذكّرها.)؛ هل يحتاج المشروع الصغير سجل تجاري؟ (حسب النشاط والنظام في بلدك، كثير من الأنشطة تحتاج ترخيص. اسأل الجهة المختصة عندك عشان تتجنب المخالفات.)

summaries.title: Travel questions
summaries.text: The user asked: How does altitude sickness work and how can it be prevented (It results from reduced oxygen at high elevation and causes headache, nausea, and fatigue. Ascend gradually, hydrate, and consider acetazolamide after consulting a clinician); What happens if a rental car breaks down mid-trip (Call the rental company's roadside assistance line; they typically arrange a tow and a replacement vehicle); What's the best way to get from Heathrow to central London (The Heathrow Express is fastest at 15 minutes, but the Piccadilly line is cheaper and direct); What does a typical hostel breakfast include (Often bread, jam, cereal, coffee, and tea; some add eggs or fruit, but it varies widely by region); Compare Glacier and Grand Teton for wildlife viewing (Glacier is known for mountain goats and grizzlies, while Grand Teton offers some of the best moose and bison sightings in the Rockies).

summaries.title: أسئلة متفرقة
summaries.text: سأل المستخدم: فرق بين التاء المربوطة والهاء في الكتابة؟ (التاء المربوطة تنطق هاء بالسكت وتصير تاء بالوصل، والهاء تبقى هاء دايماً.)؛ وش دور بيت الحكمة في العصر العباسي؟ (كان مركز ترجمة وبحث جمع علوم اليونان والفرس والهند وأسهم في نهضة علمية كبيرة.)؛ شلون أتعلم البرمجة؟ (ابدأ ببايثون وسو مشاريع صغيرة كل أسبوع.)؛ عطني مثال على جملة فيها مبتدأ وخبر (مثال بسيط: الطالبُ مجتهدٌ، فالطالب مبتدأ ومجتهد خبر.)؛ ابي اعرف أفضل وقت لتغيير زيت المحرك. (الأفضل كل ٥٠٠٠ إلى ١٠٠٠٠ كيلو حسب نوع الزيت. راجع كتيب السيارة للتأكيد.)

summaries.title: Programming questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Why does the heap grow but the leak tools report nothing (The growth may be fragmentation, allocator arenas, or native memory outside the managed heap. Check OS-level RSS and native allocation tracking separately); How do I squash the last three git commits (Run git rebase -i HEAD~3 and mark two of them as squash); Compare setuid and setgid bits and when they matter (setuid runs a program with the file owner's privileges, setgid with the group's; both matter for controlled privilege escalation); What does list.sort() return (It returns None and sorts the list in place; use sorted(list) for a new sorted list); Is mocking the database a good idea (Prefer a real test database or containers; mocking the DB often hides SQL and transaction bugs); How do I list permissions in a readable form for a file (Run ls -l file, or stat -c '%A %U %G' file for a compact summary).

summaries.title: General knowledge questions
summaries.text: The user asked: What are the key features of Art Deco architecture (Art Deco features sleek geometric forms, bold colors, and lavish ornamentation, often with metallic accents and vertical emphasis); List the periods of Western classical music in order (Medieval, Renaissance, Baroque, Classical, Romantic, and then 20th-century/modern and contemporary eras); Check this: does sodium chloride conduct electricity when solid (No, solid NaCl does not conduct; its ions are locked in the crystal lattice and only move freely when melted or dissolved); How do vaccines work (They train the immune system to recognise a pathogen without the disease); Who directed the 1929 film Man with a Movie Camera (Dziga Vertov directed it, released in 1929); How many ways can you arrange the letters of 'MATH' (24 ways, since all four letters are distinct: 4! = 24).
