summaries.title: Home and garden questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Tips for moving in the rain (Use plastic wrap on box tops, lay floor runners at both doors, keep towels handy, and prioritize moving electronics and upholstered items first); How much clearance should a coffee table have from a sofa (Leave about 18 inches between the coffee table and the sofa for comfortable legroom and easy movement); What grit sandpaper should be used before painting trim (Sand with 120-grit to smooth, then 220-grit lightly before the first coat, and tack-cloth off the dust); How should I store seasonal clothing (Wash and fully dry items, then store in labelled breathable bins. Keep out-of-season clothes out of prime closet space).

summaries.title: Learning and study
summaries.text: The user asked: Does sleep matter for learning (Yes, sleep consolidates memories, especially after studying before bed. Losing sleep to study more usually backfires on retention); How do I stop saying um so much (Replace filler with a silent pause; record a practice run and tap the table each time you hear one to build awareness); What's the difference between a certificate and a certification (A certificate marks course completion, while a certification is a formal credential earned by passing an industry exam); Give me a quick opening line for a talk about recycling (Try: "Every can you've ever thrown away is still out there somewhere.").

summaries.title: Travel questions
summaries.text: The user asked: What's the cheapest way to get from an airport to a city center (Usually a public bus or train; check if the airport runs a shuttle to the nearest transit stop, which often costs a fraction of a taxi); What's the speed limit on German autobahns (There's no general speed limit on many autobahn stretches, but an advisory speed of 130 km/h applies and some sections are restricted); Write a short explanation of how to minimize jet lag (To minimize jet lag, adjust your sleep schedule before traveling, stay hydrated, and expose yourself to natural light at the destination); What's the difference between soba and udon (Soba is thin buckwheat noodles, often served cold with dipping sauce; udon is thick wheat noodles, often in hot broth); Explain layovers like I'm five (A layover is a stop between two flights where you get off one plane and wait to board another. The waiting time is the layover); My colleague is visiting Tokyo, what should she see (Asakusa, the Meiji shrine, Shibuya crossing and a day trip to Nikko).

summaries.title: Writing help
summaries.text: The user asked: Make this email more polite: send me the report now (Could you please send me the report when you have a moment?); Could a society run entirely on barter? Explain briefly (Only in small, close-knit groups; without common measures of value, large-scale trade stalls because wants rarely match); Why do some brands drop their taglines (Brands drop taglines when they reposition, merge, or find the phrase no longer fits the audience. Sometimes the brand itself becomes recognizable enough to stand alone); Write the opening line of a noir mystery set in a greenhouse ("The orchids were the only witnesses, and they weren't talking—not for less than a confession and a bag of fertilizer."); Summarise this and flag anything that looks exaggerated (It summarises well overall, but the claim that the method 'eliminates all bias' is overstated; the study only reduced one measured bias); Write a headline about a city opening a new bike lane network ('City Rolls Out New Bike Lane Network.' Short, active, and clear about the news).

summaries.title: أسئلة متفرقة
summaries.text: سأل المستخدم: هل بيرتفع مستوى البحر بسبب تغير المناخ؟ (نعم، ذوبان الجليد وتمدد الماء الدافئ يرفعان مستوى البحر تدريجياً. المناطق الساحلية المنخفضة أكثر تأثراً.)؛ منو أفضل هداف بتاريخ دوري أبطال أوروبا؟ (كريستيانو رونالدو هو الهداف التاريخي للمسابقة.)؛ هل الحليب مفيد بعد التمرين؟ (إيه، الحليب فيه بروتين وكربوهيدرات ويساعد على الاستشفاء.)؛ الجو صار بارد، شنو أسوي بالنباتات؟ (غلف الأصص أو نقلها لمكان محمي، وقلل السقي لأن النبات يستهلك ماء أقل بالبرد.)؛ اكتب لي دالة تعكس نص بالإنجليزية (تقدر تكتب def reverse(s): return s[::-1] وبتعكس النص بسهولة.)؛ علمني كيف أكتب همزة القطع بشكل صحيح. (همزة القطع تنطق وتكتب دائماً، مثل أكل وإبراهيم، أما همزة الوصل تسقط في النطق.)

summaries.title: Programming questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Bubble sort vs insertion sort — which is faster (Insertion sort is usually faster in practice, especially on nearly sorted data, though both are O(n²) worst case); Give me a command to find all files larger than 100MB under the current directory (Use find . -type f -size +100M to list them); What's a good way to test for SQL injection (Run a scanner like sqlmap in a staging environment and manually probe inputs with quotes and boolean conditions to confirm parameterization); Can you explain lookahead and lookbehind (Lookarounds assert what comes next or before without consuming it, e.g. foo(?=bar) matches foo only if bar follows, and (?<=foo)bar matches bar only after foo); What does axis=0 versus axis=1 mean in pandas (axis=0 operates down rows (per column), and axis=1 operates across columns (per row)); How does two-phase locking work (Two-phase locking (2PL) has a growing phase where locks are acquired and a shrinking phase where locks are released; it ensures serializability but can cause deadlocks).

summaries.title: Cooking questions
summaries.text: The user asked: How do I get a flaky pie crust instead of a crumbly one (Keep the butter in pea-sized pieces and use ice-cold water, then handle the dough as little as possible. Visible butter streaks are what create flaky layers); Write a short checklist for keeping knives sharp (Use a wood or plastic board, never glass; wash and dry by hand; store on a magnetic strip or in a block; hone before each use; sharpen when a tomato starts to squash instead of slice); Give me a recipe for mushroom risotto (Toast arborio rice, add stock ladle by ladle, finish with parmesan and butter); Why did my leftover salad get soggy (Dressing and wet ingredients broke down the leaves. Store dressing separately and keep the salad dry until serving); Suggest three meals that reheat well (Chili, lentil curry, and baked pasta all reheat well and hold their texture); Name the main ingredients in traditional tiramisu (Traditional tiramisu uses ladyfingers, espresso, mascarpone, eggs, sugar, and cocoa powder, with no alcohol in the classic version).

summaries.title: General knowledge questions
summaries.text: The user asked: How many African capitals lie on the coast? Give a rough count (Roughly a dozen African capitals are coastal, including Dakar, Accra, and Dar es Salaam); Define a logical fallacy and name one common type (A fallacy is an error in reasoning that makes an argument invalid; ad hominem, attacking the arguer instead of the argument, is a common one); Summarize the history of the electric guitar in popular music (The electric guitar rose in the 1930s-40s with jazz and country, then became central to rock and roll in the 1950s and to later rock, blues, and pop styles); What was the first feature-length animated film ever released (Disney's Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs (1937) is generally cited as the first feature-length cel-animated film in English); Is a spider an insect (No, spiders are arachnids; they have eight legs and two body segments, unlike insects with six legs and three segments); Rewrite this sentence correctly: The capital of Japan is Kyoto (The capital of Japan is Tokyo; Kyoto was the capital until 1868).

summaries.title: Hobbies and sport
summaries.text: The user asked: Suggest a challenging indie game for someone who likes platformers (Celeste is a great pick; it's a tough platformer with a heartfelt story and precise controls); What's the fastest checkmate (Fool's mate in two moves: 1.f3 e5 2.g4 Qh4#); Compare the King's Indian and the Nimzo-Indian defenses (The King's Indian gives Black a kingside attack after ...d6 and ...e5, while the Nimzo-Indian uses ...Bb4 to pressure c3 and fight for the center early); Give me a tip for sewing stretchy fabric (Use a ballpoint needle, a stretch stitch, and avoid pulling the fabric as you sew to prevent wavy seams).

summaries.title: Home and garden questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Does misting actually raise humidity for tropical plants (Only briefly and slightly; a pebble tray or a humidifier raises humidity around the plant far more reliably); Cold or warm water for dark jeans (Wash dark jeans in cold water and turn them inside out to slow fading and dye loss); What's the difference between a smart plug and a smart switch (A smart plug controls whatever is plugged into it, while a smart switch replaces the wall switch and controls the fixture's wiring directly); Explain phantom loads (Phantom loads are power drawn by devices in standby or off mode. They can account for roughly 5–10% of household electricity use); Check whether Matter devices work across Apple, Google, and Amazon ecosystems (Yes, Matter is designed for cross-platform control, though feature support can vary by each platform's implementation); What's the difference between a mouse and a rat problem (Mice are small, curious, and range widely; rats are wary and follow fixed routes near ground. Rats need bigger bait stations; mice need many small traps).

summaries.title: Learning and study
summaries.text: The user asked: List three note-taking apps for students (Notion, Evernote, and OneNote are popular choices. They support multimedia notes, tagging, and search); What's the best way to practice alone (Rehearse aloud standing up, record yourself once, and review for pacing and filler. Doing it aloud is essential—silent rehearsal doesn't build delivery); Explain how to verify an online certificate's authenticity (Use the issuer's verification page or scan the credential's QR code to confirm the holder and issue date); Check this sentence: 'The mitochondria is the powerhouse of the cell.' (It's grammatically fine in casual use, but the standard biology phrasing is 'the mitochondria are the powerhouse of the cell').

summaries.title: Devices and software
summaries.text: The user asked: Compare Zoom, Teams, and Google Meet briefly (Zoom leads on breakout rooms and webinar tools, Teams integrates with Microsoft 365, and Meet is simplest and free with a Google account); Summarize the main risks of deploying chatbots in customer support (Key risks are wrong answers, privacy leaks, biased or off-brand tone, and frustrating loops when the bot can't escalate. Human handoff and monitoring mitigate most of these); What firmware update steps should be followed for a router (Back up settings, download firmware only from the manufacturer, and apply it over a wired connection if possible. Don't power off during the update, then verify settings and reboot); Compare flatbed and sheet-fed scanners (Flatbed scanners handle books and fragile items but are slower, while sheet-fed scanners rapidly process loose pages but can't scan bound documents).

summaries.title: Writing help
summaries.text: The user asked: What's the difference between affect and effect (Affect is usually a verb meaning to influence; effect is usually a noun meaning a result. "The rain affected the game" vs. "the effect was a delay."); Fix the grammar in this sentence: Me and him went to the store (Change the subject to "He and I went to the store." Subject pronouns are used for the doer of the action); Rewrite 'You're wrong' politely ('I see it a bit differently — could we walk through the details together?' keeps disagreement without blame); Check the grammar: She don't like coffee (It should be 'She doesn't like coffee' because 'doesn't' is the correct contraction for third-person singular); Explain enjambment in a sentence (Enjambment is when a sentence runs past the line break instead of pausing at it); Compare slogans for car brands versus food brands (Car slogans lean on emotion and identity, while food slogans usually emphasize taste, comfort, or convenience).

summaries.title: أسئلة متفرقة
summaries.text: سأل المستخدم: شنو الفرق بين HTTP و HTTPS؟ (HTTPS هو HTTP مع تشفير SSL/TLS، يعني البيانات تكون محمية أثناء النقل.)؛ ليش الجسم يتعب بسرعة أثناء الجري؟ (غالباً بسبب التنفس غير المنتظم أو نقص الماء أو البدء بسرعة عالية من غير تسخين.)؛ صحح لي هالجملة: إن شاء الله سوف نلتقي غداً (أفضل صياغة: إن شاء الله نلتقي غداً، لأن إن شاء الله ما تحتاج سوف.)؛ وش أفضل طريقة لتتبع المصاريف اليومية؟ (التطبيقات البسيطة أو دفتر صغير يكفون، المهم تسجل بانتظام وتشوف النمط كل أسبوع.)؛ اذكر لي علمين من علماء المسلمين في الطب. (ابن سينا والرازي، ولهما إسهامات كبيرة في الطب انتقلت لأوروبا.)؛ أبغى وصفة مطبق زبيدي (حط الرز والزبيدي والبهار بالعجين، واقليه على حرارة وسط لين يتحمر من الجهتين.)

summaries.title: Programming questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Why did my program hang with a deadlock error (A deadlock occurs when all goroutines are blocked and none can proceed, typically from an unbuffered send with no receiver. Check that every send has a matching receive or sufficient buffer); Best way to share loading state across many components (Lift it to a shared context or state library like Zustand, or use React Query which exposes isLoading per query. Avoid duplicating boolean state in each child); Remove duplicates from a list while keeping order (Use dict.fromkeys(my_list) to preserve order and remove duplicates, then convert back to a list); Explain async and await in JavaScript (async marks a function that returns a promise; await pauses until the promise settles); What's the difference between a hard link and a symbolic link (A hard link points directly to the same inode; a symlink is a separate file holding a path to the target); Are prepared statements enough to stop SQL injection (Yes for data values, but identifiers like table or column names can't be parameterized, so whitelist those against a fixed list).

summaries.title: Cooking questions
summaries.text: The user asked: How long should croissants chill between folds (About 30 minutes in the fridge per fold, enough to firm the butter without letting the dough dry out. Keep the dough covered to prevent a skin); What's the best way to store leftover stew (Cool it quickly, refrigerate in shallow airtight containers within two hours, and use it within three to four days); What's a quick vegetarian dinner idea (Chickpea curry with spinach over rice, ready in twenty minutes); What can I use instead of cheese on a vegan pizza (Cashew mozzarella or a sprinkle of nutritional yeast mixed with garlic powder works well); Quick breakfast for a crowd (A baked egg casserole or a big batch of sheet-pan breakfast potatoes with sausage feeds many people with little hands-on work); What's the difference between ramen and udon (Ramen uses thin, springy wheat noodles usually served in a rich broth; udon are thick, chewy wheat noodles often served in a lighter broth or stir-fried).

summaries.title: General knowledge questions
summaries.text: The user asked: What's the difference between a valid and a sound argument (A valid argument's conclusion follows necessarily from its premises; a sound argument is valid and also has all true premises); What's the capital of Canada and which province is it in (Ottawa is the capital, located in Ontario); What was the significance of the Magna Carta (Sealed in 1215, it established that the king was subject to law and granted certain rights to nobles, becoming a symbol for later constitutional limits on power); How long did the Hundred Years' War last (It lasted 116 years, from 1337 to 1453, with long stretches of truce and intermittent fighting between England and France); Who painted the Girl with a Pearl Earring (Johannes Vermeer, around 1665); Compare the Arctic and Southern Oceans briefly (The Arctic is largely enclosed by land and capped by sea ice, while the Southern Ocean encircles Antarctica and connects the major basins).

summaries.title: Health and fitness questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Explain why flu season peaks in winter (Colder air and indoor crowding help influenza spread, and drier air may weaken nasal defenses, so transmission peaks in winter months); Compare free weights and resistance machines (Free weights train balance and stabilizer muscles more, while machines offer guided movement and are easier for isolation); Write a one-sentence summary of what fiber does for digestion (Fiber adds bulk, feeds gut bacteria, and helps regulate bowel movements and blood sugar); How long can a person safely stay in a sauna (Typically 10 to 15 minutes per session, with hydration before and after and a break if dizziness occurs); Explain the 20-20-20 rule briefly (Every 20 minutes, look at something 20 feet away for 20 seconds to relax the eye muscles during screen work); Do children and older adults need more water in hot weather (Yes, both groups regulate fluids less effectively, so they need regular prompting to drink, even without thirst).

summaries.title: Money questions
summaries.text: The user asked: What's the 50/30/20 budget rule (It allocates 50% of after-tax income to needs, 30% to wants, and 20% to savings and debt repayment); What's the difference between cash basis and accrual accounting (Cash basis records revenue and expenses when money moves; accrual records them when earned or incurred, regardless of payment timing); Can you explain what working capital means (It's current assets minus current liabilities, showing short-term liquidity available to run operations); What does 'real interest rate' mean in an inflation context (It's the nominal interest rate minus the inflation rate, showing the actual change in purchasing power); Is the 70/20/10 rule any good (It allocates 70% to living costs, 20% to savings, and 10% to debt or giving; it suits people with modest fixed costs but leaves little room for irregular expenses).

summaries.title: Devices and software
summaries.text: The user asked: Give me a quick checklist before hosting an important video call (Test camera, mic and screen share, close distracting tabs, check lighting, and confirm the meeting link and passcode. Have a backup phone dial-in in case audio fails); What's the difference between a webinar and a video meeting (Meetings let everyone interact and share video freely, while webinars give hosts control and usually make attendees view-only. Webinars suit large presentations; meetings suit collaboration); Check this formula for me: =SUM(A1:A10)/COUNT(A1:A10) (That's valid and computes the average of the numeric cells; =AVERAGE(A1:A10) does the same more simply); Check this sentence: 'Please join the call at 10 AM sharp.' (It's correct and clear. You could add a time zone, e.g., '10 AM ET sharp.'); Quick: what's credential stuffing (Attackers replay username-password pairs leaked from one breach against other sites, exploiting password reuse — unique passwords per site defeat it); Briefly explain what thermal throttling is (It's when a laptop slows its processor to prevent overheating).

summaries.title: Tool runs: tests, disk, files, servers
summaries.text: The user asked: Is there a limit on recurring reminders (Most apps cap recurrence by an end date or occurrence count, but otherwise allow indefinite repetition within the calendar system's supported range); What's the difference between virtual memory and physical RAM (Physical RAM is the actual memory chips installed; virtual memory is the per-process address space the OS maps onto RAM and disk. Swapping lets virtual pages live on disk when RAM is full); Is 90% memory usage bad (Not necessarily; modern systems cache aggressively and can run fine near 90%. It's a problem if you see heavy swapping or apps becoming unresponsive); check the disk space (C: has 118 GB free of 476 GB).

summaries.title: Travel questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Can you explain what a one-way rental fee is (It's a surcharge for returning a car to a different location than pickup, covering repositioning costs. Fees vary widely, so compare one-way quotes across companies before booking); Is Copenhagen expensive for a weekend (Yes, Copenhagen is pricey, but budget tips include eating street food and using the 24-hour transit pass); How much should I expect a child's airfare to cost (Lap infants usually cost 10-20% of the adult fare or a flat fee, while children in their own seat pay the standard fare plus taxes); Can luggage be checked in on Indian Railways (Yes, Indian Railways offers a luggage booking service at most major stations, letting passengers send heavier bags in the guards' van); Compare hostels and guesthouses for budget travel (Hostels are cheaper and more social; guesthouses offer more privacy and often include breakfast); Compare aisle vs window seats for long-haul flights (Aisle seats let you stand and stretch without climbing over anyone; window seats give a headrest wall and uninterrupted sleep but trap you in).

summaries.title: Writing help
summaries.text: The user asked: Is 'Dear Mr. Smith' acceptable in British English (Yes, though British style often omits the full stop: "Dear Mr Smith" is standard in UK usage); Rewrite this title shorter: 'A Comprehensive Guide to Understanding Modern Web Development Frameworks' (Try 'A Guide to Modern Web Frameworks.' It keeps the topic and cuts the filler); Correct this: He is taller then me (Change 'then' to 'than' and 'me' to 'I' for formal correctness: 'He is taller than I.' However, 'than me' is common in informal speech); TL;DR of this piece (Coffee drinking was linked to slightly lower heart risk, but the effect was small and the study was observational); Do formal letters still use 'Esq.' after a name (In UK convention "Esq." can follow a man's name instead of "Mr," but it is now largely archaic and best avoided).

summaries.title: أسئلة متفرقة
summaries.text: سأل المستخدم: فرق لي بين السيرفر والكلاينت (السيرفر يقدم الخدمة ويخزن البيانات، والكلاينت هو الجهاز أو البرنامج اللي يطلبها.)؛ وش أسوي عشان أسرع إنبات البذور؟ (انقع البذور قبل الزراعة وحطها في مكان دافي ورطب، وغطها بشفاف لين تطلع.)؛ عطني توقعات الأسبوع كامل (الأيام الأولى حارة وصافية، وآخر الأسبوع ممكن تجي غيوم متفرقة.)؛ شلون أسوي كيكة بالشوكولاتة؟ (اخلط الطحين والكاكاو والبيض والسكر واخبزها على ١٨٠ درجة.)؛ أبي طريقة سهلة أسمّد بها الزرع بدون مواد كيماوية. (استخدم مخلفات القهوة وقشور البيض المطحونة أو كومبوست طبيعي، وخلطها بالتربة كل شهر تقريباً.)؛ سمّ لي ثلاث حيوانات تعيش في القطب الشمالي. (الدب القطبي، الفقمة، والثعلب القطبي.)

summaries.title: Programming questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Give an example of Promise.all (`Promise.all([Promise.resolve(1), Promise.resolve(2)]).then(console.log)` logs `[1, 2]`); How do I make a script executable (Run chmod +x script.sh to add execute permission for all users); Give a one-line example of returning an owned String from a function (`fn greet() -> String { String::from("hi") }` — ownership transfers to the caller); When should I use HAVING versus WHERE (WHERE filters rows before grouping; HAVING filters groups after aggregation, so use HAVING with aggregate conditions); How can I center a div with CSS (Use display:flex with justify-content:center and align-items:center on the parent); What causes a memory leak in a long-running Python service (Unreleased references—global caches, unclosed files, or cycles held by objects with __del__—keep objects alive. Use tracemalloc and gc.get_objects to find the growing allocation site).

summaries.title: Health and fitness questions
summaries.text: The user asked: List three foods with high water content (Watermelon, cucumber, and oranges are all over 80% water); Compare running and cycling for building aerobic fitness (Both build aerobic fitness, but running loads your bones and joints more while cycling lets you train longer with less impact. Combining them gives high aerobic volume with lower injury risk); Write a short script for a guided breathing session to calm anxiety (Here's a script: 'Close your eyes. Breathe in slowly through your nose for 4 counts, hold for 2, exhale through your mouth for 6. Repeat 10 times.'); Explain why screen position matters for posture (The top of the screen should be at or slightly below eye level so the neck stays neutral instead of flexing forward, which reduces strain).

summaries.title: أسئلة متفرقة
summaries.text: سأل المستخدم: هل فيه موجة حر قادمة هالأسبوع؟ (نعم، توقعات تشير لارتفاع تدريجي بالحرارة وسط الأسبوع. يفضل تجنب الشمس وقت الظهيرة.)؛ أبي مثال على المفعول به في جملة بسيطة. (مثال بسيط: أكل الولد التفاحة، فالتفاحة مفعول به منصوب.)؛ ليش الجو رطب هالفترة؟ (الرطوبة ترتفع بسبب الرياح الشرقية القادمة من الخليج.)؛ شنو الفرق بين المدرسة الشافعية والحنفية؟ (الفرق الأساسي في أصول الاستدلال؛ الحنفية يعتمدون القياس أكثر، والشافعية يشددون في الحديث والأصول.)؛ ما أفضل طريقة للتسويق لمشروع جديد بميزانية قليلة؟ (ركز على السوشيال ميديا والمحتوى المجاني وخدمة العملاء الممتازة، وابدأ بمنطقة صغيرة وخل العملاء يوصون فيك.)؛ ليش لازم نشرب ماي أكثر في الجو الحار؟ (لأن الجسم يفقد سوائل كثيرة بالتعرق، فتعويض الماء يمنع الجفاف والإجهاد.)

summaries.title: Programming questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Command to abort a rebase that's going badly (Run git rebase --abort to return the branch to its state before the rebase started); Can you check if this array is a valid min-heap: [1, 3, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7] (Yes, it's a valid min-heap: each parent (1, 3, 2) is smaller than its children (3,2; 4,5; 6,7 respectively)); What does numpy broadcasting do when shapes differ (It aligns dimensions from the right, stretching size-1 dims to match. If a pair of dims differs and neither is 1, it raises an error); How do I create a promise that resolves after 1 second (Use `new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 1000))`); Write a generic function that returns the first element of an array (`function first<T>(arr: T[]): T | undefined { return arr[0]; }` works and returns `undefined` for empty arrays); Check this approach: run a load test for an hour, snapshot heap every ten minutes, and diff the last against the first (That works well; consistent growth in retained size across snapshots confirms a leak, and the diff isolates the object types responsible).

summaries.title: Cooking questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Give me a quick high-protein vegan lunch idea (Try a chickpea salad sandwich with mashed chickpeas, vegan mayo, and celery in whole-grain bread); Give me a quick list of herbs for a basic herb garden (Basil, parsley, mint, rosemary, thyme, oregano, chives, and sage cover most cooking needs. Rosemary, thyme, and sage are the hardiest perennials); Explain why leftovers should cool before going in the fridge (Cooling first limits condensation and keeps the fridge from warming up, though food should not sit out more than 2 hours total); Give a quick recipe outline for fattoush (Toss mixed greens, tomatoes, cucumber, and radish with toasted pita pieces and a sumac-lemon dressing); Give me a safe way to carry a knife across a kitchen (Hold it by the handle with the blade pointing down and slightly away from the body, and announce your path so others step aside); Is it safe to refreeze meat that thawed in the fridge (Yes, if it was thawed in the refrigerator and kept cold, it can be safely refrozen, though quality may suffer).

summaries.title: General knowledge questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Check this: heavier objects always fall faster than light ones (That's false in a vacuum; without air resistance, all objects accelerate at the same rate regardless of mass); Compare the sizes of Mars and Earth (Mars has about half Earth's diameter and roughly 15% of its volume, with a surface gravity around 38% of Earth's); Explain the difference between necessary and contingent truths with an example (A necessary truth couldn't be false, like 'all bachelors are unmarried'; a contingent truth could have been otherwise, like 'it is raining.'); Did the Vikings reach North America (Yes, Norse explorers established a short-lived settlement at L'Anse aux Meadows in Newfoundland around 1000 CE); Compare the capitals of Canada and the United States in size (Ottawa has roughly one million people, while Washington, D.C. has about 700,000, so Ottawa is larger); What's the story behind the invention of penicillin (Alexander Fleming noticed in 1928 that mold on a petri dish killed bacteria; later Howard Florey and Ernst Chain turned it into a usable drug).

summaries.title: Health and fitness questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Explain the 20-20-20 rule (Every 20 minutes, take a 20-second break to look at something 20 feet away. This relaxes eye muscles and reduces fatigue); Suggest a breathing exercise for sleep (Try the 4-7-8 technique before bed: inhale 4, hold 7, exhale 8, repeat four times); Quick tip for climbing hills on a bike (Shift early into an easier gear and keep a steady cadence instead of grinding. Sit back slightly for traction and pace yourself); How does room temperature affect sleep (A cool room of roughly 15 to 19°C helps the body drop its core temperature, which supports sleep onset and deeper sleep); What angle should knees be at when seated (Around 90 to 100 degrees, with feet flat and thighs roughly parallel to the floor); How long should I practice breathing exercises daily to manage stress (Aim for 5–10 minutes daily; consistency is more important than duration for stress management).

summaries.title: Hobbies and sport
summaries.text: The user asked: How do I cast on for knitting (Use the long-tail cast-on: make a slip knot, then loop the yarn around your thumb and needle to create stitches); Summarize the plot of 'Sapiens' in two sentences (It traces how Homo sapiens came to dominate Earth through cognitive, agricultural, and scientific revolutions. Harari argues shared myths like money and nations enabled large-scale cooperation); Explain the difference between a tennis tiebreak and a regular game (A regular game is won by the first player to reach four points with a two-point lead, while a tiebreak is usually played to seven points with a two-point margin and decides a set); Recommend a book that explains quantum physics for laypeople ('Quantum: A Guide for the Perplexed' by Jim Al-Khalili offers an accessible introduction without heavy math); What does VAR stand for and what does it review (VAR stands for Video Assistant Referee, and it reviews goals, penalty decisions, direct red cards, and cases of mistaken identity); Describe the plot of 'The Road' in two sentences (A father and son journey through a post-apocalyptic America, struggling to survive. The novel focuses on their bond and the father's determination to protect the boy).

summaries.title: Home and garden questions
summaries.text: The user asked: How do I get a grease stain out of a cotton shirt (Blot the stain with a paper towel, then work in a small amount of dish soap and wash in the hottest water the fabric allows); How high should a pendant hang over a kitchen island (Hang it about 30 to 36 inches above the countertop, higher if the ceiling is very tall); Compare velvet and linen upholstery for durability (Velvet is plush but can crush and show marks, while linen is breathable and durable but wrinkles easily); Explain how a smart lock connects to a phone (Most smart locks use Bluetooth for nearby unlocking and Wi-Fi or a bridge for remote access, with encrypted keys stored in the app); Draft a checklist for securing a home automation setup (Use unique passwords, enable two-factor authentication, segment IoT devices on a separate network, keep firmware updated, and disable unused remote access); What's a good way to label storage boxes (Use broad categories on the visible side, plus a short contents list. Keep labels consistent and legible from the front).

summaries.title: Learning and study
summaries.text: The user asked: Is the Arabic alphabet read right to left (Yes, Arabic script runs right to left, and letters change shape depending on their position in the word); How long do typical online certificate programs take (Most range from a few weeks for single courses to six to twelve months for professional certificate programs, depending on weekly study hours); Why does multitasking feel productive but fail (Task-switching feels busy but costs time as attention reloads, often 20-40% slower overall. Single-tasking with short breaks produces more finished work); What is Parkinson's Law (Parkinson's Law states that work expands to fill the time available for its completion, so setting shorter deadlines can boost efficiency); How do I review notes so they actually stick (Space short reviews at increasing intervals and convert notes into recall questions rather than rereading them passively); What's the difference between notes and annotations (Notes are separate records of information, while annotations are comments added directly to a text or document. Annotations often supplement notes).

summaries.title: Money questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Write a one-line definition of currency depreciation (Currency depreciation is a fall in a currency's value relative to other currencies under a floating exchange rate); Is a bookkeeper the same as an accountant (No—bookkeepers record daily transactions, while accountants interpret the books and handle reporting, taxes, and advisory work); What's the 50/30/20 rule (It splits after-tax income into 50% needs, 30% wants, and 20% savings or debt payoff); Break down the difference between fixed and variable expenses (Fixed expenses stay constant each period, like rent; variable expenses fluctuate with usage, like groceries and utilities); Convert 250 Canadian dollars into Japanese yen (At roughly 110 yen per Canadian dollar, that's about 27,500 yen); Give me a short definition of taxable income (Taxable income is the portion of income subject to tax after allowed deductions and exemptions are subtracted from gross income).

summaries.title: Devices and software
summaries.text: The user asked: Explain VLOOKUP vs INDEX-MATCH (VLOOKUP searches only rightward from the key column, while INDEX-MATCH can look in any direction and is more flexible); How do I set up a filter to move emails from a specific sender to a folder (In most email clients, go to settings, create a new filter rule with the sender's address as the condition and the target folder as the action); Does router placement really matter, and where should it go (Yes—central, elevated, and unobstructed placement improves coverage. Keep it away from metal, thick walls, and appliances like microwaves, and avoid cabinets or floors); How can I check if an email is phishing (Look for mismatched sender addresses, urgent language, suspicious links, and unexpected attachments; hover over links to verify the URL); How do I share my screen on a Zoom call (Click the green Share Screen button in the meeting toolbar and pick the window you want to show. On mobile, tap Share and choose Screen); Explain DKIM and DMARC simply (DKIM adds a cryptographic signature so receivers can verify a message wasn't altered. DMARC tells receivers what to do with mail that fails SPF or DKIM and sends reports back to the domain owner).

summaries.title: Tool runs: tests, disk, files, servers
summaries.text: The user asked: Can git log show only merge commits (Yes, `git log --merges` filters to commits with more than one parent. Pair it with `--oneline` for brevity); Is it safe to delete temp files (Generally yes, temporary files can be removed safely; programs recreate them as needed); Give me a quick command to see my default gateway (Run `ip route | grep default` on Linux. It prints the gateway IP next to the word `default`); How do I filter git log by author (Use git log --author="name", which matches the author field by substring or regex. Combine with --oneline and -n to keep it brief); Why do some folder names end in a slash (The trailing slash marks the path as a directory rather than a file in many systems); What does a red build mean (A red build means the CI pipeline failed, usually because a test, lint check, or build step returned an error).

summaries.title: Travel questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Why does snow squeak under boots (Squeaking occurs when ice crystals rub together at very cold temperatures, creating friction and tiny vibrations that produce sound); Is Bondi Beach in Sydney (Yes, Bondi Beach is a suburb and beach in eastern Sydney, Australia); Give me three ways to cut food costs while traveling (Shop at local markets, cook in hostel kitchens, and eat the main meal at lunch when restaurants charge less); List the pros and cons of staying in a hostel for a week (Pros: low cost, kitchen access, and easy socializing; cons: less privacy, noise, and shared bathrooms that can get busy); Compare the Maldives and Seychelles for beach scenery (The Maldives offers low coral atolls with shallow turquoise lagoons, while the Seychelles has granite boulders and steeper green hills behind its beaches); Check whether the Dead Sea is swimmable for a non-swimmer (Yes, its high salinity makes floating easy, but avoid getting water in your eyes and never put your head under).

summaries.title: Writing help
summaries.text: The user asked: Turn 'fix this' into something gentler ('Could you take a look at this and let me know what you think?' invites action without an order); Is this line iambic: 'The cat sat on the mat' (Not quite—it reads as four stresses with uneven feet, closer to trochaic than iambic); What's the difference between a cover letter and a letter of enquiry (A cover letter accompanies another document and introduces it, whereas a letter of enquiry simply requests information); Translate 'I love you' into Mandarin Chinese ('I love you' in Mandarin is 'wǒ ài nǐ' (我爱你)); Can you explain when to use a semicolon (Use a semicolon to connect two independent clauses that are closely related, like 'I have a big test tomorrow; I can't go out tonight.'); What font and size are best for a CV (Use a clean, professional font like Arial or Calibri at 10 to 12 points for body text, with headings slightly larger).

summaries.title: أسئلة متفرقة
summaries.text: سأل المستخدم: من أول من وضع علم العروض؟ (الخليل بن أحمد الفراهيدي هو أول من وضع علم العروض.)؛ وش أفضل طريقة أسوق فيها لبضاعتي؟ (ركز على منصات التواصل وقرب من عملائك، والصور الواضحة تفرق كثير. جرب إعلان بسيط وشوف وش يجيب نتائج وكرر الناجح.)؛ شكثر يجي وقت بين الأذان والإقامة في المساجد؟ (عادة من عشر لعشرين دقيقة حسب المسجد، يكفي الناس يصلون السنة.)؛ أبي أعرف إذا مكان الحوض مناسب للزرع، وش أتحقق منه؟ (شوف كم ساعة شمس يوصله باليوم وناحية هبوب الريح وقرب مصدر الموية، هذي أهم الأشياء.)؛ كم عدد لاعبي الفريق الواحد داخل الملعب؟ (أحد عشر لاعب لكل فريق، منهم حارس واحد.)؛ كيف تتكون الثقوب السوداء؟ (تتكون غالباً لما ينهار نجم ضخم على نفسه بعد ما يخلص وقوده، فيصير جاذبيته قوية لدرجة ما يفلت منها شي.)

summaries.title: Programming questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Write a custom hook that debounces a value (Create useDebounce(value, delay) that stores value in state and sets a timeout in useEffect to update it after delay, clearing the timeout on cleanup); How do I fix 'cannot borrow as mutable because it is also borrowed as immutable' (End the immutable borrow's use before the mutable one, often by scoping it or cloning the needed data); Compare lookahead and lookbehind with examples (Lookahead (?=...) checks what follows, lookbehind (?<=...) checks what precedes; neither consumes characters); Write a query to find the second highest salary (Use a subquery: SELECT MAX(salary) FROM employees WHERE salary < (SELECT MAX(salary) FROM employees);); How do I center a div both horizontally and vertically with flexbox (Set the parent to display: flex, justify-content: center, and align-items: center); Short: what's a stack overflow vs a memory leak (A stack overflow is unbounded recursion exhausting the fixed call stack. A leak is heap memory retained after it's no longer needed).

summaries.title: Cooking questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Write a short shopping list for three fast dinners (Eggs, canned tomatoes, pasta, spinach, canned chickpeas, tortillas, cheese, and onions cover three quick meals); Quick one: can honey go bad (Honey rarely spoils, but it can crystallize; warm the jar in water to make it smooth again); What pasta shape goes best with ragù (Tagliatelle or pappardelle are ideal because their wide, porous surfaces hold the meat sauce); Can reheated pasta be kept moist (Yes, sprinkle a little water over it and cover before reheating, or toss with sauce or oil); What lentils work best in a vegan Bolognese (Brown or green lentils hold their shape and give a meaty texture; red lentils break down and thicken the sauce instead); Write a two-line rhyme about a chocolate chip cookie (Golden edges, soft within, / a scatter of chips is where joy begins).

summaries.title: General knowledge questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Describe Starry Night briefly (Van Gogh's Starry Night shows a swirling night sky over a small village with a cypress tree in the foreground, painted in 1889. The thick, curling brushstrokes give the sky a restless, almost moving quality); Write a one-line logline for a heist film set in 1920s Paris (A disgraced couturier assembles a crew of cabaret performers to steal a jeweled gown before the season's biggest show); Check this fact: was Metropolis released in 1927 (Yes, Fritz Lang's Metropolis premiered in Berlin in January 1927); What does the suffix '-phobia' mean and where's it from (It means fear of, from Greek 'phobos' (fear), as in 'claustrophobia' or 'xenophobia'); Why does a straw work when you suck on it (Sucking lowers the pressure in the straw, and the higher atmospheric pressure on the drink's surface pushes the liquid up); When did synchronized sound first appear in a feature film (The Jazz Singer in 1927 is widely credited as the first feature with synchronized dialogue sequences).

summaries.title: Health and fitness questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Compare water and sports drinks for rehydration (Water rehydrates well for most activity; sports drinks help mainly during prolonged sweating because they replace sodium and glucose); Why is vitamin B12 important for vegetarians to watch (B12 occurs mainly in animal foods, so vegetarians and vegans often need fortified foods or supplements); Why does flu make the whole body ache (Influenza triggers a strong immune response releasing cytokines, which cause widespread muscle aches and fatigue); Give me three good sources of omega-3 fatty acids (Salmon, walnuts, and flaxseed are all reliable omega-3 sources); Write a short bedtime wind-down routine (Dim the lights an hour before bed, stop screens, do ten minutes of light stretching or reading, then keep the room cool and dark at a consistent bedtime).

summaries.title: Hobbies and sport
summaries.text: The user asked: How many quarters are in an NBA game (An NBA game has four quarters, each 12 minutes long); Any tips to find a podcast's best episodes (Sort by most-played or check the show's own 'start here' page, and read recent reviews for standout episode mentions); How long is a tennis court (A tennis court is 78 feet (23.77 m) long for singles and doubles play); What's the safest solvent for thinning oil paint indoors (Odorless mineral spirits are the usual choice, though ventilation and a closed container are still needed); Explain magical realism in two sentences (Magical realism blends supernatural events into otherwise realistic settings, presented as ordinary. It's associated with Latin American writers like García Márquez and Isabel Allende); What does the aperture number on a lens actually mean (It's the ratio of focal length to entrance pupil diameter, so f/2 lets in four times the light of f/4).

summaries.title: Home and garden questions
summaries.text: The user asked: What should I do with items I might need someday (Box them with a date and revisit in six months. If you haven't opened the box, donate it unopened); Best way to get coffee stains out of a mug (Scrub the inside with a paste of baking soda and water, then rinse thoroughly); How do I reset a tripped GFCI outlet (Press the reset button firmly; if it won't hold, the circuit may have a ground fault or the device is faulty); Can a doorbell camera work without a subscription (Many models support local storage on an SD card or NVR and still offer live view and basic alerts without a cloud plan); Why does my smart bulb flicker when dimmed (Flicker usually comes from incompatible dimmer switches, low-quality LED drivers, or a bulb not rated for the dimming range being used); Compare LED bulbs and compact fluorescent bulbs for a kitchen (LEDs use about 25–30% less energy than CFLs, last longer, and contain no mercury. CFLs are cheaper upfront but cost more over time).

summaries.title: Learning and study
summaries.text: The user asked: Explain the Feynman technique briefly (Explain a concept in plain language as if teaching a beginner, spot the gaps, then revisit the source to fill them); List five reputable platforms offering free online courses with certificates (Coursera, edX, Khan Academy, OpenLearn (Open University), and Google's Skillshop all offer free courses, though paid certificates may be optional on some); Write three example sentences using the French passé composé (J'ai mangé une pomme. Elle est arrivée hier. Nous avons fini le travail); What abbreviations do note-takers commonly use (Common ones include w/ for with, b/c for because, → for leads to, ∴ for therefore, and + or & for and); How long should a reading lesson be for a 6-year-old (Keep lessons to about 15 to 20 minutes, since attention spans at that age are short); Should I look at the audience or the camera on a video call (Look at the camera when making key points and at the screen for reactions. The camera is the audience's eye contact).

summaries.title: Money questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Describe the tradeoff between risk and return for beginners (Higher expected returns usually require accepting more risk, so safer assets like bonds tend to earn less over time than stock index funds); What's the difference between hard and soft credit inquiries (Hard inquiries occur when lenders check credit for a loan and can lower scores slightly; soft inquiries don't affect scores); Describe what tax evasion means (Tax evasion is the illegal non-payment or underpayment of taxes, often through concealment or fraud); How can someone dispute an error on a credit report (File a dispute with the credit bureau and the creditor, providing evidence; the bureau must investigate within 30 days); Why did the Swiss franc strengthen so much in 2015 (Switzerland's central bank abandoned its euro peg in January 2015, and the franc surged nearly 30 percent against the euro within minutes); List three common types of taxes (Income tax, sales tax, and property tax are three common types. Others include payroll, excise, and estate taxes).

summaries.title: Devices and software
summaries.text: The user asked: Compare Gmail, Outlook, and Thunderbird briefly (Gmail and Outlook are web-first services tied to their vendors, while Thunderbird is a free desktop client that works with many providers. Gmail and Outlook handle filtering automatically; Thunderbird relies on built-in and add-on tools); Check this password: Tr0ub4dor&3 (It's a known-style pattern and relatively weak; a longer passphrase of four or five random words would be stronger and easier to remember); What's the best way to organize email folders (Create folders by project, sender, or topic, and use filters to automatically sort incoming mail); Write a memorable passphrase example for a password manager (Something like "copper-Lantern-47-puzzle" works: random words joined by a symbol and number make it long yet easy to recall); Write a short definition of cold storage in cloud context (Cold storage is a low-cost cloud tier for infrequently accessed data, with slower retrieval times. It is used for backups and archives); Does changing a password regularly help (Modern guidance says no for strong unique passwords; forced rotation encourages weak variations. Change it when there's a breach or suspicion, not on a schedule).

summaries.title: Tool runs: tests, disk, files, servers
summaries.text: The user asked: Check this path for mistakes: C:/Users/docs/final?.txt (The question mark is invalid in Windows filenames, so that path would fail; remove or replace it); What does a failing test suite typically report first (It usually reports the first test failure with its name, the assertion error, and a stack trace pointing to the failing line); How do I see which branch I'm on and whether it's ahead (git status prints the current branch and any ahead/behind counts versus its upstream. git branch -vv lists all local branches with tracking info); Check if DNS is resolving correctly for example.com (Run 'dig example.com' or 'nslookup example.com' to verify DNS resolution and see the returned IP); What does 'Your branch is ahead of origin/main by 2 commits' mean (It means the local branch has two commits not yet on the remote tracking branch. `git push` would publish them); What does ping actually measure (Ping measures round-trip time for an ICMP echo request to reach a host and return. It reflects latency and packet loss, not bandwidth).

summaries.title: Travel questions
summaries.text: The user asked: What's the best time of year to visit Prague (Late spring and early autumn offer mild weather and fewer crowds than midsummer); What temperature is too cold to ski (Skiing becomes risky below about -20°C (-4°F) due to frostbite, and many resorts close lifts in extreme cold or high wind chill); How did the Louvre start out (As a medieval fortress built by Philip II around 1190; parts of the original keep are still visible in the basement); Name a good historic site near Edinburgh (Rosslyn Chapel, about 30 minutes south, famed for its carved stonework and Da Vinci Code fame); Can I travel with an expired passport (No, an expired passport is not valid for international travel and must be renewed before departure); Write a short note to give a hotel asking for a crib ("Hello, we will be staying with you and would like to request a crib or cot in our room, if available. Please let us know if this can be arranged. Thank you.").

summaries.title: Writing help
summaries.text: The user asked: Fix this opening: 'Hey, I wanna ask about the refund.' (Revise to: 'I am writing to enquire about the status of my refund.'); Should a formal letter use contractions (No, avoid contractions like 'don't' or 'can't'; write 'do not' and 'cannot' for a formal tone); Why do many slogans use imperatives like "Just" or "Try" (Imperatives feel direct and action-oriented, which makes the message stick and invites participation); What font and size should a CV use (A clean sans-serif or serif at 10–12pt, with 1–1.15 line spacing for body text. Consistency matters more than the specific choice); Explain the difference between 'Yours faithfully' and 'Yours sincerely' ("Yours faithfully" pairs with an unnamed recipient, while "Yours sincerely" is used when the recipient's name appears in the salutation); Explain the difference between a toast and a speech (A toast is a brief call to raise glasses, usually under a minute, while a speech is a longer structured address. Toasts often close a speech, but they serve different purposes).

summaries.title: أسئلة متفرقة
summaries.text: سأل المستخدم: متى يبدأ موسم الأمطار في السعودية؟ (المواسم تختلف حسب المنطقة، لكن الأمطار غالباً تزيد في الربيع على الوسط والشرق. الجنوب الغربي له موسم مختلف.)؛ ليش الشاي يطلع مرّ إذا خلّيته وايد على النار؟ (لأن الأوراق تنطبخ زيادة وتطلع المرارة. اسحبه بعد ثلاث إلى خمس دقايق وريّح.)؛ أعطني مثال على تشبيه في الشعر العربي. (في قول ابن الرومي: "وليس سوى الإسلامِ دينٌ محمدٍ ... إذا نحنُ كنا في البلايا نُراجعُ".)؛ متى أفضل وقت لقص الحشيش؟ (أفضل وقت الصبح بعد ما ينشف الندى، عشان ما تتعب الحشيشة وتطلع نظيفة.)؛ شنو معنى كلمة وجيز؟ (وجيز يعني قصير ومختصر، وكثير تستخدم لوصف الكلام أو النص القصير الواضح.)؛ كيف أستفيد من الفائدة المركبة؟ (كل ما بدأت أبكر وتركت المبلغ ينمو بدون سحب، زاد أثر الفائدة المركبة. الانتظام أهم من المبلغ الكبير.)

summaries.title: Programming questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Why does memory usage drop after a restart and then creep back up (A restart clears accumulated state, so gradual regrowth points to something that retains references or grows caches over time); Is it legal to hold multiple immutable references simultaneously (Yes, any number of shared `&T` references may coexist as long as no mutable reference exists); How do I create a Promise that resolves after a delay (Use `new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, delay))` to create a Promise that resolves after the specified milliseconds); Explain the difference between merge and rebase in one paragraph (Merge joins two histories with a merge commit, preserving both branches; rebase rewrites commits onto a new base for a linear history); Compare BFS and DFS (BFS explores level by level using a queue and finds shortest paths in unweighted graphs; DFS dives deep using a stack and suits cycle detection or topological sorting); Write a short PostgreSQL example of a transaction that transfers 100 between two accounts (BEGIN; UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - 100 WHERE id = 1; UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance + 100 WHERE id = 2; COMMIT;).

summaries.title: Cooking questions
summaries.text: The user asked: List the core aromatics for a basic Chinese stir-fry (Garlic, ginger, and scallion are the core, often with a splash of soy sauce and Shaoxing wine); Can cooked beans be frozen, and for how long (Yes, cooked beans freeze well for up to 3 months; freeze them in their liquid for best texture); Does adding baking soda tenderize beef for stir-fry (Yes, a small amount dissolved in water and tossed with sliced beef for about 20 minutes helps it stay tender); Suggest a high-protein breakfast (Cottage cheese with fruit and nuts, or a three-egg omelet with cheese and vegetables, both deliver solid protein); Does decaf coffee still contain caffeine (Yes, small amounts remain, typically 2–5% of the original caffeine content); Best way to cook bacon without a mess (Bake it on a foil-lined sheet at 400°F for about 15–20 minutes; it stays flat and splatters far less).

summaries.title: General knowledge questions
summaries.text: The user asked: What's the capital of Mongolia (Ulaanbaatar is the capital of Mongolia); Write a riddle where the answer is a shadow (I follow you in sunlight but vanish in darkness; I copy your shape but never speak—what am I? A shadow); Who painted the Mona Lisa (Leonardo da Vinci painted it around 1503 to 1519; it hangs in the Louvre in Paris); Describe the twilight zone of the ocean (It spans roughly 200 to 1,000 meters down, dimly lit, where many animals migrate upward at night to feed); What is a classic puzzle involving a wolf, a goat, and a cabbage (A farmer must cross a river with a wolf, goat, and cabbage; the boat carries only the farmer and one item, and the solution requires taking the goat first to avoid wolf-goat or goat-cabbage pairs being left alone); How far away is the Moon (The Moon averages about 384,400 km from Earth, though the distance varies from roughly 363,000 to 405,000 km over its orbit).

summaries.title: Health and fitness questions
summaries.text: The user asked: How long should a breathing session last (Five to ten minutes is a solid starting point for stress relief. Even two to three minutes of slow breathing can help in the moment); Explain the Heimlich maneuver briefly (Stand behind the person, make a fist above the navel, and give quick inward-upward thrusts until the object clears); Write a 20-second reminder script for taking posture breaks ("Stand up, roll shoulders back, tuck chin slightly, take three slow breaths, and reset your seat height before sitting down again."); Which foods are good sources of vitamin D (Fatty fish, egg yolks, and fortified milk or cereals are main sources, plus sunlight exposure); Give me the 20-20-20 rule in one sentence (Every 20 minutes, look at something about 20 feet away for at least 20 seconds. It relaxes the eye muscles used for close work); Does a lumbar roll help or is it overrated (It helps when the chair lacks lumbar support; place it at the small of the back to maintain the natural inward curve).

summaries.title: Hobbies and sport
summaries.text: The user asked: What is a triple-double in basketball (It's when a player reaches double digits in three statistical categories, most commonly points, rebounds, and assists); How should I punish a premature queen sortie (Develop pieces with tempo by attacking the queen while completing your setup, gaining time and central control); How do I freeze motion at a concert (Use a shutter speed of at least 1/250s, raise ISO, and open the aperture wide, since stage light is usually dim); Why does oil paint take so long to dry (Oil paints dry by oxidation rather than evaporation, and the oil binders react slowly with air, so layers can take days to weeks to cure); Compare watercolor and gouache (Watercolor is transparent and relies on the white of the paper, while gouache is opaque and can be layered light over dark); Name a podcast that covers science news weekly (Science Friday is a well-known weekly podcast covering current science news. Another option is Nature Podcast, which features weekly highlights).

summaries.title: Home and garden questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Best way to proof a garage door against rodents (Fit a snug rubber threshold seal and brush strips along the sides and top. Mice squeeze through gaps as small as a quarter inch, so close every opening); Is it too late to repot a root-bound plant (No—repot into a container one size larger whenever roots circle the pot, ideally in spring but any time works if the plant is struggling); Is it safe to clean glass with newspaper (Yes, newspaper's low lint and slight abrasiveness leave glass streak-free, though avoid it on wet, fragile surfaces); What causes smart home devices to disconnect from Wi-Fi (Common causes are weak signal, 2.4 GHz congestion, router band-steering, and IP address conflicts from too many devices); Do draft stoppers under doors really help (Yes, sealing gaps under doors reduces heated or cooled air escaping and can noticeably lower heating and cooling demand); Is it cheaper to run a dishwasher or wash by hand (A full, efficient dishwasher cycle usually uses less hot water than hand-washing. Run only full loads and skip the heated dry).

summaries.title: Learning and study
summaries.text: The user asked: Suggest a way to cut meeting time in half (Require an agenda and a stated decision goal before any meeting is booked. Cap default meetings at 25 minutes instead of 60); Create a five-question quiz on basic Korean greetings (1) How do you say hello? 2) Thank you? 3) Goodbye to someone leaving? 4) Good morning? 5) Nice to meet you? Answers: 안녕하세요, 감사합니다, 안녕히 가세요, 좋은 아침, 만나서 반갑습니다); How long should a five-minute talk actually be (Aim for 4 minutes 30 seconds of content, leaving buffer for pauses and audience reaction. Speaking pace averages about 130–150 words per minute); Explain the difference between mitosis and meiosis (Mitosis makes two identical diploid cells for growth; meiosis makes four genetically varied haploid cells for reproduction); Check this sentence for errors: I have completed a online course in project management (Change "a" to "an": "I have completed an online course in project management."); Why does sleep matter for memory (Sleep consolidates newly learned material, moving it toward long-term storage, so studying before sleep aids retention).

summaries.title: Money questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Check this: revenue 80k, COGS 32k, operating expenses 20k. What's operating profit (Gross profit is 48k; subtracting 20k in operating expenses leaves 28k operating profit); Compare envelope budgeting and the cash-only method (Envelope budgeting divides cash or digital buckets by category, while cash-only simply limits spending to physical money on hand. Envelopes give category detail; cash-only gives a single hard ceiling); Check if this statement is true: closing a credit card always lowers your score (False. Closing a credit card can lower your score by reducing available credit and shortening history, but not always); What's a good rule for how much debt is manageable (A common guideline is keeping total debt payments under about 36% of gross monthly income); Write a brief description of pet insurance (Pet insurance helps cover veterinary expenses for accidents, illnesses, and sometimes routine care, depending on the policy); What does it mean when a currency is pegged (A pegged currency has its value locked to another currency or basket, with the central bank intervening to maintain that rate).

summaries.title: Devices and software
summaries.text: The user asked: Quick tip to reduce spam (Keep your address off public sites and use a separate address for sign-ups. Never reply to spam, since replies confirm the address is active); How do I pin a participant so they stay on screen (Hover over their video and choose Pin, which locks them as the main view for you only. Hosts can also spotlight someone so everyone sees them); Write a short message telling attendees a video call is starting in five minutes ("Just a reminder that we'll begin in five minutes. Please test your mic and camera, then join when ready."); Compare authenticator apps and hardware security keys (Authenticator apps are free and work on any phone but are phishable if you type a code into a fake site. Hardware keys resist phishing entirely but cost money and need a spare); Write a polite refusal a support bot could use when asked for medical advice ("I can't give medical advice, but I can help you find general information or suggest contacting a healthcare professional."); How do I check if an email is a phishing attempt (Hover over links to see the real destination, inspect the sender address closely, and look for urgency or credential requests. When in doubt, contact the organization through a known channel).

summaries.title: Tool runs: tests, disk, files, servers
summaries.text: The user asked: Explain the difference between a unit test and an integration test (A unit test checks one small piece of code in isolation, while an integration test checks that multiple components work together correctly); How do I check if a server is up (Use ping to test reachability; if it responds, the server is up at the network level); Check if port 443 is open on example.com (You can use nc -zv example.com 443 or nmap -p 443 example.com to test if the port is open); How do I see just the files that changed (Use git status --short to get a compact list of changed and untracked files. Add --porcelain for stable, script-friendly output); How many days until the next leap year begins (The next leap year starts January 1, 2028, which is about 15 months away); How can I run only tests matching a pattern (Use the runner's filter flag, such as `pytest -k pattern` or `jest -t pattern`, to run only matching tests).

summaries.title: Travel questions
summaries.text: The user asked: How can I find out the minimum connection time for a specific airport (Check the airport's official website or the airline's booking site, which usually lists minimum connection times for domestic and international transfers); What should go in a travel first-aid kit for children (Include child-dose pain reliever, fever thermometer, bandages, antiseptic wipes, antihistamine, rehydration packets, and any prescription medicines. Add tweezers and a small flashlight); What animals should be watched for in Yellowstone (Bison, grizzly bears, elk, and wolves are the main hazards; keep at least 25 yards from bison and 100 yards from bears); Write a short riddle about an island (I am land ringed by water, reachable only by boat or bridge; what am I? An island); Explain how sand is formed (Sand forms as rocks, shells, and coral are broken down by waves, wind, and weathering into small grains over long periods); What items are banned from checked baggage entirely (Spare lithium batteries, e-cigarettes, fireworks, and most flammable or explosive materials cannot go in checked bags).

summaries.title: Writing help
summaries.text: The user asked: How do you spell the Russian word for yes (It's "да" — pronounced "da."); List three caption styles for a food post (Three styles: descriptive ("crispy, golden, gone in minutes"), playful ("calories don't count on weekends"), and minimalist ("Worth it.")); How do I address a letter to an organisation rather than a person (Address it to the organisation's title, such as "Dear Customer Services," and close with "Yours faithfully."); Give me a one-line poem about rain (Rain rewrites the street in silver shorthand); What's a good way to handle nerves before speaking (Slow, low breathing and a few minutes of speaking aloud backstage calm the body more than positive self-talk. Arrive early and test the room); How long should a cover letter be (A cover letter should typically be one page, around 250 to 400 words, focusing on the most relevant qualifications).

summaries.title: أسئلة متفرقة
summaries.text: سأل المستخدم: شلون أستفيد من ماء المكيف للزرع؟ (ماء المكيف ينفع للزرع لأنه خالي من الأملاح غالباً، جمعه واستخدمه للسقي.)؛ عطني معلومة عن ملعب كرة القدم الرسمي (الطول من ١٠٠ إلى ١١٠ متر والعرض من ٦٤ إلى ٧٥ متر حسب اللوائح.)؛ اذكر لي أهم أسباب قيام الدولة الأموية. (من أبرز أسبابها ضعف الدولة الراشدية الأخير وتنظيم معاوية بن أبي سفيان للشام واتساع الفتوحات.)؛ وش أفضل لغة برمجة للمبتدئين؟ (بايثون خيار ممتاز لأن قواعده سهلة وتقرأ مثل الإنجليزي تقريباً.)؛ كيف أراجع مادة حفظ بدون ملل؟ (غير الطريقة بين القراءة والكتابة والشرح بصوت عالي، هالشي يقلل الملل ويثبت الحفظ.)؛ كيف أقدر أفرق بين الكواكب في السماء؟ (الكواكب ما تلمع مثل النجوم، وغالباً تتحرك ببطء بالنسبة لباقي النجوم.)

summaries.title: Programming questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Can a 204 response include a body (No, 204 No Content must not include a message body); Quick rundown of Big O notation (Big O describes an upper bound on growth rate, ignoring constants—e.g., O(n²) means runtime scales with the square of input size); How many goroutines should I start for a worker pool (A common choice is runtime.NumCPU() or a few times that for IO-bound work. Benchmark to tune it for the workload); Does moving a value invalidate the original variable (Yes, after a move the original binding can no longer be used unless the type implements `Copy`); What does chmod 755 mean (It gives the owner read/write/execute and group/others read/execute permissions); Explain Big O notation in one line (Big O describes how an algorithm's time or space grows relative to input size, ignoring constants and lower-order terms).

summaries.title: Cooking questions
summaries.text: The user asked: How hot should the oven be for croissants (Start at 200°C (400°F) for the first 10 minutes to set the layers, then drop to 180°C (350°F) until deep golden, about 15–20 more minutes); Is a 15-minute meal actually realistic on a weeknight (Yes, if you use fast-cooking ingredients like eggs, canned beans, or pre-cut vegetables); Why does a dull knife cause more cuts than a sharp one (A dull blade requires more force and can slip off food, so it tends to skid toward fingers instead of biting cleanly); Can I bake bread in a cast iron Dutch oven (Yes, and it's excellent: preheat the pot, bake covered for steam, then uncovered to brown. The enclosed space mimics a professional steam oven); What is the difference between oolong and green tea (Oolong is partially oxidized and sits between green and black tea in flavor, while green tea is minimally oxidized and more vegetal); How long should tea steep (Black tea about 3–5 minutes, green tea 2–3 minutes, and herbal infusions 5–7 minutes).

summaries.title: General knowledge questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Write one sentence about the Aztec capital (Tenochtitlan was built on islands in Lake Texcoco and by the early 1500s was one of the largest cities in the world, with causeways, canals, and floating gardens); Define opportunity cost (Opportunity cost is the value of the next best alternative forgone when making a decision); Name three countries whose capitals start with the letter B (Bangkok (Thailand), Berlin (Germany), and Brasília (Brazil) all fit); What's the largest animal that has ever lived (The blue whale is the largest known animal ever, reaching around 100 feet and 200 tons); Is it true that humans have five senses (Not really—beyond sight, hearing, touch, taste, and smell, humans also have senses like balance, proprioception, temperature, and pain); Which museum holds The Persistence of Memory (That Dalí painting is held by the Museum of Modern Art in New York).

summaries.title: Health and fitness questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Someone's choking and can't cough—what now (Give five back blows between the shoulder blades, then five abdominal thrusts, and repeat until it clears); Check this: should I use a tourniquet for a small cut (No—tourniquets are for severe limb bleeding that won't stop; a small cut needs pressure and a dressing); List signs of poor sleep quality (Waking unrefreshed, frequent awakenings, daytime sleepiness, and relying on caffeine to function are common indicators worth tracking); Explain cadence in cycling (Cadence is pedal revolutions per minute; most cyclists aim for 80–100 rpm on flat terrain for efficiency); Write a short warm-up for a beginner before lifting weights (Do 5 minutes of brisk walking, then 10 arm circles, 10 bodyweight squats, and 10 hip hinges, all controlled and easy); How far should a monitor be from eyes (About 20 to 28 inches (50–70 cm), with the top of the screen at or slightly below eye level).

summaries.title: Hobbies and sport
summaries.text: The user asked: Check this: I prime a canvas, then paint with watercolor. Will that work (Watercolor needs an absorbent surface, so standard acrylic gesso will make it bead; use watercolor ground instead); Who has won the most World Cups (Brazil has won the most FIFA World Cups, with five titles (1958, 1962, 1970, 1994, and 2002)); How do I clean a paintbrush with dried acrylic in it (Soak the bristles in warm water with a little soap, then gently work out the dried paint, and use isopropyl alcohol for stubborn spots); Write a short description of the rule of thirds (Divide the canvas into a 3x3 grid; place key elements along the lines or at intersections to create balanced, dynamic compositions); What's the difference between a spinning reel and a baitcaster (Spinning reels are easier for beginners and handle lighter lures, while baitcasters offer more control and accuracy for heavier gear); Can you compare the penalty kick rules in football and hockey (In football a penalty is taken from 12 yards against only the goalkeeper, while in ice hockey a penalty shot starts from centre ice with the shooter moving in on the goalie).

summaries.title: Home and garden questions
summaries.text: The user asked: What does an energy audit involve (A professional checks insulation, air leaks, appliances, and heating systems, often using a blower door and thermal camera. It ends with prioritized upgrade recommendations); Does closing vents in unused rooms save energy (Usually not for central systems; it can increase duct pressure and reduce efficiency. It only helps with certain zoned setups); Why does a full freezer use less energy than an empty one (Frozen items hold cold and reduce the air volume that escapes when the door opens, so the compressor runs less); What should go in a donation bag versus a trash bag (Donate anything clean and usable; trash anything broken, stained, expired, or unsafe to reuse); Give me a quick way to clean a microwave (Microwave a bowl of water with lemon for three minutes, then wipe the loosened grime away); Compare the KonMari method and the 20/20 rule (KonMari sorts by category and keeps items that spark joy; 20/20 discards anything replaceable for under $20 in under 20 minutes. Use KonMari for sentiment, 20/20 for clutter triage).

summaries.title: Learning and study
summaries.text: The user asked: What is the Pomodoro Technique (The Pomodoro Technique is a time management method that uses a timer to break work into 25-minute intervals separated by short breaks); Write a short practice question on the quadratic formula (Solve x² − 5x + 6 = 0 using the quadratic formula. The roots are x = 2 and x = 3); Compare phonics and whole language approaches (Phonics builds decoding from letter-sound rules, while whole language emphasizes meaning and context; most effective instruction blends both); Give three tips for a job talk to a technical audience (Lead with results, define jargon once, and leave a third of the time for questions); Explain the Pomodoro Technique in two sentences (Work in focused 25-minute blocks separated by 5-minute breaks, then take a longer break after four rounds. The fixed timer makes starting easier and limits fatigue); Check this sentence: 'Yo soy tengo hambre.' (That's incorrect; say 'Yo tengo hambre' because 'tener' expresses hunger, not 'ser').

summaries.title: Money questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Check whether this is correct: tax evasion is legal (That is incorrect; tax evasion—deliberately not paying owed taxes—is illegal. Tax avoidance, using legal means to reduce tax, is different); Write a one-paragraph explanation of how central banks use interest rates to fight inflation (Central banks raise policy rates to make borrowing costlier, which cools spending and investment, slowing price growth; they cut rates to stimulate demand when inflation runs low); Write a short explanation of expense ratios (An expense ratio is the annual percentage of fund assets charged for management and operations, deducted automatically from returns); What's a chart of accounts (It's the organized list of all accounts a business uses—assets, liabilities, equity, revenue, and expenses—that transactions are coded to); Summarize capital gains tax in two sentences (Capital gains tax applies to profit from selling assets like stocks or property. Many systems tax long-term gains at lower rates than short-term gains); What types of insurance do businesses commonly need (Common business insurance types include general liability, property, workers' compensation, and professional liability).

summaries.title: Devices and software
summaries.text: The user asked: Why do legitimate emails end up in spam (Legitimate emails may be marked as spam due to poor sender reputation, spammy content, or aggressive filtering settings); What's the difference between absolute and relative references (Absolute references lock a cell with $ signs, like $A$1, while relative references shift when copied); Compare lithium-ion and lithium-polymer batteries (Both share similar chemistry; lithium-polymer uses a gel or solid electrolyte and can be shaped thinner, while lithium-ion is cheaper and more robust. Phones mostly use lithium-polymer for slim designs); Is clicking unsubscribe in spam risky (Yes, it can confirm your address is live and active to spammers. Only unsubscribe from legitimate senders you recognize); Write a short note explaining what an IP address is (An IP address is a numeric label assigned to a device on a network so data can be routed to and from it, like a mailing address for packets); How do I change a router's Wi-Fi password (Log in to the router's admin page via its IP address, open the wireless security settings, set a new WPA2 or WPA3 password, and save).

summaries.title: Tool runs: tests, disk, files, servers
summaries.text: The user asked: Is there a way to show status of a different directory (Run git with `-C <path>`, e.g. `git -C ../other status`, or `git --git-dir=... --work-tree=... status`. Each targets that repository's working tree); What does git log --stat add to the output (It appends a per-file diffstat showing lines added and removed for each commit. It gives change size at a glance without full patch contents); Can a reminder fire without a notification sound (Yes, most reminder apps let you set the alert to silent or badge-only in the reminder's notification settings); What command shows listening ports (Use netstat -tuln or ss -tuln to list all listening TCP and UDP ports); Is a cloud drive the same as a backup (No. A cloud drive syncs your working files, so mistakes and deletions replicate; a real backup keeps untouched historical copies); What's the difference between the index and the working tree (The index is Git's staging area holding what the next commit will contain. The working tree is the actual files on disk where edits happen).

summaries.title: Travel questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Explain overnight buses versus budget flights for long routes (Overnight buses save a night's accommodation and often cost less, while budget flights are faster but add baggage and transfer fees); List five safety rules for skiing (Always control speed, yield to downhill skiers, stop only in safe visible spots, obey signs and closures, and use helmets and proper gear); Compare medical evacuation coverage limits across typical plans (Budget plans often cap evacuation at $50,000–$100,000, while premium plans commonly reach $500,000 to $1 million); Is it safe to fly with a newborn (Most airlines allow newborns after 7-14 days, but pediatricians often suggest waiting until 1-2 months; check with a doctor for premature or health concerns); Check whether Jeju Island is good for hiking (Yes, Hallasan is a standout volcano hike, and the Olle trails circle the island with coastal views); How do I read a boarding pass (Look for your gate, boarding group, seat number, and boarding time—usually the four boldest items near the top and middle).

summaries.title: Writing help
summaries.text: The user asked: What is a cover letter actually for (It introduces why you fit a specific role and points hiring managers to your most relevant evidence. It complements the CV rather than repeating it); How do I end a toast without it feeling awkward (Finish with a clear cue like 'Please raise your glasses' and a short, definite toast line. A clean ending removes the awkward pause); Compare block and indented letter formats (Block format aligns everything to the left margin, while indented format offsets paragraphs and often the date and closing; block is now more common in business); Give me a closing line for a cover letter that asks for an interview ("I'd welcome the chance to discuss how my experience matches your team's goals and can make time for a call this week." Keep it confident and brief); Can you suggest a title for a story about a second moon appearing ("Two Tides" or "The Borrowed Moon" both work—the first hints at consequence, the second at origin); What are common mistakes in headlines (Common mistakes include being too vague, using clickbait, and failing to include key information or keywords).

summaries.title: أسئلة متفرقة
