summaries.text: سأل المستخدم: ليش يطلع لي خطأ undefined في جافاسكريبت؟ (غالباً تحاول تستخدم متغير أو خاصية ما تم تعريفها، تأكد من الاسم ومن ترتيب تحميل الكود.)؛ شنو أحسن تمرين للإحماء؟ (ابدأ بمشي خفيف أو قفز خفيف خمس دقايق وبعدها تحريك للمفاصل.)؛ هل ينفع أزرع ريحان في نفس الحوض مع النعناع؟ (أي ينفع بس النعناع ينتشر بسرعة، افصل بينهم بحاجز بلاستيكي داخل الحوض عشان ما يطغى عليه.)؛ اكتب لي رسالة تهنئة قصيرة برمضان. («مبارك عليكم الشهر، الله يتقبل صيامكم وقيامكم ويرزقكم العافية».)؛ اكتب لي رسالة قصيرة عن فوائد الشاي الأخضر (الشاي الأخضر فيه مضادات أكسدة ويساعد على الاسترخاء والهضم. اعتدل فيه وما تشربه على معدة فاضية.)؛ كيف أسوي كبسة لحم على الطريقة الكويتية؟ (حط اللحم مع البصل والبهار وخلّه ينطبخ، وبعدين ضيف الرز والماء الحار وخلّه على نار هادية.)

summaries.title: Programming questions
summaries.text: The user asked: How do you detect a cycle in an undirected graph (Run DFS or union-find, and a cycle exists if an edge connects two already-joined vertices); Explain the difference between 401 and 403 (401 Unauthorized means authentication is missing or invalid, while 403 Forbidden means the client is authenticated but lacks permission); Is force pushing after a rebase safe on a shared branch (Generally no; use git push --force-with-lease only on branches others aren't building on, and coordinate first); Explain test doubles briefly (Test doubles are stand-ins for real dependencies: dummies, stubs, spies, mocks, and fakes); Give an example of a CROSS JOIN (SELECT * FROM colors CROSS JOIN sizes; returns the Cartesian product, pairing every color with every size); Check the shape and dtypes of my array and frame (For a DataFrame use df.shape and df.dtypes; for a numpy array use arr.shape and arr.dtype).

summaries.title: Cooking questions
summaries.text: The user asked: What causes tea scum on the surface (Calcium and minerals in hard water react with tea compounds; filtered water reduces it); How do I make a stew thicker without cream (Mash some of the cooked vegetables, stir in a cornstarch or flour slurry, or add pureed beans or a spoon of tomato paste); Check whether honey is vegan (Honey is not considered vegan by most standards because it is an animal product, though some vegetarians accept it); Is saffron really worth the price (Gram for gram it's the costliest spice, but a pinch flavors a whole dish with honeyed, floral notes. Its expense comes from hand-harvesting roughly 150,000 crocus flowers per kilo); Suggest a vegetarian pasta dish with mushrooms (Try fettuccine with sautéed mushrooms, garlic, thyme, and a splash of cream or olive oil); Check this: is labneh a type of cheese (Labneh is a strained yogurt product often treated like a soft cheese in Middle Eastern cooking).

summaries.title: General knowledge questions
summaries.text: The user asked: When was the Great Pyramid of Giza built (It was built around 2560 BCE during the reign of Pharaoh Khufu); Check this: H2 + O2 gives H2O. Is it balanced (No, it isn't balanced; use 2H2 + O2 → 2H2O to balance the atoms); What is the largest animal on Earth (The blue whale is the largest, reaching up to about 100 feet and 200 tons); Explain the difference between Baroque and Classical music (Baroque music (c. 1600-1750) is ornate and contrapuntal with steady rhythms, while Classical music (c. 1750-1820) favors clarity, balanced phrases, and homophonic textures); Do penguins live at the North Pole (No, penguins live almost entirely in the Southern Hemisphere; the North Pole has no penguins); Write a one-line safety tip for thunderstorms (When thunder roars, go indoors and stay away from windows and plumbing until 30 minutes after the last thunder).

summaries.title: Health and fitness questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Compare a standing desk with a sitting desk for focus (Standing tends to aid alertness early but worsens fine motor precision and fatigue over time; alternating sit-stand every 30-45 minutes usually preserves focus best); Write a one-line definition of a micronutrient (A micronutrient is a vitamin or mineral needed in small amounts for normal body function); Can you list three breathing techniques for panic (Try extended exhale breathing, pursed-lip breathing, and the physiological sigh. All three emphasize long, slow exhales to counter hyperventilation); Flu vs cold — key differences (Flu hits suddenly with high fever and body aches, while colds build slowly with runny nose and mild symptoms); How do you perform the Heimlich maneuver on a choking adult (Give five back blows between the shoulder blades, then five abdominal thrusts just above the navel, alternating until the object clears); Quick tip for reducing neck strain at a laptop (Raise the laptop on a stand and add an external keyboard so the screen sits at eye level without craning the neck).

summaries.title: Hobbies and sport
summaries.text: The user asked: Write a short caption for a landscape painting of a foggy harbor ("Morning fog swallows the harbor, leaving only the faint masts of sleeping boats."); How long is a standard NBA game (An NBA game consists of four 12-minute quarters, totaling 48 minutes of regulation play); What's the best first move in chess (1.e4 and 1.d4 are the strongest; e4 opens lines for the queen and bishop and controls the center immediately); Is a 2B pencil softer than an HB (Yes, 2B is softer and darker than HB, which is the middle of the pencil grade scale); How can I make my piano practice more effective (Set specific goals, practice slowly, and break difficult passages into smaller sections); Explain the difference between an open and a closed file (An open file has no pawns on it, while a closed file has at least one pawn, which blocks rooks from using it effectively).

summaries.title: Home and garden questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Quick fix for fruit flies in the sink drain (Pour boiling water down the drain and set a small dish of apple cider vinegar with dish soap nearby); How do I protect furniture during a move (Wrap furniture in moving blankets or stretch film, remove legs where possible, and tape drawers shut. Corner protectors and cardboard sheets help prevent scratches); Check whether these two colors clash: navy and mustard (They don't clash; navy and mustard are complementary in tone and pair well with a neutral base); Do smart blinds need special wiring (Most run on rechargeable batteries or low-voltage adapters, though some models require mains power or a wired motor controller); What signs indicate a rodent infestation (Droppings, gnaw marks, grease rub marks along walls, and nighttime scratching sounds are common indicators); How much space should be left around a coffee table (Leave 14 to 18 inches between the table and the sofa for comfortable walking and reaching).

summaries.title: Learning and study
summaries.text: The user asked: Check this sentence for grammar: 'She don't have no time.' (It has a double negative; correct it to 'She doesn't have any time.'); Compare duolingo and anki for vocabulary (Duolingo builds habit through gamified lessons, while Anki excels at long-term retention via scheduled review); Give me a 25-minute study schedule for one sitting (Study focused for 25 minutes, then take a 5-minute break. Repeat four times, then rest 15 to 30 minutes); What are the main cases in Russian and what do they do (Russian has six: nominative (subject), genitive (possession), dative (recipient), accusative (direct object), instrumental (means), and prepositional (location after prepositions)); What does 'vocal variety' mean concretely (It means varying pitch, pace, and volume to mark importance—slowing down for key points, raising pitch for questions, and pausing before big claims); Are free online certificates worth listing on a resume (Yes, if they show relevant skills; list them under a certificates section with the issuer and completion year).

summaries.title: Money questions
summaries.text: The user asked: List three common causes of inflation (Demand outpacing supply, rising production costs, and growth in the money supply are common causes); What's a high-yield savings account (It's a savings account paying above average interest, often at online banks, usually with federal insurance up to set limits); Why are auto loan rates lower than credit card rates (Auto loans are secured by the car, which lowers lender risk, whereas credit cards are unsecured and carry higher default risk); What's a credit score (It's a number, typically 300 to 850, that lenders use to estimate how likely someone is to repay borrowed money); How do I buy an index fund (Open a brokerage account, search the fund's ticker, and place a buy order; many brokers also offer automatic recurring purchases); If prices double in 10 years, what's the average annual inflation rate roughly (It's about 7.2% per year, since 1.072 raised to the 10th power is roughly 2).

summaries.title: Devices and software
summaries.text: The user asked: Best way to connect a mechanical keyboard to a laptop with no USB-A ports (Use a USB-C to USB-A adapter or a USB-C hub, or choose a Bluetooth keyboard if wireless is acceptable); Can you explain what egress fees are (They're charges for data transferred out of a cloud provider's network to the internet or another region. Inbound data is usually free); What's the maximum scan resolution that matters for archiving documents (300 to 600 DPI is enough for searchable text archives; higher resolution mainly adds file size without extra legibility); What's a mesh network and when should someone use one (A mesh system uses multiple nodes that cooperate to cover a larger area with one network name. It suits multi-floor or large spaces where a single router leaves weak spots); Compare mechanical and membrane keyboards in two sentences (Mechanical keyboards use individual spring switches for tactile feedback and longer lifespan, while membrane keyboards use a rubber dome sheet over a circuit for a quieter, cheaper, mushier feel); Check this: is 192.168.1.1 a common router login address (Yes, 192.168.1.1 is one of the most common default gateway addresses for accessing a router's admin interface).

summaries.title: Tool runs: tests, disk, files, servers
summaries.text: The user asked: Compare incremental and full backups (A full backup copies everything each run; an incremental copies only what changed since the last run, saving space and time but requiring the chain to restore); Give me a checklist for setting up a weekly reminder (Choose the reminder title, pick a start date and time, set repetition to weekly, select the weekday, then save and confirm the alert); What causes high CPU with low memory usage (A tight compute loop, a runaway thread, or heavy syscalls can burn CPU while RAM stays flat. Profile with `perf top` or `top -H` to see thread-level activity); Compare top and htop briefly (Both show live processes, but `htop` adds color, scrollable lists, per-core bars, and mouse support. `top` is lighter and available almost everywhere by default); How big can a single file be on most systems (On modern NTFS or ext4 drives files can reach several terabytes, limited mainly by disk capacity); Explain the difference between an alert and a notification in calendars (An alert is the scheduled trigger tied to an event, while a notification is how that alert is delivered to you, such as a popup or email).

summaries.title: Travel questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Is it cheaper to buy UK train tickets in advance (Yes, advance fares on UK routes are often 50-70% cheaper than walk-up tickets, but they tie you to a specific train); Is a Schengen visa valid in all European countries (A Schengen visa covers 29 European countries in the Schengen Area, but not the UK, Ireland, or non-member states); Recommend a beginner ski resort in Europe (Consider Les Gets in France or Söll in Austria, both known for gentle slopes, ski schools, and family-friendly infrastructure); How many pages does a standard passport have (Most standard passports have 32 or 48 pages; some countries offer 64-page versions for frequent travelers); Which beach is famous for pink sand in Indonesia (Pink Beach on Komodo Island, and also Pink Beach on Lombok, get their color from red coral fragments mixed with white sand); What year did the Louvre first open as a public museum (It opened as a public museum in 1793, during the French Revolution).

summaries.title: Writing help
summaries.text: The user asked: Draft three tagline options for a bike repair shop ("Get rolling again," "Every ride, tuned right," and "From flat to fast." Each emphasizes speed of service and reliability); What's a good opening conflict for a story about a failed prophecy (The prophecy came true, but in the least useful way—so the believers must decide whether they were wrong or merely outwitted); Can a poem be one word long (Yes, and such poems are usually called one-word poems; the title or spacing carries much of the meaning); Explain when to use a semicolon instead of a period (Use a semicolon to join two closely related independent clauses, as in "The sky darkened; rain was coming." A period also works but signals a harder stop); Give me an example of a strong opening sentence for a cover letter (A strong opening might be: "I am excited to apply for the Marketing Manager position at XYZ Company, where my five years of experience in digital campaigns can drive measurable growth."); Explain the difference between a slogan and a tagline (A slogan is a repeated phrase tied to a brand's identity, while a tagline is a short line attached to a specific campaign or product).

summaries.title: أسئلة متفرقة
summaries.text: سأل المستخدم: اكتب لي تعريف مبسط عن الشعر الحر. (الشعر الحر هو شعر لا يلتزم بوزن واحد أو قافية موحدة، بل يعتمد على تفعيلة متكررة بحرية أكبر.)؛ اكتب لي طريقة تحضير الشاي الكرك خطوة خطوة (اغلي الماء مع الشاي والحليب المبخر والسكر والهيل والحبهان، وخلّه يغلي على نار هادية دقايق. صفّيه وقدمه حار.)؛ وش أسوي إذا نسيت المعلومات في قاعة الامتحان؟ (خذ نفس وابدأ بالأسئلة اللي تعرفها. أحياناً استرجاع سؤال ثاني يفتح لك المعلومة المنسية.)؛ كيف أقرأ توقعات الطقس بشكل صحيح؟ (ركز على نسبة الاحتمال وليس الرقم فقط، وشف الرياح والرطوبة مع الحرارة. التحديثات القريبة أدق من التوقعات البعيدة.)؛ ليش الحلى يطلع لي جاف؟ (يمكن فرنك حار زيادة أو خليطك فيه طحين أكثر من اللازم، جرّب تختبر بعود خشب قبل ما تطلعه.)؛ شنو الفرق بين المؤسسة الفردية والشركة ذات المسؤولية المحدودة؟ (المؤسسة الفردية أسهل وأرخص في التأسيس لكن الملكية والمسؤولية عليك شخصياً، أما ذات المسؤولية المحدودة فتفصل ذمتك عن الشركة وتناسب الشركاء.)

summaries.title: Programming questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Can I copy a file out of a running container (Yes: `docker cp <container>:/path/in/container ./local-path` works on running or stopped containers); What does \d match in a regex (It matches any single digit character, equivalent to [0-9]); Explain tree traversal: inorder, preorder, postorder (Inorder visits left-root-right, preorder visits root-left-right, and postorder visits left-right-root; these differ in when the root is processed relative to subtrees); Give me a command to stop and delete every container (`docker stop $(docker ps -q) && docker rm $(docker ps -aq)` stops running ones, then removes all containers); Write code to group a DataFrame by a column and sum another (Use df.groupby('category')['amount'].sum() to get a summed Series per category); Why does setTimeout with 0ms run after a Promise (Promise callbacks are microtasks, which run before macrotasks like setTimeout, even with 0ms delay, because the event loop prioritizes microtasks).

summaries.title: Cooking questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Check this: raw chicken stored above salad in the fridge — problem (Yes, that's a cross-contamination risk from drips; raw meat should always go on the bottom shelf); Compare sheet-pan salmon and skillet salmon for speed (Skillet salmon cooks faster, about 4 minutes per side, while sheet-pan takes 12–15 minutes total. The skillet gives a crisper crust); What's the best way to cook dried pasta (Boil in plenty of salted water until al dente, then drain and toss with sauce immediately); Suggest a vegan dessert that doesn't need baking (Try avocado chocolate mousse: blend ripe avocado, cocoa powder, maple syrup, and a splash of plant milk); List five breakfast foods from around the world (Miso soup with rice in Japan, chilaquiles in Mexico, shakshuka in North Africa and the Middle East, croissants in France, and idli with sambar in India); How much caffeine is in a cup of tea versus coffee (An 8-ounce cup of coffee has roughly 95 mg of caffeine, while the same amount of black tea has about 40–50 mg).

summaries.title: General knowledge questions
summaries.text: The user asked: What does the prefix 'meta-' mean now (Originally Greek for 'beyond' or 'after', it now often means self-referential, as in 'metadata' or 'metafiction'); Compare the sizes of Jupiter and Earth (Jupiter's diameter is about 11 times Earth's, and it could hold over 1,300 Earths by volume); Explain how neurons send signals (Neurons fire action potentials when depolarization passes a threshold, releasing neurotransmitters across synapses to excite or inhibit the next cell); Is 91 a prime number? Justify your answer (No, 91 = 7 × 13, so it is composite); Who was Hammurabi and what is his code known for (Hammurabi was a Babylonian king who created one of the earliest written legal codes, known for its principle of proportional punishment); Compare ionic and covalent bonds in one sentence (Ionic bonds transfer electrons between atoms, while covalent bonds share electrons between them).

summaries.title: Health and fitness questions
summaries.text: The user asked: How often should someone run to improve cardiovascular fitness (Aim for at least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity running per week, spread over 3–5 sessions); Is it true you can catch up on lost sleep (Partly; extra sleep on weekends reduces some debt but doesn't fully reverse metabolic and cognitive effects of chronic short sleep); How do I treat a minor burn (Cool it under running water for 20 minutes, then cover loosely with cling film or a clean non-fluffy dressing); Is napping good or bad (Short naps of 10 to 20 minutes can boost alertness, but long or late-afternoon naps often disrupt nighttime sleep); Suggest a cross-training activity for runners (Swimming is excellent—it builds aerobic fitness and strengthens upper body without impact stress); Quick one: how long do I cool a burn (Twenty minutes under cool running water).

summaries.title: Hobbies and sport
summaries.text: The user asked: Write a one-sentence summary of '1984' (In a totalitarian future, a man rebels against a regime that controls every aspect of life, including truth and language); Write a short explanation of what a hat-trick is (A hat-trick is when a single player scores three goals in one match, and a perfect hat-trick means one goal with each foot and one with the head); What's the difference between a yellow and a red card (A yellow card is a warning for misconduct, while a red card means immediate ejection; two yellows in one match also result in a red); How long is the average audiobook (Most audiobooks run about 8 to 12 hours, though length varies widely with genre and title); How do I keep food away from bears at a campsite (Store food in bear-proof containers or hang it at least 10 feet off the ground and 4 feet from tree trunks); Write a short description of the game Ticket to Ride (Ticket to Ride is a train-themed board game where players collect train cards to claim routes between cities, aiming to complete destination tickets and score points).

summaries.title: Home and garden questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Check whether a hub is required for Thread devices (Yes, Thread devices need a Thread border router, which is often built into a speaker hub or a newer router); Write a short description of mid-century modern style (Mid-century modern favors clean lines, tapered legs, organic shapes, and a mix of wood, metal, and bold accent colors); How do I measure for a slipcover (Measure the sofa's length, depth, height, and armrest dimensions, then compare with the slipcover size chart for a snug fit); How do I get rid of fungus gnats (Let the topsoil dry out and use yellow sticky traps; for heavy infestations, water with a mosquito-dunk solution); How far in advance should someone book a moving truck (Book at least two to four weeks ahead for local moves, and six to eight weeks for peak summer weekends when rentals sell out); Remove hard water spots from a shower door (Wipe with a vinegar-soaked cloth, let it sit five minutes, then buff dry to dissolve mineral deposits).

summaries.title: Learning and study
summaries.text: The user asked: How do I take notes faster while still legible (Drop full sentences, use abbreviations and symbols consistently, and leave generous margins so you can add detail later instead of writing it live); How do I handle a heckler (Acknowledge briefly without engaging the content, then redirect: 'Good point—I'll come back to that.' If it persists, calmly invite a conversation after the talk); How can I stop procrastinating (Break tasks into smaller steps and commit to just five minutes of work to overcome initial resistance); Give me three filler words to eliminate first (Target 'um,' 'like,' and 'you know.' Pausing silently instead of filling space reads as confidence); How do online course certificates work (They're digital credentials issued after you complete required coursework, often as PDFs or verifiable badge links); Compare outlining and mind mapping for lectures (Outlining enforces linear hierarchy and suits structured talks, while mind mapping branches radially and suits brainstorming or showing relationships between topics).

summaries.title: Money questions
summaries.text: The user asked: What is hyperinflation (Hyperinflation is extremely rapid, out-of-control price increases, often over 50% per month, as seen in 1920s Germany); Compare sole proprietorship and LLC for tax treatment (A sole proprietorship is taxed on the owner's personal return; an LLC is typically taxed the same way by default but offers liability protection and can elect corporate treatment); Is a business loan payment deductible (Only the interest portion is typically deductible; principal repayment is not treated as a deductible expense); How many yuan are in one US dollar (One US dollar is worth about 7.2 Chinese yuan); Is deflation the opposite of inflation (Yes, deflation is a sustained fall in the general price level, the opposite of inflation); Which is worth more, the British pound or the Swiss franc (The pound is worth more, trading around 1.13 francs per pound).

summaries.title: Devices and software
summaries.text: The user asked: What's the difference between scissor-switch and chiclet keyboards (Chiclet describes the flat, island-style keycap shape, while scissor refers to the mechanism underneath; most chiclet laptop keyboards use scissor switches); What is a presigned URL (A time-limited link that grants temporary access to a private object without sharing credentials. It's commonly used to let clients upload or download directly); Write a short greeting a customer-service bot could use ("Hi there! I'm here to help with orders, returns, and product questions. What can I do for you today?"); Give me a quick checklist for securing an email account (Use a unique long password, turn on app-based or hardware-key 2FA, add a recovery option, and review active sessions for anything unfamiliar); What does 'duplex printing' mean (Duplex printing means printing on both sides of a sheet automatically, saving paper); How does data durability differ from availability (Durability is the assurance that data won't be lost, while availability is the assurance that data is accessible when needed. High durability doesn't guarantee high availability).

summaries.title: Tool runs: tests, disk, files, servers
summaries.text: The user asked: What's the best way to check for scheduling conflicts (Compare proposed times against existing events, allowing for travel or buffer time, and flag any overlapping intervals); Write a command showing the last five commits compactly (Run git log -n 5 --oneline. It lists the five most recent commits with short hashes and subjects); How can I find the largest files eating my disk space (`du -ah /path | sort -rh | head -20` lists the biggest files under a path. On macOS, `ncdu` gives an interactive view); How do I skip a single test in Jest (Prefix the test with `test.skip` or use `xit` to skip it without removing the code); Compare RAM and disk storage in one line (RAM is fast, volatile working memory wiped on shutdown, while disk storage is slower and keeps data permanently. RAM holds what's running now; disk holds what's kept); Give a command to monitor disk I/O live on Linux (Use `iostat -x 1` from the sysstat package for per-device I/O stats refreshed every second. `iotop` shows per-process disk activity instead).

summaries.title: Travel questions
summaries.text: The user asked: What's the difference between a layover and a stopover (A layover is typically under 24 hours for international flights, while a stopover exceeds 24 hours and may allow you to leave the airport); What's the minimum connection time at Atlanta Hartsfield (Delta recommends at least 35 minutes for domestic-to-domestic connections, but 60+ minutes is safer in the world's busiest airport); Best tips for jet lag in kids (Shift sleep and meals gradually before the trip, get morning sunlight at the destination, and keep naps short until the new schedule settles); When was the first public steam railway opened (The Stockton and Darlington Railway opened in 1825 in northeast England, carrying both freight and passengers); What's the best month to visit Oman for mild weather (November through March brings cooler, pleasant temperatures across most of Oman); Does travel insurance cover lost luggage (Yes, most plans reimburse lost or delayed baggage up to a set limit, often $500–$2,500, with per-item caps).

summaries.title: Writing help
summaries.text: The user asked: What's the French word for 'book' (The French word for 'book' is 'livre'); What's a polite way to ask someone to reply faster ('I'd appreciate a quick reply when you get a chance' signals urgency without pressure); Give me the German translation of 'Good night' ('Good night' in German is 'Gute Nacht'); What salutation suits a letter to a government department (Use 'Dear Sir or Madam' if no name is known, or address the named official directly, e.g. 'Dear Ms Patel'); How many hashtags should a caption include (Instagram allows 30, but 3 to 10 relevant tags usually perform well. Quality beats quantity); What's a caption for a city night photo ("The city doesn't sleep" or "Neon nights and skyline lights" suit urban night shots well).

summaries.title: أسئلة متفرقة
summaries.text: سأل المستخدم: كم درجة الحرارة المتوقعة بالدمام الليلة؟ (الليلة الحرارة تنزل حوالي الثلاثين مع رطوبة عالية. الجو يكون دافي إلى حد ما.)؛ وش علامات الإعراب الأصلية؟ (أربع علامات: الضمة للرفع، الفتحة للنصب، الكسرة للجر، والسكون للجزم.)؛ شلون أكتب ملخص قصير لمقال طويل؟ (استخرج الفكرة الرئيسية والنقاط الداعمة، واكتبها بجملتين أو ثلاث بدون تفاصيل.)؛ شنو الفرق بين القهوة العربية والتركية؟ (العربية تنطبخ خفيفة وتنكه بالهيل والزعفران، والتركية تغلي غليان وتنشرب مع الرغوة ومرّة حيل.)؛ كم استمرت الخلافة العثمانية تقريبًا؟ (استمرت نحو ستة قرون، من أواخر القرن الثالث عشر حتى إلغائها سنة 1924.)؛ اقترح لي رحلة برية من الرياض إلى أبها (الطريق طويل، خذ استراحات في الطائف أو الباحة وتأكد من صيانة السيارة قبل الانطلاق.)

summaries.title: Programming questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Compare SameSite=Lax and SameSite=Strict for cookies (Lax sends the cookie on top-level navigations like link clicks, while Strict withholds it on all cross-site requests, including those navigations); Quick one: does SameSite=Lax fully fix CSRF (No, it reduces risk substantially but doesn't cover every edge case, like some top-level GET navigations. Pair it with CSRF tokens for strong protection); Explain multi-stage builds briefly (They use multiple `FROM` stages so build tools stay in an earlier stage and only the final artifacts are copied into a small runtime image); How do unbuffered channels differ from buffered ones (Unbuffered channels synchronize sender and receiver so each send blocks until a receive happens. Buffered channels hold up to their capacity and only block when full or empty); Can you sort a linked list in O(n log n) (Yes—merge sort works well on linked lists, splitting and merging nodes with O(n log n) time and O(log n) stack space); Write a comprehension that filters out odd numbers from a list (`[x for x in nums if x % 2 == 0]` keeps only the even values).

summaries.title: Cooking questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Write a short poem about spaghetti (Long strands of wheat, a twirl on the fork, spaghetti sings in a tomato embrace); What can I eat for breakfast without cooking (Yogurt with granola, a peanut butter sandwich, or overnight oats made the night before all require no morning cooking); How long can overnight oats sit in the fridge (They keep safely for about three to four days when covered and refrigerated); Write a short description of Iranian ghormeh sabzi (Ghormeh sabzi is a Persian herb stew with parsley, cilantro, fenugreek, kidney beans, and lamb, slow-cooked and served with rice); What is the difference between ravioli and tortellini (Ravioli are square or rectangular pillows, while tortellini are ring-shaped and typically filled with meat or cheese); What's the difference between a soup and a stew (Soups are typically brothier and served in a bowl, while stews are thicker with less liquid and chunkier ingredients simmered longer).

summaries.title: General knowledge questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Is the Girl with a Pearl Earring a portrait of a specific person (No, it is generally considered a tronie, a character study rather than a portrait of a named individual); When did synchronized sound become standard in Hollywood (It spread rapidly after The Jazz Singer in 1927, and by roughly 1930 most major studios had converted to sound production); Who wrote 'Pride and Prejudice' ('Pride and Prejudice' was written by Jane Austen and published in 1813); Give me a quick riddle with answer (What has keys but can't open locks? A piano); Is Frankenstein considered a Gothic novel (Yes, Frankenstein is a classic Gothic novel, blending horror, science, and Romantic elements); Who designed the Sydney Opera House (Jørn Utzon, a Danish architect, designed it with a series of precast concrete shells).

summaries.title: Health and fitness questions
summaries.text: The user asked: List three iron-rich foods (Red meat, lentils, and fortified cereals are all good iron sources); Is a multivitamin worth taking daily (For most people eating a varied diet it adds little, but it can fill gaps for those with restricted intake); Write a short checklist for what to do at a car accident scene (Ensure scene safety, call emergency services, check casualties for responsiveness and breathing, and don't move injured people unless there's danger); What's the first thing to do if someone collapses and isn't breathing (Call emergency services and start chest compressions at 100–120 per minute, about 5–6 cm deep, if you're trained); Someone fainted but is breathing—what now (Lay them flat and raise their legs slightly, loosen tight clothing, and monitor breathing until they recover); How often should posture be reset during a workday (A brief reset every 30-45 minutes works well, since static posture itself, not just bad posture, drives discomfort).

summaries.title: Hobbies and sport
summaries.text: The user asked: What's a deuce in tennis (Deuce is a tied score of 40-40, after which a player must win two consecutive points to take the game); Check whether *The Great Gatsby* is in the public domain in the US (Yes, it entered the US public domain on January 1, 2021, since it was published in 1925); How do I pick a needle size for worsted yarn (Most worsted-weight yarn labels suggest US 7–9 (4.5–5.5 mm) needles. Swatch first, since gauge matters more than the label); How many players are on a football pitch per team (Each team fields 11 players, including one goalkeeper); How do podcasts make money (Podcasts earn through ads, sponsorships, listener donations, premium subscriptions, and merchandise. Many use dynamic ad insertion for targeted advertising); Compare *Dune* and *Foundation* for someone new to classic sci-fi (*Foundation* is shorter and idea-driven with linked stories, while *Dune* is denser with politics, ecology, and a slower build).

summaries.title: Home and garden questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Is a smart speaker always listening (It listens for a wake word locally, and only streams audio to the cloud after that trigger, though mute buttons physically disable the mic); How do I fix a leaking faucet (Turn off the water supply, then replace the washer or cartridge inside the handle. Most leaks come from worn seals); Explain the one-touch rule (Handle each item once: open mail, file it, or bin it immediately. It stops piles from forming); What's the best way to arrange furniture in an open-plan living and dining area (Define zones with rugs and lighting, keep walkways clear, and use consistent colors to unify the spaces); Name one cheap device that reveals which appliances waste power (A plug-in power meter measures watts and kilowatt-hours for individual appliances, costing around $15–$30); What's the difference between a Phillips and a Pozidriv screwdriver (Pozidriv has four extra angled ribs between the main cross arms, so using a Phillips bit in a Pozidriv screw tends to cam out).

summaries.title: Learning and study
summaries.text: The user asked: Check this note for clarity: 'Meeting moved to 3pm, bring reports.' (The note is clear and concise. It states the time change and action item); What should a good course description include (It should list learning outcomes, syllabus, prerequisites, instructor bio, time commitment, assessment methods, certificate details, and cost); How to use color coding in notes effectively (Assign specific colors to categories like definitions, examples, or questions. Use consistently to aid visual memory and organization); Is grammar study a waste of time (No, but keep it short and apply each rule immediately in a sentence you say or write); Make a checklist for the night before an exam (Pack your ID and pens, set two alarms, review key formulas briefly, and sleep at least seven hours. Avoid last-minute cramming); Give me a quick breathing exercise to calm nerves before going on (Inhale for four counts, hold for four, exhale for six, and repeat three times. The longer exhale slows the heart rate).

summaries.title: Money questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Can closing a credit card lower a score (It can, because closing an account reduces total available credit and may raise utilization, though the effect usually fades over time); How should I handle a bounced customer check in the books (Reverse the original payment entry to restore the receivable, then record any bank fee as a separate expense); Compare floating and fixed exchange rate systems (Floating rates are set by markets and adjust freely, while fixed rates are held by central bank policy, trading flexibility for stability); Write a one-sentence explanation of withholding (Withholding is the practice of an employer deducting estimated income tax from each paycheck and sending it to the government); Is a sales tax regressive (Yes, sales taxes are generally considered regressive because they take a larger share of income from lower-income people); What does IRS stand for (It stands for Internal Revenue Service, the U.S. federal agency that administers tax laws).

summaries.title: Devices and software
summaries.text: The user asked: How long do smartphone batteries usually last before they degrade (Most lithium-ion phone batteries retain about 80% capacity after 300 to 500 full charge cycles, roughly 2 to 3 years of typical use); Is it safe to use public Wi-Fi for video calls (Risky without protection. Use a VPN or your phone's hotspot, and stick to services with end-to-end encryption where possible); Best free email client for Windows (Thunderbird is a solid free choice, with good filtering and many add-ons. The built-in Windows Mail app is simpler but less capable); Describe how syncing works in cloud storage (Syncing keeps files identical across devices by automatically uploading changes to the cloud and downloading them to other devices. It typically uses a client agent to monitor and transfer updates); What's the difference between a webinar and a meeting (In a webinar, attendees are view-only or limited to Q&A, while meetings let everyone speak and share. Webinars suit large audiences); How do I clear a paper jam in a laser printer (Open the rear and front access doors, gently pull the jammed sheet in the direction of paper travel, then close all doors and press the resume button).

summaries.title: Tool runs: tests, disk, files, servers
summaries.text: The user asked: Why would traceroute show asterisks for some hops (Asterisks mean those routers didn't reply to the probe, often due to filtering. The path can still be fine if later hops respond normally); Compare one-time and recurring reminders (One-time reminders fire once and are done, while recurring reminders repeat on a schedule you define. Recurring ones suit habits; one-time ones suit single deadlines); What does 3-2-1-1-0 mean (It extends 3-2-1 with 1 copy offline or immutable and 0 errors verified by test restores); How do I check if a website is down for everyone or just me (Use a service like Down For Everyone Or Just Me, or check the site from a different network. If it fails on both, the outage is likely server-side); What is test coverage and how is it measured (Test coverage measures how much of the code is executed by tests, typically reported as line, branch, or function percentages by coverage tools); How often should backups run (Match frequency to how much work you can afford to lose: daily for active documents, hourly for fast-changing data, weekly for static archives).

summaries.title: Travel questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Which European cities have the best Christmas markets (Nuremberg, Strasbourg, Vienna and Dresden are top picks. Nuremberg's Christkindlesmarkt is the most famous, running late November to Christmas Eve); Compare renting a car at the airport versus a downtown location (Airport rentals offer more vehicle choice and longer hours but often carry extra surcharges and taxes. Downtown locations tend to be cheaper but may have limited inventory and shorter opening times); How do toll roads work in Florida (Most Florida tolls use SunPass or pay-by-plate billing, so you can drive through without stopping and get billed later); Is it cheaper to buy train tickets in advance (Yes, advance tickets are often significantly cheaper than walk-up fares, especially for long-distance routes); What's the best way to stay warm on a chairlift (Wear windproof layers, cover exposed skin, and use hand and toe warmers; pull your hood up and keep gloves on. Sitting still on a lift chills you fast, so dress warmer than for active skiing); What's the longest continuous train journey in the world (The Moscow to Vladivostok Trans-Siberian service covers 9,289 km and takes about six days).

summaries.title: Writing help
summaries.text: The user asked: Should a formal letter include the date? Where does it go (Yes; in most conventions the date sits below the sender's address and above the recipient's address, written in full such as 3 June 2024); Compare a humorous toast with a sentimental one (Humorous toasts win the room fast but risk landing flat or offending; sentimental ones build warmth but can drag. Most effective toasts blend one light moment with one sincere one); Is it 'between you and me' or 'between you and I' ('Between you and me' is correct because 'between' is a preposition and takes the object pronoun 'me.'); Any tagline ideas for a rooftop bar ("Drinks above the noise" or "Skyline views, slow evenings."); What's a polite way to say no to a meeting invite ('Thanks for the invite — I won't be able to join this time, but I'd appreciate the notes.'); Write a correctly punctuated version of: however i was late so we left ("However, I was late, so we left." Add a comma after the introductory word and before the conjunction).

summaries.title: أسئلة متفرقة
summaries.text: سأل المستخدم: ليش تطلع صوت طقطقة لما أشغل المكيف أحياناً؟ (ممكن يكون من الكمبروسر أو السير، والأفضل يفحصه فني تكييف سيارات.)؛ شنو الفرق بين الدوري والكأس؟ (الدوري يُلعب بنظام النقاط على مدار الموسم، أما الكأس فبنظام خروج المغلوب.)؛ شنو الفرق بين الذكاء الاصطناعي التوليدي والنماذج التقليدية؟ (التوليدي ينشئ محتوى جديد مثل نصوص وصور، التقليدي غالباً يصنف أو يتنبأ بناءً على بيانات.)؛ متى كانت غزوة بدر الكبرى؟ (صارت في السابع عشر من رمضان في السنة الثانية للهجرة.)؛ وش أفضل وجبة خفيفة قبل التمرين؟ (موزة أو تمر مع شوية ماي يعطيك طاقة سريعة من غير ثقل في المعدة.)؛ شنو سبب صوت الصرير لما ادوس بريك؟ (غالبًا الفحمات خالصة أو الأقراص متآكلة. يحتاج فحص سريع عند ورشة.)

summaries.title: Programming questions
summaries.text: The user asked: What is a directed acyclic graph used for (DAGs model dependencies like build systems and task scheduling, and support topological sorting); Can you rollback a transaction after a deadlock (Yes, most databases automatically roll back one of the deadlocked transactions; you can retry it. Explicit ROLLBACK also works if the transaction is still active); Write a dict comprehension that maps numbers 1-5 to their squares ({n: n**2 for n in range(1, 6)} produces {1: 1, 2: 4, 3: 9, 4: 16, 5: 25}); What is a composite index and when should I use it (A composite index spans multiple columns; use it when queries filter or sort on those columns in the same order as the index definition); Why do conflict markers like <<<<<<< appear in files (Git inserts them where it can't automatically reconcile changes from both branches, marking each side's version); Explain the difference between greedy and lazy quantifiers (Greedy quantifiers match as much as possible, while lazy ones (with ?) match as little as possible. For example, a.*b grabs through the last b, a.*?b stops at the first b).

summaries.title: Cooking questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Write a short checklist for shaping a boule (Pre-shape and rest 20 minutes, then flip seam-side down, fold edges to the center, and drag on the bench to build surface tension. Seal the seam and place it seam-side up in a floured basket); Can I skip the second rise in a brioche recipe (You can shorten it but not skip it entirely; the cold retard develops flavor and firmness. Chill at least 4 hours, then let it warm slightly before shaping and baking); Explain the claw technique for chopping safely (Curl your fingertips under and press them against the blade's flat side, keeping knuckles forward as a guide. The knife rides your knuckles and never touches fingertips); Best way to thaw frozen fish (Thaw it in the refrigerator overnight, or sealed in cold water; never on the counter); How long can cooked rice sit out before it's unsafe (Two hours at room temperature max; rice can grow Bacillus cereus quickly, so refrigerate it sooner if possible); Can you explain al dente (Al dente means the pasta is cooked until firm to the bite, not soft or mushy).

summaries.title: General knowledge questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Explain the Silk Road in two sentences (It was a network of trade routes linking China to the Mediterranean from roughly 130 BCE onward. Goods, technologies, and religions moved along it, though few traders traveled the whole distance); How many languages are estimated to exist worldwide (Roughly 7,000 living languages are estimated, though counts vary with how dialects are classified); Is the Great Barrier Reef a single organism (No, it is a vast colony of many coral species and associated life stretching over 2,000 kilometers); How many times do clock hands overlap in 12 hours (Eleven times, since the minute hand gains a full lap on the hour hand 11 times in 12 hours); Write a short explanation of opportunity cost (Opportunity cost is the value of the next best alternative forgone when making a choice. For example, choosing to invest in stocks means forgoing potential returns from bonds); List some inventions of the Industrial Revolution (Key ones include the steam engine, spinning jenny, power loom, cotton gin, and the telegraph, all reshaping production and communication).

summaries.title: Health and fitness questions
summaries.text: The user asked: How much vitamin A is too much (Chronic intake above about 3,000 mcg RAE daily in adults can cause toxicity); Name two signs of iron deficiency (Fatigue and pale skin are common signs, often alongside shortness of breath); What's the best font size for reducing eye strain (Use a font size that allows comfortable reading without leaning forward, typically 12–16 points for screens. Adjust based on viewing distance); Compare running and cycling for calorie burn (Running typically burns more calories per minute because it's weight-bearing, but cycling allows longer sessions with less joint stress); How do I prevent saddle sores from cycling (Use chamois cream, wear padded shorts, and ensure the saddle fits properly; stand periodically during rides to relieve pressure); Can you give me the recovery position steps (Roll them onto their side, tilt the head back, and place the upper knee and arm to keep them stable).

summaries.title: Hobbies and sport
summaries.text: The user asked: Why are my indoor photos orange (The white balance is set for daylight while tungsten bulbs cast orange light. Switch white balance to tungsten or shoot raw and correct later); Recommend a good podcast for learning history (Try 'The History of Rome' or 'Hardcore History' for in-depth narratives. Both are widely praised for engaging storytelling); How do I keep minnows alive in a bucket (Use a aerated bucket kept in shade, change a third of the water daily with dechlorinated water, and avoid overcrowding); What does gauge mean in knitting patterns (Gauge is the number of stitches and rows per inch (or 10 cm) in a swatch. It determines finished size, so always swatch and adjust needle size to match); When was the first FIFA World Cup held (The first FIFA World Cup was held in 1930 in Uruguay, and Uruguay won it); Give me a warm-up exercise for guitar finger independence (Play the chromatic pattern 1-2-3-4 on each string from the first fret upward, keeping every finger close to the fretboard and using alternate picking).

summaries.title: Home and garden questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Does ultrasonic pest repellent actually work (Evidence is weak; most studies find rodents and insects habituate quickly. Traps, sealing gaps, and sanitation are more reliable); How do I get rid of wasps nesting under the eaves (Treat the nest at dusk with a labeled wasp spray from a distance, or call a professional for large nests); Explain why rooms feel bigger with light walls (Light walls reflect more light to the eye, reducing perceived shadow depth, so the space reads as larger); Can fabric softener damage athletic wear (Yes, it coats synthetic fibers and reduces wicking and elasticity, so skip it on athletic fabrics); What's the proper way to store paintbrushes between uses (Wrap them tightly in plastic wrap or foil and place in the freezer for short-term storage. For longer periods, clean them thoroughly with the appropriate solvent); How do smart thermostats save energy (They schedule setbacks and learn occupancy patterns, which can reduce heating and cooling energy by roughly 8–15%).

summaries.title: Learning and study
summaries.text: The user asked: What is the testing effect (It's the finding that retrieving information through self-testing strengthens memory more than rereading it); Compare mind maps and outlines for review (Mind maps suit seeing connections between concepts, while outlines suit ordered, hierarchical material); How should I structure notes for a research paper (Keep a source log with full citations, a per-source summary sheet, and a separate synthesis page where themes are linked across sources); How many practice problems should I do per topic (Aim for 5 to 10 varied problems per topic, then revisit missed ones. Quality of review matters more than raw count); What is interleaving and does it help (Interleaving mixes different problem types or topics in one session instead of blocking one at a time. It feels harder but improves discrimination and transfer on later tests); What's the difference between paraphrasing and quoting in notes (Paraphrasing rewrites the idea in your own words and aids recall, while quoting preserves exact wording and should be marked with quotation marks and a source).

summaries.title: Money questions
summaries.text: The user asked: What's typically excluded from homeowners insurance (Floods, earthquakes, and normal wear and tear are commonly excluded and need separate policies); Is 850 the highest possible score (Yes, 850 is the top of the standard FICO and VantageScore ranges); Quick one: what does amortization mean (Amortization is the schedule of payments where each installment covers interest first and then reduces principal over time); Are government bonds safer than corporate bonds (Generally yes, because governments have stronger repayment capacity, though this varies by country and currency); Summarize how inflation affects savings in two sentences (Inflation erodes the real value of savings if interest rates don't keep pace. Money left in low-yield accounts buys less over time); How does disability insurance work (Disability insurance replaces a portion of income if you become unable to work due to illness or injury).

summaries.title: Devices and software
summaries.text: The user asked: Why do legitimate emails sometimes go to spam (Missing SPF or DKIM records, poor sender reputation, or trigger words can flag real mail. Ask senders to authenticate their domain and whitelist known addresses); Explain absolute versus relative references in one line (Relative references like A1 shift when copied, while absolute ones like $A$1 stay fixed); How do password managers actually store my passwords (They encrypt your vault locally with a key derived from your master password, so the provider typically can't read the contents); List two benefits of using cloud storage for backups (Cloud backups offer offsite protection and scalability. They also reduce the need for physical media management); What is the difference between a laptop's USB-C and Thunderbolt ports (USB-C is a connector shape; Thunderbolt is a faster protocol that also uses USB-C connectors); What's a passkey and how does it differ from a password (A passkey is a cryptographic credential tied to your device and the site, so there's no shared secret to steal or reuse. It also resists phishing).

summaries.title: Tool runs: tests, disk, files, servers
summaries.text: The user asked: What's a quick way to test HTTP response time (Use 'curl -o /dev/null -s -w "%{time_total}\n" http://example.com' to get total time in seconds); How do I rename a file (Right-click the file and choose Rename, then type the new name and press Enter); My laptop fan keeps spinning loudly — could that be CPU related (Likely yes: sustained high CPU load or a stuck process heats the chip, so the fan ramps up. Check with `top` sorted by CPU and look for anything pegged near 100%); What does a 503 error indicate (A 503 Service Unavailable error means the server is temporarily unable to handle the request, often due to overload or maintenance); Should backups be encrypted at rest (Yes — encrypt backups at rest and in transit, and keep keys separate from the backup media); What does a red build status usually mean (A red build status means the build or its tests failed, so the artifact should not be considered reliable).

summaries.title: Travel questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Which country has the most extensive rail network (The United States has the longest rail network by route length, though much of it is freight-only); Which European city is best for street food (Istanbul is famous for its street food, from simit to balık ekmek, but Naples and Palermo are also strong contenders); How does cabin pressure affect jet lag (Cabin pressure mimics about 6,000–8,000 feet of altitude, which dries you out and disrupts sleep, worsening fatigue on top of time-zone shifts); Is it cheaper to rent a car at an airport or downtown (Airport rentals often carry extra surcharges, so downtown locations can be cheaper, though airport lots usually have more selection); What's the difference between a museum and a historic house (A museum is usually a purpose-built or converted space for collections, while a historic house is preserved at its original site with its original domestic context); What documents are needed to pick up a rental car (Typically a valid driver's license, a credit card in the renter's name, and proof of insurance if not buying the rental company's coverage. Some countries also require an international driving permit).

summaries.title: Writing help
summaries.text: The user asked: Proofread this: Their going to the store later (Change 'Their' to 'They're' because it's a contraction of 'they are.' The corrected sentence is: 'They're going to the store later.'); What's the difference between a toast and a speech (A speech is a longer set piece with structure and story; a toast is a brief 30-to-90-second raise-a-glass moment. Toasts usually end in an actual invitation to drink); Check the tone: 'You failed to respond to my email.' (It sounds accusatory; soften it to 'I have not yet received a response to my previous email.'); Give me the German word for a light rain ("Nieselregen" means a fine, light drizzle); What's a dek in publishing (A dek is the short summary line under a headline that expands on it and entices the reader. It's also called a subhead or standfirst); How should I handle references on a CV (Omit names and contact details; write "References available on request" or leave it off entirely. Provide references only when asked).

summaries.title: أسئلة متفرقة
summaries.text: سأل المستخدم: عطني جدول بسيط لتنظيم الوقت في رمضان. (قسمه بين النوم والعمل والعبادة والجمعات، وخلّ لك وقت ثابت للقرآن قبل الإفطار أو بعده.)؛ ابغى أعرف الفرق بين الكوكب والنجم. (النجم يطلع نور من نفسه، أما الكوكب يعكس نور الشمس.)؛ اكتب لي قائمة فحوصات قبل سفر طويل بالسيارة (افحص الزيت والماي والإطارات والفرامل والبطارية، وتأكد من الإسفنجية والأنوار.)؛ من هو شاعر النبطي المعاصر الأكثر تأثيراً؟ (يُعدّ الأمير خالد الفيصل من أبرز شعراء النبط المعاصرين، وله تأثير كبير في تطور الشعر النبطي.)؛ متى ابدل زيت القير الأوتوماتيك؟ (غالبًا كل ٤٠ ألف إلى ٦٠ ألف كيلو. راجع كتيب السيارة لنوع القير.)؛ اكتب لي رسالة اعتذار رسمية عن حضور اجتماع (أعتذر عن عدم تمكني من حضور الاجتماع، وأتمنى لكم اجتماعاً مثمراً.)

summaries.title: Programming questions
summaries.text: The user asked: How do I check what image a container was created from (Inspect it: `docker inspect <container> --format '{{.Config.Image}}'` prints the source image reference); Compare PUT and PATCH with an example (PUT replaces the entire resource, while PATCH applies a partial update; sending only a changed field is a PATCH, not a PUT); How do you add a key to a dictionary (Use dict[key] = value or the update() method to insert or modify a key-value pair); Why is escaping alone not enough in some HTML contexts (HTML escaping breaks in contexts like JavaScript strings, CSS, or URLs, so each sink needs its own encoding scheme); Give an example of a graph where BFS and DFS visit nodes in different orders (In a triangle 1-2, 1-3, 2-3 starting at 1, BFS visits 2 then 3, while DFS may go 2 then 3 via 2's edge); Quick way to undo the last merge commit (Run git reset --hard HEAD~1 if it hasn't been pushed, or git revert -m 1 <merge-commit> if it has).

summaries.title: Cooking questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Check whether decaf coffee still contains caffeine (Yes, decaf coffee retains a small amount of caffeine, typically 2–5 mg per cup compared with about 95 mg in regular coffee); How do I make overnight oats (Combine equal parts rolled oats and milk, add yogurt or chia if you like, refrigerate overnight, and top with fruit in the morning); Explain tempering chocolate in one sentence (Tempering heats and cools chocolate so its cocoa butter crystallizes into a stable form, giving a glossy snap); Quick dinner using frozen shrimp (Thaw shrimp under cold water for 5 minutes, then sauté with garlic and butter for 3–4 minutes. Toss with cooked pasta or rice); Give me three breakfast ideas that don't use eggs (Try overnight oats with berries, avocado toast with tomato, or a smoothie with banana, spinach, and peanut butter); How can I replace dairy milk in mashed potatoes (Use unsweetened almond or oat milk and olive oil or vegan butter for a creamy texture).

summaries.title: General knowledge questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Who built Machu Picchu and when (The Inca built Machu Picchu around 1450 CE, likely as a royal estate for Emperor Pachacuti); How many versions of The Scream exist (Munch produced four versions, two paintings and two pastels, plus a lithograph stone); Why do octopuses have blue blood (Their blood uses hemocyanin, a copper-based protein that carries oxygen and appears blue); Write a one-sentence summary of the French Revolution (Starting in 1789, it toppled the French monarchy, reshaped society around liberty and equality, and ended in Napoleon's rise); How do noise-cancelling headphones work (Microphones sample the incoming sound and the headphones play an inverted wave that cancels it by destructive interference); Is Pluto still a planet (No, the International Astronomical Union reclassified Pluto as a dwarf planet in 2006 because it hasn't cleared its orbital neighborhood).

summaries.title: Health and fitness questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Is it true that coffee dehydrates you (Only mildly and mostly at high doses; moderate coffee still contributes to daily fluid intake); What is sleep debt (Sleep debt is the accumulated shortfall from getting less sleep than needed; it impairs attention and mood and can't be fully repaid in one long lie-in); List three quick breathing techniques for immediate stress relief (Three quick techniques are deep belly breathing, box breathing, and the physiological sigh (double inhale, long exhale)); What's a good way to stretch tight hamstrings (Try a seated or standing hamstring stretch with a straight leg and a flat back, held for 20 to 30 seconds per side); Check this claim: vitamin C cures colds (That claim is overstated—vitamin C may slightly shorten a cold but doesn't prevent or cure it).

summaries.title: Hobbies and sport
summaries.text: The user asked: Give me three warm-up exercises before painting (Try loose gesture sketches, value scales in gray, and quick color-mixing swatches. Each takes about five minutes); Compare the Sicilian Defense and the French Defense for Black (The Sicilian gives unbalanced, counterattacking positions with a half-open c-file, while the French is more solid but often cramped behind the e6 pawn chain); What's the difference between a slip stitch and a chain stitch in crochet (A slip stitch is a join or a tight stitch with no height, while a chain stitch creates a foundation or space and has height); How do I pick up stitches along a knitted edge (Insert the needle under both loops of each edge stitch and knit through, spacing picks evenly along the edge); Name two card games that are played with a standard deck and involve trick-taking (Bridge and Hearts are two popular trick-taking card games played with a standard deck); Is there a card game where bluffing is the whole point (Yes—Cheat (also called Bullshit) is built entirely on lying about what you're discarding and calling out others' lies).

summaries.title: Home and garden questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Explain the purpose of a credenza in interior design (A credenza is a sideboard used for storage in dining or living areas, often holding dishes or media equipment while keeping clutter hidden); How do I declutter a closet efficiently (Work in one category at a time, keep only items used in the past year, and bag the rest for donation before rehanging); Explain how to unclog a drain without chemicals (Use a plunger or a drain snake to physically remove the blockage. A mixture of baking soda and vinegar can help break down minor clogs); Why are the lower leaves on a pothos turning yellow (Overwatering is the most common cause; let the top inch of soil dry out between waterings and check that the pot drains freely); Why are my monstera's new leaves smaller than the old ones (Smaller new leaves usually mean the plant needs more light or nutrients; move it closer to a bright window and feed it monthly in spring and summer); Explain the difference between task lighting and ambient lighting (Task lighting focuses on specific work areas like desks or counters, while ambient lighting provides overall illumination for a room).

summaries.title: Learning and study
summaries.text: The user asked: How does the SQ3R method work (SQ3R stands for Survey, Question, Read, Recite, Review. It guides you to preview, ask questions, read actively, recite key points, and review); Why is reading aloud to kids important (It builds vocabulary, listening comprehension, and a positive association with books before children can read independently); Name three things that hurt memory during studying (Passive rereading, multitasking with notifications, and cramming all undermine encoding and consolidation. Sleep loss is a close fourth); Suggest free alternatives to paid certificate programs (Open courseware from MIT and Yale, freeCodeCamp certifications, and library-linked platforms like LinkedIn Learning via public libraries are strong free options); Name three techniques that beat rereading (Active recall, spaced practice, and interleaving different problem types all outperform passive rereading); What's the most effective study method according to research (Active recall through self-testing consistently outperforms passive rereading in controlled studies. Spacing those tests over days adds another large boost).

summaries.title: Money questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Why do bond prices fall when interest rates rise (When new bonds pay higher rates, older lower-rate bonds become less attractive, so their prices drop until their yield matches the market); Compare sole proprietorship vs LLC for taxes (A sole proprietorship reports income on the owner's personal return via Schedule C; an LLC is taxed similarly by default but adds liability protection and options like S-corp election); What factors don't affect credit scores (Factors like income, employment history, and debit card use generally do not affect credit scores); Check this: did inflation rise if CPI went from 300 to 315 (Yes, that's a 5% increase in the CPI, indicating inflation rose over that period); Is a high-yield savings account worth it (Usually yes—it offers higher interest than a standard savings account with similar federal insurance protection); What's the difference between inflation and stagflation (Stagflation combines high inflation with stagnant growth and high unemployment, while inflation alone is just rising prices).

summaries.title: Devices and software
summaries.text: The user asked: What causes a printer to say it's offline when it's plugged in (Often the printer is set to Use Printer Offline in the queue, or the connection or IP address has changed; check the port settings and re-enable it); Why do some laptop keyboards have a numpad and others don't (A numpad requires a wider chassis, so 15-inch and larger laptops often include one while 13- and 14-inch models omit it to save space); Give me a checklist for securing an account (Use a unique long password, enable app-based or key-based 2FA, save recovery codes offline, and review active sessions for anything unfamiliar); What makes a good spam filter score threshold (A moderate threshold around 5 on a 10-point scale is common, catching most spam with few false positives. Tune it against your own mail flow and review flagged messages); What does 'token' mean in AI (A token is a chunk of text, often a word or word-piece, that the model processes as a unit); What should I do if a 2FA code arrives unexpectedly (Don't share or approve it; someone likely has your password, so change it immediately and check your account's login activity).

summaries.title: Tool runs: tests, disk, files, servers
summaries.text: The user asked: Explain virtual memory briefly (Virtual memory is an abstraction letting programs use more address space than physical RAM, backed by disk when needed. It prevents crashes but is much slower than real RAM); Write a short reminder note for watering plants weekly (Water indoor plants every Sunday morning, checking soil moisture before adding water); Write a short bash loop that pings a list of hosts (`for h in host1 host2 host3; do ping -c1 -W1 "$h" >/dev/null && echo "$h up" || echo "$h down"; done`. It reports up or down for each host); Can a reminder repeat on the last weekday of each month (Yes, some calendar tools support rules like "last weekday of the month" for recurring reminders); What does read-only mean for a file (A read-only file can be opened and viewed but not modified or deleted until its permissions are changed); Explain incremental vs full backups briefly (A full backup copies everything each run; an incremental copies only what changed since the last backup, making runs faster but restores dependent on a chain).

summaries.title: Travel questions
summaries.text: The user asked: List what's banned from carry-on but allowed in checked bags (Full-size liquids over 100 ml, most knives and tools, sporting equipment like bats and ski poles, and aerosol sprays above the limit are allowed checked but not carried on); What's the cheapest way to travel between Amsterdam and Brussels (FlixBus is usually cheapest, often around €10–20, taking about three hours. The train is faster at under two hours but costs more); What should a basic travel safety plan include (Emergency contacts, embassy details, copies of key documents, local emergency numbers, and a communication check-in schedule. Share the plan with someone trusted before departure); What causes rip currents (Rip currents form when water piled near shore by waves funnels back seaward through a gap, creating a narrow fast flow); Explain the difference between a ryokan and a hotel (A ryokan is a traditional inn with tatami rooms, futons, and often kaiseki meals, while hotels offer Western-style rooms and services); Check if hostel breakfasts are usually worth it (Often they're basic toast and coffee; free breakfast saves money, but paid ones are rarely good value).

summaries.title: Writing help
summaries.text: The user asked: Does 'irregardless' count as a real word (It appears in some dictionaries but is widely considered nonstandard; use "regardless" instead); How should a formal letter open when the recipient's name is unknown (Use 'Dear Sir or Madam' or 'Dear Hiring Manager'; close with 'Yours faithfully' in British style); How do I handle nerves before speaking (Slow, deep breaths and a few minutes of quiet rehearsal help most. Arriving early to walk the space also reduces surprise and anxiety); Is it ever okay to end a sentence with a preposition (Yes, it's standard English in most cases, as in "the person I spoke to." Rewording is only needed when the result sounds awkward); What's a strong closing line for a graduation speech (End with a forward-looking call: "The future isn't waiting for you; it's asking what you'll build. Go build it."); Explain the difference between a caption and alt text (A caption is visible post copy for readers, while alt text is a hidden description for screen readers and accessibility).

summaries.title: أسئلة متفرقة
summaries.text: سأل المستخدم: شنو الفرق بين التمساح والورل؟ (التمساح زاحف مائي بجلد حرشفي وفك قوي، والورل سحلية برية أسرع وخفة وأصغر حجمًا.)؛ كيف أطبخ مجبوس دجاج؟ (حمّر البصل والبهار وحط الدجاج، وبعدها ضيف الرز والماء وخلّه يتنفس على نار هادية.)؛ كيف ارجع ضغط الكفرات طبيعي؟ (روح لأقرب محطة وعبّي حسب الرقم المكتوب على باب السائق. تأكد والإطارات باردة.)؛ كم مدة نقع الشاي الأخضر عشان ما يصير مر؟ (الأخضر يحتاج ما بين دقيقتين لثلاث وماي أقل من الغليان. إذا زادت المدة يطلع مر وعفن.)؛ أبي أشتري سماعات بلوتوث، وش تنصح؟ (حدد ميزانيتك واستخدامك: للرياضة جرب Jabra، وللعزل الصوتي Sony WF-1000XM5 خيار ممتاز.)؛ ليش أوراق الطماطم صارت صفراء مع إن الموية منتظمة؟ (غالباً فيه نقص حديد أو تصريف الموية ضعيف، جرب تحسن التصريف وتضيف سماد غني بالحديد.)

summaries.title: Programming questions
summaries.text: The user asked: How can I sort a list of dictionaries by one key (Pass a key function: `sorted(people, key=lambda p: p['age'])`); Describe how quicksort's partition step works (Pick a pivot, then rearrange elements so smaller ones go left and larger ones go right, returning the pivot's final index); What is useEffect for (useEffect runs side effects after render, like subscriptions or data fetching, and can clean them up via a returned function); What does docker-compose do that plain docker doesn't (Compose defines multi-container apps in one YAML file, handling networking, volumes, and startup order with a single `docker compose up` command); What makes a unit test flaky (Shared state, real time, randomness, network calls, or test-order dependence — isolate those with seams or seeds); What's the fastest way to sort a million random integers (Quicksort or introsort averages O(n log n) and is usually fastest in practice; radix sort can win for fixed-width integers).

summaries.title: Cooking questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Is it okay to refreeze thawed chicken (Only if it was thawed in the fridge, not at room temperature; otherwise cook it before refreezing); What's a good way to label meal prep containers (Use freezer tape or masking tape with the dish name and date written in permanent marker); How do you make tofu taste less bland (Press it to remove water, then marinate in soy sauce, garlic, and sesame oil for 30 minutes before cooking); What is fish sauce and can I substitute it (It's a salty fermented fish condiment; substitute soy sauce plus a squeeze of lime for a rough equivalent); How long does a whole chicken take on a grill (At roughly 350°F indirect, a 4-pound chicken takes about 1 to 1½ hours; cook to 165°F in the thigh); What is the difference between kabsa and mandi (Kabsa is a spiced rice dish cooked with meat and tomatoes, while mandi is meat slow-cooked in a clay oven and served with rice).

summaries.title: General knowledge questions
summaries.text: The user asked: How many chambers does the heart have and why (Four: two atria receive blood and two ventricles pump it, with the separation preventing oxygenated and deoxygenated blood from mixing); How does the Pantheon's dome work structurally (The Pantheon's unreinforced concrete dome uses a coffered interior to reduce weight and an oculus at the apex for light and structural relief); Two fathers and two sons caught 3 fish, each got one. How (They were a grandfather, father, and son—three people, so each caught one fish); What materials were used to build the Pantheon in Rome (The Pantheon was built using concrete, brick, and marble, with a massive unreinforced concrete dome); Who directed Psycho (Alfred Hitchcock directed Psycho, released in 1960); Write a two-sentence blurb about Akira Kurosawa's influence on Westerns (Kurosawa's Seven Samurai was remade as The Magnificent Seven, and Yojimbo inspired A Fistful of Dollars. His staging and camera movement shaped the visual language of the genre).

summaries.title: Health and fitness questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Why do people wake up at 3 a.m (Brief awakenings are normal between cycles; waking around 3 a.m. often reflects stress, alcohol, or a too-early bedtime); Give me a quick explanation of antioxidants (Antioxidants neutralize free radicals that can damage cells, and are found in fruits, vegetables, and nuts); Write a short cool-down routine after cycling (Spin easy for 5 minutes, then stretch calves, hamstrings, and hip flexors for 30 seconds each); Which muscles does a plank work (A plank mainly works the abs, obliques, lower back, and shoulders); What lighting setup reduces glare on a screen (Place the screen perpendicular to windows and use indirect or diffused lighting. Avoid a lamp or window directly behind or in front of the display); Give me a quick checklist for an ergonomic workstation setup (Check monitor top at eye level, elbows near 90 degrees, feet flat, lower back supported, and screen about an arm's length away).

summaries.title: Hobbies and sport
summaries.text: The user asked: How do I read piano sheet music (Learn the treble and bass clefs, then associate notes with keys on the piano); What's the diameter of a basketball hoop (A regulation basketball hoop has an inner diameter of 18 inches (about 45.7 cm)); Suggest a daily 20-minute piano routine (Spend five minutes on scales, five on a technical exercise, five on a piece's difficult section, and five playing through repertoire for flow); Name three games with great soundtracks (Hollow Knight, Journey, and NieR: Automata all have widely praised soundtracks); How do you mix a muted green (Combine a green with a touch of its complement, red, or add a little yellow ochre to dull the saturation); Recommend a setting for freezing fast motion outdoors (Try a shutter speed of 1/1000s or faster with a low ISO and a wide enough aperture to expose correctly).

summaries.title: Home and garden questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Command: list steps to remove ink from a fabric sofa (Blot the ink with a cloth dampened with rubbing alcohol, working from the outside in. Rinse with cold water and let it air dry); Quick tip for a messy desk (Clear everything off, keep only daily-use items, and add one tray for incoming paper); Write a one-line reminder about unplugging chargers (Unplug chargers and small electronics when not in use to stop standby power draw); Why does a ceiling fan help in summer (Moving air makes skin feel cooler, so a fan can let you raise the thermostat about 4°F. Turn it off when the room is empty); Write a short voice command phrase for turning off all lights at night (Try: "Good night, turn off all lights." It's short enough for most assistants to parse reliably); Best way to keep raccoons out of trash bins (Use bins with locking lids and secure them with straps or place them in an enclosed structure).

summaries.title: Learning and study
summaries.text: The user asked: Write a one-sentence rule for beating procrastination on a big task (Commit to just five minutes of the task, since starting usually dissolves the resistance. Momentum carries you past the hardest part); Recommend a beginner-friendly online course on financial literacy (Coursera's "Financial Planning for Young Adults" and Khan Academy's personal finance series are solid beginner options); How many words do I need to hold a basic conversation (Around 1,000 to 1,500 high-frequency words cover most everyday conversation); Translate 'Where is the train station?' into Japanese politely (駅はどこですか (Eki wa doko desu ka) works politely); Write a short list of sight words for kindergarten (Common kindergarten sight words include: the, and, is, you, that, it, he, was, for, on, are, as, with, his, they); What is the Zettelkasten method (It's a system of linking individual notes by unique IDs to build a network of ideas. Each note contains one idea and references to related notes).

summaries.title: Money questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Check this logic: if fixed costs exceed 60% of income, is 50/30/20 workable (No, the 50% needs cap is already breached, so you would need a modified ratio or a plan to lower fixed costs); What's the difference between inflation and deflation (Inflation is rising prices; deflation is falling prices, which can happen during deep economic downturns); What's a good credit score (A score of 700 or above is generally considered good, with 750+ being excellent); What's the difference between fixed and variable rates (A fixed rate stays the same for the loan's term, while a variable rate moves with a benchmark index, so payments can rise or fall); Name three common budgeting mistakes (Forgetting irregular annual expenses, budgeting unrealistically low for food, and having no buffer category for surprises); Write a one-line definition of a variable-rate loan (A variable-rate loan has an interest rate that can change over time, typically tied to a benchmark index).

summaries.title: Devices and software
summaries.text: The user asked: What does SPF mean in email (SPF is Sender Policy Framework, a DNS record listing which servers may send mail for a domain. Receivers use it to detect forged sender addresses); What is cloud storage (Cloud storage is a service where data is stored on remote servers and accessed via the internet. It lets you save and retrieve files without relying on local hardware); Compare passkeys and passwords (Passkeys use cryptographic keys tied to your device instead of a shared secret, so there's nothing to phish or guess; passwords are portable but weaker and reusable across sites); Why do AI assistants sometimes refuse requests (They're often trained with safety guidelines that block harmful, private, or disallowed content. Refusals can also be false positives when a benign request looks risky); What is a guest network and why use one (It's a separate SSID with its own password that isolates visitors from your main devices and files while still sharing your internet connection); How do I freeze the top row (Go to View > Freeze Panes and choose Freeze Top Row so it stays visible while scrolling).

summaries.title: Tool runs: tests, disk, files, servers
summaries.text: The user asked: Should tests hit the real database or use mocks (Use mocks or an in-memory database for unit tests, and reserve real database tests for a smaller integration suite); Is there a way to set a reminder two hours before an event (Yes, most calendars let you add a custom alert offset, such as two hours before the event starts); Explain the difference between git log and git status (`git status` describes current working tree and index state, while `git log` lists committed history. Status looks forward at pending changes; log looks backward at what's already committed); What's the difference between a backup and a sync (A backup is a point-in-time copy kept separately so it survives deletion or corruption; a sync mirrors changes live across devices, so a deleted file disappears everywhere); Give a one-liner to check if a website is up (Use 'curl -Is http://example.com | head -n 1' to get the HTTP status line); Write a command that shows commits touching a specific file (`git log --follow -- path/to/file` lists commits that changed that file, following renames. Add `-p` to see the diffs).

summaries.title: Travel questions
