summaries.text: The user asked: What documents do I need to rent a car in the US (You'll typically need a valid driver's license, a credit card in the renter's name, and proof of insurance or a waiver purchase); Name a good family-friendly trail in Acadia (The Jordan Pond Path is a flat 3.3-mile loop with views of the Bubbles and a nearby popovers spot); Give three examples of barrier islands in the United States (Examples include Fire Island in New York, Padre Island in Texas, and the Outer Banks of North Carolina); Give me three tips to beat jet lag flying east (Shift bedtime 30–60 minutes earlier for a few days before flying, get morning light at the destination, and avoid late caffeine); How do I pack fragile items safely (Wrap them in clothing or bubble wrap, place them in the center of the bag surrounded by soft items, and avoid putting them near the wheels or edges); What's the emergency number in Europe (112 works throughout the European Union for police, fire, and medical emergencies).

summaries.title: Writing help
summaries.text: The user asked: Can you check if 'Je suis fini' is correct French for 'I am finished' (No, 'Je suis fini' means 'I am finished' in the sense of being ruined or done for. For completing a task, say 'J'ai fini'); How should I handle salary requirements in a cover letter (Avoid stating specific salary requirements in a cover letter; instead, indicate flexibility and willingness to discuss compensation based on the role's responsibilities); Difference between a title and a headline (A title names a work, like a book or article; a headline is the display line that sells a news story or piece of content. Titles identify, headlines attract); Give me a one-sentence definition of a sonnet's final couplet (It is the closing two rhyming lines that often summarize or twist the poem's argument); Is "embarazada" Spanish for embarrassed (No, it means pregnant; "avergonzada" is embarrassed. It's a classic false friend); What makes a tagline memorable (Brevity, rhythm, and a clear benefit, often with a bit of wordplay or contrast).

summaries.title: أسئلة متفرقة
summaries.text: سأل المستخدم: كم عدد الكواكب في المجموعة الشمسية؟ (ثمانية كواكب، وآخرها نبتون.)؛ شنو أسرع حيوان بري في العالم؟ (الفهد هو الأسرع على البر، ويوصل سرعته تقريبًا إلى ١١٠ كيلومتر بالساعة لمسافات قصيرة.)؛ وش يعني منخفض جوي؟ (منخفض جوي منطقة ضغطها أقل من حولها، وغالباً تجيب رياحاً وسحباً وأمطاراً.)؛ أبي أعرف الفرق بين التاء المربوطة والهاء في آخر الكلمة. (التاء المربوطة تنطق هاء عند الوقف وتُكتب تاء في الوصل، والهاء تبقى هاء دائمًا. جرب تقف على الكلمة وشوف صوتها.)؛ كيف أحمي مدخراتي من التضخم؟ (التضخم يأكل القوة الشرائية للمبلغ الراكد. فكر في أدوات استثمارية منخفضة المخاطرة تنمو مع الوقت.)؛ هل يحتاج الإطار الهواء يكون أقل بالصيف؟ (لا تنقصه كثير، التزم بضغط المصنع. الضغط الزايد أو الناقص يضر الإطار.)

summaries.title: Programming questions
summaries.text: The user asked: How do you delete the root of a max-heap (Replace the root with the last element, remove the last element, then sift down the new root by swapping with the larger child until the heap property is restored); Why does returning a reference to a local variable fail to compile (The local is dropped at the end of the function, so the reference would dangle; return an owned value or take the data as a parameter instead); How do I avoid stale closures in useEffect (Include all referenced values in the dependency array, or use a ref to hold the latest value and read it inside the effect); Does Content-Security-Policy stop XSS (A strict CSP with nonces or hashes blocks most injected inline script, but it's a defense-in-depth layer, not a replacement for output encoding); Write a short SQL injection example against a login form (A payload like `' OR '1'='1` in the username field can turn a query into one that always evaluates true. The fix is parameterized queries, not string concatenation); What's the difference between a binary tree and a binary search tree (A binary tree allows any ordering of children, while a BST keeps left values smaller and right values larger than the parent).

summaries.title: Cooking questions
summaries.text: The user asked: What's a good substitute for fresh ginger (Ground ginger works in baking at about 1/4 teaspoon per tablespoon of fresh, but for stir-fries or marinades, galangal or a pinch of dried ginger is a closer stand-in); Write a short description of manakish (Manakish is a Levantine flatbread topped with za'atar and olive oil or cheese, baked until crisp and often eaten for breakfast); Can I cook pasta and sauce in one pot (Yes, use a one-pot method: combine pasta, water, and sauce ingredients and boil until the pasta is tender and the liquid reduces. It usually takes 12–15 minutes); What percentage cacao counts as dark chocolate (In the US, dark chocolate must contain at least 35% cacao, though most products marketed as dark range from 50% to 85%); How do I dice an onion without crying so much (Chill the onion for 15 minutes first and cut with a sharp knife to minimize cell damage. Keep the root end intact until the end, since it releases the most irritant); How long does cooked rice keep in the fridge (Cooked rice keeps about 3 to 4 days in a sealed container in the fridge).

summaries.title: General knowledge questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Explain supply and demand (Supply and demand describe how prices are set: when demand exceeds supply, prices rise; when supply exceeds demand, prices fall. This interaction determines market equilibrium); Check this: heavier objects always fall faster than lighter ones (That's false in a vacuum; without air resistance, all objects accelerate at the same rate regardless of mass); Give a counterexample to 'all generalizations are false.' (The statement 'all generalizations are false' is itself a generalization; if true it would be false, so it's self-undermining rather than a clean counterexample); List two languages written right to left (Arabic and Hebrew are both written right to left); Compare arteries and veins (Arteries carry blood away from the heart under high pressure with thick muscular walls, while veins return blood to the heart at low pressure and have valves to prevent backflow); Who created the sculpture David in Florence (Michelangelo carved the marble David between 1501 and 1504; Donatello and Bernini also made famous Davids).

summaries.title: Health and fitness questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Explain the difference between dynamic and static stretching (Dynamic stretching moves joints through their range of motion to warm up, while static stretching holds a position to lengthen muscles, usually best after activity); Compare computer glasses vs. regular glasses for eye strain (Computer glasses often have blue light filters or anti-reflective coatings, which can reduce glare and strain. Regular glasses may not address screen-specific issues); How many minutes of stretching before a run is ideal (About 5 to 10 minutes of dynamic stretching is enough before a run); Quick tip for falling asleep faster (Try slow breathing with exhales longer than inhales, which calms the nervous system and speeds sleep onset); Check this claim: melatonin is a sleeping pill (That's inaccurate; melatonin is a timing signal that can shift circadian rhythm, and it's not a sedative, so effects on sleep onset are modest); Suggest three stretches for tight hamstrings (Try a standing toe reach, a seated hamstring stretch, and a lying band-assisted hamstring stretch, holding each 20 to 30 seconds).

summaries.title: Hobbies and sport
summaries.text: The user asked: What does the sustain pedal actually do (It lifts the dampers off all strings so notes keep ringing after you release the keys, letting you connect chords and blend harmonies); What's the difference between a tennis forehand and a backhand (A forehand is hit on the dominant-hand side of the body, while a backhand is hit on the opposite side); Check this sequence for a tactical mistake: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Nf6 4.Ng5 d5 (That's fine; 4.Ng5 attacks f7, and 4...d5 is the standard counter, hitting the bishop and opening the center); How do I read guitar tablature (Each line is a string with the highest string on top, and numbers show which fret to press; read left to right for timing and order of notes); Give me a quick drill to improve tennis footwork (Try the split-step drill: hop lightly as your opponent hits, land on both feet, then push off toward the ball); How do podcast ratings get calculated on Apple Podcasts (Apple shows an aggregate star rating from listener reviews, and it can reset when a show changes networks or relaunches).

summaries.title: Home and garden questions
summaries.text: The user asked: What's a fair way to tip movers (A common guideline is about 10 to 15 percent of the total bill, split among the crew, or a flat amount per mover. It is optional but appreciated for a careful, efficient job); What's the best way to move clothes on hangers (Keep them on hangers and use wardrobe boxes, or slide a trash bag over bundled hangers to carry several at once); Write a short routine for turning off all lights at bedtime (Use a single scene trigger at a set time that sends an off command to every light group and confirms each device responded); Check whether I need to notify a utility company before moving out (Yes, give the utility provider your move-out date and a final meter reading so the account closes correctly. Doing this a week ahead avoids being billed for the next occupant's usage); Do movers usually disassemble beds and wardrobes (Many removal companies will dismantle and reassemble standard furniture for a fee, but policies vary. Confirm in writing before booking what is included); Compare hiring professional movers versus a moving container service (Movers handle loading and transport but cost more; containers let you pack at your own pace and pay per container, though you do the loading).

summaries.title: Learning and study
summaries.text: The user asked: Compare memorizing a script versus speaking from bullet points (Memorizing gives exact wording but breaks badly if forgotten; bullets sound natural and flex with the room but demand practice to avoid rambling); Write a one-line rule for deciding what to write down (Record anything you could not reconstruct from memory or a quick lookup, and skip what is already in the slide deck); How long do most online courses take (Most run four to twelve weeks at a few hours per week, while self-paced ones vary widely); How many sight words should a first grader know (A typical first grader should recognize around 100 to 200 common sight words by year's end); Compare Coursera Plus and edX's subscription model (Coursera Plus is an annual all-you-can-learn subscription across most courses, while edX sells individual verified certificates and offers program bundles rather than one broad subscription); How do mind maps help with studying (They organize ideas around a central topic using branches, which shows relationships visually. This aids recall and brainstorming).

summaries.title: Money questions
summaries.text: The user asked: What's the best budgeting app feature to look for (Prioritize automatic transaction import with category rules, since manual entry is the main reason budgets fail); Quick tip for cutting a bloated budget (Audit recurring subscriptions and renegotiate fixed bills first; those cuts persist without requiring daily discipline); List the main factors in a FICO score (Payment history about 35%, amounts owed 30%, length of credit history 15%, new credit 10%, and credit mix 10%); Write a short explanation of how sales tax works (Sales tax is a percentage added to the price of goods and services at the point of sale, collected by the seller and remitted to the government); What's the difference between stocks and bonds (Stocks are ownership stakes with uncertain dividends and growth, while bonds are loans with scheduled interest and repayment, generally making bonds lower-risk and lower-return); What does a balance sheet show that an income statement doesn't (A balance sheet shows assets, liabilities, and equity at a point in time, while an income statement shows revenue and expenses over a period).

summaries.title: Devices and software
summaries.text: The user asked: How long should a strong password be (At least 12–16 characters is a good target; length matters more than complexity, so a long passphrase beats a short jumble of symbols); What is a hallucination in AI terms (A hallucination is when a model states false information confidently, such as inventing a citation or misstating a fact. It happens because the model predicts plausible text rather than verifying truth); Compare membrane and mechanical keyboards briefly (Membrane keyboards are quieter and cheaper but mushier; mechanical keyboards offer crisper, more durable switches and tactile feedback); Write a short polite report of a phishing email (Here's one: "I received a message claiming my account would be closed unless I clicked a link and entered credentials. The sender address did not match the organization and the link pointed elsewhere. Please investigate and advise."); Make a formula that adds A1 to A10 (Use =SUM(A1:A10); it totals every value in that range); Can you compare IF and IFS briefly (IF handles a single condition, while IFS checks multiple conditions in order without nesting).

summaries.title: Tool runs: tests, disk, files, servers
summaries.text: The user asked: Explain how recurring calendar reminders work (A recurring reminder repeats on a set schedule, like daily or every Monday, until an end date or indefinitely. Each occurrence can trigger its own alert); How do I check if the working tree is clean in a script (Use `git status --porcelain`; empty output means clean. Or run `git diff --quiet && git diff --cached --quiet` and check the exit code); Check whether a date range overlaps another range (Overlap occurs when the first range's start is before the second's end and the second's start is before the first's end); Command to show top memory-hungry processes on Linux (Run `ps aux --sort=-%mem | head` to list the biggest memory consumers first. Add `-n 10` style limits with `head` to control how many show); What's packet loss and why does it matter (Packet loss is the percentage of sent packets that never arrive. Even 2-5% loss degrades voice and video and triggers TCP retransmissions that slow transfers); List common reasons a service fails to start (Common causes include misconfigured settings, missing dependencies, port conflicts, or insufficient permissions).

summaries.title: Travel questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Compare window and aisle seats for long-haul flights (Window seats offer a view and a wall to lean on, while aisle seats provide easier access to move around without disturbing others); Check if there's a direct train from Paris to Berlin (Yes, there are direct high-speed trains between Paris and Berlin, taking about 8 hours); How long does the Bright Angel Trail take to hike to Plateau Point (Plan on roughly 8 to 10 hours round trip, about 12 miles with significant elevation gain); Best way to get from Amman to Petra (The JETT bus runs daily from Amman to Petra in about three and a half hours, or a private car takes roughly the same); How much should a city walking tour tip be (For free walking tours, tipping about five to ten units of local currency per person is customary if the guide was good); How do I use a Korean T-money card (Buy it at a convenience store, load cash, and tap it on buses and subways; it also works for some taxis).

summaries.title: Writing help
summaries.text: The user asked: Why do so many fantasy stories start in a village (Villages give a low-stakes baseline, so any stranger or odd event reads as significant. They also make the wider world feel discovered rather than described); What's the difference between a CV and a resume (A CV is a comprehensive academic document listing all publications and achievements, while a resume is a concise one-to-two-page summary tailored to a specific job); Can you condense this 2,000-word essay into about 100 words (The essay argues that urban farming reduces food transport emissions but faces land-cost barriers. It recommends rooftop incentives and zoning reform as the most scalable fixes); Suggest a headline for a news article about a new vaccine ('New Vaccine Shows 95% Efficacy in Late-Stage Trials' is direct and informative); How long should a headline be (Headlines typically range from 6 to 14 words, with 8-10 words being optimal for clarity and SEO); Give me the gist of this long article in two sentences (Archaeologists found a 4,000-year-old trading hub with imported pottery, suggesting wider ancient trade routes than previously believed. The site was abandoned abruptly, possibly due to drought).

summaries.title: أسئلة متفرقة
summaries.text: سأل المستخدم: شنو أحسن وقت أزور فيه جبل طويق؟ (أحسن وقت من نوفمبر إلى مارس، الجو يكون بارد وحلو للتنزه.)؛ ليش الناس يتسحرون تمر وماء؟ (لأنه خفيف ويعطي طاقة، والسنة أن يكون السحور بسيط ومو ثقيل على المعدة.)؛ هل الشاحن السريع يضر البطارية على المدى الطويل؟ (الشواحن الأصلية آمنة لأنها تنظم الشحن، لكن الحرارة العالية هي اللي تضر، فالأفضل تشحن باعتدال.)؛ من هو مؤسس الدولة الأموية؟ (معاوية بن أبي سفيان، رضي الله عنه، أسسها سنة 41 للهجرة.)؛ من هو الخليفة الذي بنى مدينة بغداد؟ (هو أبو جعفر المنصور، وقد بدأ بناؤها سنة 145 للهجرة.)؛ أبغى أعرف كيف أحسب تكلفة المشروع (اجمع كل المصاريف الثابتة والمتغيرة وحط هامش للطوارئ. قارن التكلفة بسعر البيع عشان تعرف ربحك الحقيقي.)

summaries.title: Programming questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Is it safe to read from a closed channel (Yes, receives on a closed channel return the zero value immediately without blocking. Use the comma-ok form to distinguish real values from close); Check this pattern: ^\s*$ — what does it do (It matches a line containing only whitespace, including empty lines, from start to end); How do I infer the return type of a function type (Use `ReturnType<typeof fn>` to get the function's return type); Quick one: what's 500 (500 Internal Server Error signals an unexpected failure on the server side); Can you check this for errors: SELECT name FROM users WHERE age = NULL (Comparing with NULL never matches; use WHERE age IS NULL instead); Explain test doubles like I'm new to this (Test doubles are stand-ins for real dependencies; stubs give data, mocks verify calls, fakes are lightweight working implementations, and spies record while delegating).

summaries.title: Cooking questions
summaries.text: The user asked: How is gumbo different from jambalaya (Gumbo is a thick soup-stew thickened with roux or okra and served over rice, while jambalaya is a rice dish cooked together with meat and vegetables); Write a short vegan shopping list for a beginner (Include lentils, canned beans, tofu, oats, plant milk, fruits, vegetables, rice, pasta, and nutritional yeast); Is tahini made from sesame (Yes, tahini is a paste made from ground sesame seeds); My knife drags through tomatoes—what's wrong (The edge is likely dull or slightly rolled, since a sharp knife bites tomato skin instantly. Hone it, and if it still slips, sharpen it on a whetstone); What goes well with pancakes (Maple syrup, butter, fresh berries, whipped cream, or bacon and eggs on the side all pair well); How is maqluba made (Maqluba layers rice, meat, and vegetables in a pot, then is flipped upside down onto a platter before serving).

summaries.title: General knowledge questions
summaries.text: The user asked: What was the main purpose of the Great Wall of China (It was built mainly as a defensive barrier against northern nomadic invasions, with watchtowers and garrisons along its length); Who was the first emperor of Rome (Augustus, who took power after Julius Caesar's assassination and ruled from 27 BCE until 14 CE); Explain why the Birth of Venus matters (Botticelli's Birth of Venus, painted around 1485, is among the first large-scale mythological nudes of the Renaissance. It revived classical imagery and became an icon of Western art); Which Brontë sister wrote 'Jane Eyre' (Charlotte Brontë wrote 'Jane Eyre'; her sisters Emily and Anne wrote 'Wuthering Heights' and 'The Tenant of Wildfell Hall.'); What's the difference between an atom and an ion (An atom is electrically neutral, while an ion has gained or lost electrons and carries a net charge); Who invented the telescope (Hans Lippershey is usually credited with the first patent request for a telescope in 1608, though others made similar devices).

summaries.title: Health and fitness questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Quick tip for using a laptop without wrecking posture (Raise the laptop on a stand to eye level and add an external keyboard and mouse so arms stay at a comfortable 90-degree angle); Write a 4-week beginner cycling plan (Start with 3 rides per week: 20 minutes easy, 30 minutes with 3 short efforts, and a 40-minute steady ride, increasing duration by 10% each week); How does the body make vitamin D from sunlight (UVB light converts a cholesterol compound in skin into vitamin D3, which the liver and kidneys then activate); Suggest a 10-minute cool-down after a run (Walk for 3 minutes, then do calf, quad, hamstring, and hip stretches for about 30 seconds each); Which vitamin is linked to blood clotting (Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and is found in leafy greens); How often should someone stand up from a desk (Roughly every 30 minutes, even for a minute or two of movement, helps offset prolonged static sitting).

summaries.title: Hobbies and sport
summaries.text: The user asked: What is an audiobook narrator called (An audiobook narrator is often called a voice actor or narrator. They perform the text, distinguishing characters and setting tone); Recommend a cooperative board game for four players (Pandemic is a strong pick: all four players work together to cure diseases before outbreaks spread, with no traitor mechanic); Write a short pattern for a garter-stitch scarf (Cast on 30 stitches with worsted yarn and US 8 needles. Knit every row until the scarf reaches your desired length, then bind off and weave in ends); Explain atmospheric perspective in one paragraph (Distant objects appear lighter, lower in contrast, cooler in color, and less detailed because more air sits between them and the viewer); What's ISO (ISO measures the sensor's sensitivity setting; higher values brighten the image but add noise); Compare knitting in the round vs flat knitting (Knitting in the round creates a tube with no seams, while flat knitting uses back-and-forth rows and requires seaming).

summaries.title: Home and garden questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Why does mold keep returning to the same corner of a ceiling (That spot likely stays damp from poor ventilation or a leak, so mold regrows. Fix the moisture source and improve airflow after cleaning); How do you get rid of ants without poison (Wipe their trail with vinegar and place barriers of cinnamon, diatomaceous earth, or soapy water at entry points); How can I get rid of hard water spots on faucets (Soak a cloth in white vinegar and wrap it around the faucet for 15 minutes, then wipe. Vinegar dissolves the mineral deposits); How do smart thermostats learn a household's daily schedule (They log when heating or cooling is adjusted and when motion is detected, then build a weekly pattern to preheat or precool before those times); How do I stop a garbage disposal from smelling (Grind ice cubes and citrus peels in the disposal, then flush with cold water. A baking soda and vinegar rinse also helps); Can I use wood filler on exterior trim (Use an exterior-grade epoxy or polyester filler, since standard wood filler cracks when it gets wet and freezes).

summaries.title: Learning and study
summaries.text: The user asked: How do I say 'thank you' in Japanese (The standard form is 'arigatou' (ありがとう), and the more polite version is 'arigatou gozaimasu'); What are good ways to take notes from a textbook (Use the Cornell method with a cue column and summary, and convert headings into questions before reading each section); Check this opener: 'Today I will talk about our quarterly results and the various factors that influenced them.' (It's accurate but flat. Try: 'We missed our target by 12%—and the reason is not what most people assume.'); Any trick to stop opening new tabs constantly (Keep a single 'later' list and close tabs you aren't using right now. Fewer open tabs reduce visual clutter and the urge to drift); What's the two-minute rule (The two-minute rule says if a task takes less than two minutes, do it immediately instead of planning it for later); What does interleaving mean in studying (It means mixing different topics or problem types in one session instead of blocking one type at a time).

summaries.title: Money questions
summaries.text: The user asked: How long do late payments stay on a report (Late payments typically remain for seven years from the date of the delinquency); Compare fixed and adjustable rates in two sentences (A fixed rate stays the same for the loan's life, giving predictable payments. An adjustable rate starts lower but can rise or fall with the market); How is inflation measured (It's typically measured by tracking price changes in a representative basket of goods and services, such as the Consumer Price Index); Give an example of inflation in the 1970s US (US inflation peaked near 14.8% in 1980 after oil shocks and loose monetary policy drove sustained price increases); What's the minimum credit score for a mortgage (Many conventional mortgages require a minimum score of 620, while FHA loans may accept 580 or lower); How do I check whether my savings are keeping up with inflation (Compare your account's annual percentage yield to the current inflation rate; if it's lower, your purchasing power is shrinking).

summaries.title: Devices and software
summaries.text: The user asked: What is a spam trap (A spam trap is an email address set up to catch spammers; it's never used for real communication, so any email sent to it is considered spam); What's the difference between POP3 and IMAP (POP3 downloads emails to one device and often removes them from the server, while IMAP keeps emails synced across multiple devices); Recommend a scanning resolution for archiving text documents (300 DPI in grayscale or black-and-white is generally sufficient for archiving text documents while keeping file sizes manageable); What does 'eleven nines of durability' mean (Eleven nines of durability means 99.999999999% annual durability, implying a very low probability of data loss. It is a common rating for major cloud object storage services); What's the difference between a laser printer and an inkjet (Laser printers use toner and are faster for text, while inkjets use liquid ink and excel at photos); Check this password for strength: Tr0ub4dor&3 (It looks complex but follows a common pattern and is short; a longer random passphrase would be considerably stronger).

summaries.title: Tool runs: tests, disk, files, servers
summaries.text: The user asked: What's the difference between a file and a folder (A file holds data like text or images, while a folder is a container that holds files and other folders); Compare flaky tests and failed tests (A failed test fails consistently for a real reason, while a flaky test passes and fails intermittently, often due to timing or shared state); How to check disk space on a remote server (SSH into the server and run 'df -h' to see disk usage in human-readable format); Compare uptime and top for checking system load (uptime shows load averages and uptime, while top provides real-time process and resource details); What does the 'both modified' status mean (It indicates a merge conflict: the file changed in both branches since their common ancestor. Resolve the conflict, then `git add` the file); What's the max file size on a USB drive formatted as exFAT (exFAT supports files up to 16 exabytes, so effectively there is no practical file size limit for normal use).

summaries.title: Travel questions
summaries.text: The user asked: What's the difference between Tokyo and Osaka vibes (Tokyo is vast, polished, and district-by-district; Osaka is looser, food-focused, and more compact around Namba and Umeda); Can I bring a full water bottle through airport security (No, containers over 100 ml (3.4 oz) must be empty at the checkpoint. Refill after security or buy drinks in the terminal); Write a one-sentence description of a coral atoll (A coral atoll is a ring-shaped reef enclosing a central lagoon, often topped with low sandy islets); How do I check the avalanche forecast for an area (Look up the regional avalanche center's website or app, which issues daily danger ratings by elevation and aspect. Read the forecast's danger scale, problem types, and travel advice before heading out); What is a visa on arrival (It's a visa issued at the border when you land, rather than before departure, often with a fee and specific eligibility rules); Explain how to childproof a hotel room quickly (Move fragile items and cords out of reach, cover outlets with tape, block sharp corners with towels, and request a crib away from windows and blind cords).

summaries.title: Writing help
summaries.text: The user asked: Check this line: 'I've known him since we were kids and he's always been there.' (It's grammatically fine but generic. Swap in one specific incident or trait so the audience sees him rather than just hearing praise); Short casual: best way to end a short story (End a beat after the change lands, on something concrete the character now does differently); Write a caption for a hiking photo ("The view is worth every step" fits well, or "Trade the screen for the summit" for a punchier tone); Write a two-sentence formal complaint about a delayed delivery (I am writing to express my concern regarding the delayed delivery of my order, which was due on the agreed date. I would appreciate a prompt explanation and confirmation of when it will arrive); Give me a title for a blog post about time management (Try 'Master Time Management: 7 Strategies to Boost Productivity and Reduce Stress'); Compare 'ser' and 'estar' in Spanish ('Ser' is used for permanent or inherent traits, while 'estar' is used for temporary states or locations).

summaries.title: أسئلة متفرقة
summaries.text: سأل المستخدم: كيف أحجز تذكرة قطار الحرمين؟ (عن طريق موقعهم الرسمي أو التطبيق، وتحجز قبل بكم يوم عشان تلاقي مقاعد.)؛ كيف أكتب رسالة رسمية لجهة حكومية؟ (ابدأ بالتحية واسم الجهة، بعدها اكتب موضوعك باختصار وطلبك بوضوح، واختم بالشكر والتوقيع.)؛ كم ضغط الإطارات المناسب عادة؟ (الرقم موجود على استيكر باب السواق أو دليل السيارة، وعادة بين ٣٠ و٣٥ PSI.)؛ هل الرطوبة تأثر على الإحساس بالحرارة؟ (نعم، الرطوبة العالية تخلي الحرارة تحس فيها أعلى من قيمتها الفعلية.)؛ شلون أخزّن حبوب القهوة عشان تبقى طازة؟ (حطها في علبة محكمة بعيد عن الشمس والرطوبة، والأفضل تطحنها وقت الاستخدام.)؛ وش أكلات رمضان المشهورة في الخليج؟ (الهريس والثريد واللقيمات والسمبوسة، وكل بيت له لمسته الخاصة.)

summaries.title: Programming questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Explain reference counting cycles in Swift (Two objects holding strong references to each other keep their counts above zero forever. Break the cycle with `weak` or `unowned` on one side); Show me a multi-stage build that compiles a Go binary into a tiny image (Use `FROM golang:1.22 AS build`, `WORKDIR /src`, copy files, `RUN CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o app`, then `FROM scratch` (or alpine), `COPY --from=build /src/app /app`, and `ENTRYPOINT ["/app"]`); What does the `Copy` trait actually do (It makes assignment and passing copy the bits instead of moving, so the original stays usable); What does topological sort produce for a DAG (A linear ordering where every directed edge points from earlier to later, valid only if the graph is acyclic); Give a one-line rule of thumb for ownership (Each value has one owner at a time; when the owner goes out of scope, the value is dropped); What is a lost update and how to prevent it (A lost update occurs when two transactions read and write the same row, and one overwrites the other's change. Prevent it with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE or by using a higher isolation level like repeatable read with locking).

summaries.title: Cooking questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Check whether leftover pasta should be stored with sauce or without (Store it with a little sauce to prevent sticking, but keep extra sauce separate so the pasta doesn't absorb it all); What's the quickest way to cook dried pasta (Boil it in salted water; thin spaghetti cooks in about 7–9 minutes, the fastest common shape); What spices go into baharat (Baharat typically includes black pepper, cumin, coriander, cinnamon, cloves, cardamom, and nutmeg); Give me a quick formula for batch-cooking grains for the week (Cook 1 cup dry grain per 2 to 3 meals planned, using a 1:2 grain-to-water ratio for rice and 1:3 for oats); What is shakshuka (Shakshuka is a North African dish of eggs poached in a spicy tomato and pepper sauce, often served in the Levant); How do I keep rice noodles from sticking (Soak or boil them just until tender, then rinse under cold water and toss with a little oil. Add them to the wok last and toss gently).

summaries.title: General knowledge questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Why is 'colonel' pronounced with an r sound (It came through French 'coronel' before settling on the Italian spelling 'colonel', so the pronunciation kept the older r-form); Give me a quick logic puzzle with the answer (Three boxes labeled Apples, Oranges, and Mixed are all mislabeled; drawing one fruit from the Mixed-labeled box tells you all three); Why did the Roman Empire split (Emperor Diocletian divided the empire administratively in 285 CE to ease governance, and the split became permanent after Theodosius in 395 CE); Was Frida Kahlo a surrealist (She denied it, saying she painted her own reality, though critics often group her work with Surrealism); Compare acids and bases in one sentence (Acids donate protons and lower pH, while bases accept protons and raise pH); List three animals that can regrow body parts (Axolotls, starfish, and planarian flatworms can all regenerate lost body parts).

summaries.title: Health and fitness questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Give me a quick checklist for staying hydrated outdoors in summer (Carry water, drink on a schedule, add electrolytes for long sweats, wear light clothing, and rest in shade); How far should a monitor be from the eyes (About 50-75 cm, roughly an arm's length, with the top of the screen at or slightly below eye level); Write a one-line tip for preventing colds (Wash hands often with soap and water for at least 20 seconds, especially before eating); Explain the difference between static and dynamic stretching (Static stretching holds a position still, while dynamic stretching moves joints through their range of motion); Write a short checklist for treating a nosebleed (Sit upright, lean forward, pinch the soft part of the nose for 10 minutes, and avoid tilting the head back); Is the flu shot worth it (Yes, it reduces flu risk and severity, and it's updated yearly for circulating strains).

summaries.title: Hobbies and sport
summaries.text: The user asked: Write a short explanation of opposition in king and pawn endgames (Opposition means kings face each other with one square between them and the side to move must give way, letting the other king advance); Is linseed oil safe on canvas (Yes, refined linseed oil is a standard oil-painting medium, but use it thinly and let each layer dry); Is there a podcast about learning Spanish ('Coffee Break Spanish' is a popular option, starting from beginner level with short, structured lessons); How do I tune a guitar to standard tuning (Standard tuning is E-A-D-G-B-E from the lowest string to the highest; tune each string to those pitches using a tuner or a reference tone); What speed do most people listen to audiobooks at (Many listeners use 1.25x to 1.5x speed, though surveys vary and plenty stick to normal speed); Check this: I plan to fish a weed edge at noon in July (That works, but fish the shaded or deeper side of the weed edge and slow your retrieve, since midday summer bass sit tight to cover).

summaries.title: Home and garden questions
summaries.text: The user asked: How many items should I aim to remove per session (Aim for one bag or about ten items; a fixed small target beats an open-ended purge); What actually attracts cockroaches into a kitchen (Crumbs, grease film, standing water, and cardboard boxes are the main draws. Roaches also shelter in warm gaps behind appliances); Compare traps and bait stations for mice (Traps kill quickly but need disposal, while bait stations target multiple mice over time yet risk secondary poisoning of predators); Quick fix for a leaky pipe joint (Dry the joint, wrap self-fusing silicone tape tightly around it, or apply epoxy putty for a longer-lasting patch); Best way to clean a greasy stovetop (Sprinkle baking soda on the grease, add a few drops of dish soap and warm water, then scrub gently. Wipe clean with a damp cloth); Does ultrasonic pest repellent work (Evidence is weak; studies show rodents and insects largely habituate, so physical exclusion is more reliable).

summaries.title: Learning and study
summaries.text: The user asked: Compare classical and operant conditioning (Classical conditions involuntary responses to stimuli; operant conditions voluntary behavior through rewards and punishments); How long should a Pomodoro session be (The classic format is 25 minutes of focused work followed by a 5-minute break, with a longer break every four cycles); Is it bad to read from a script (Not inherently, but verbatim reading flattens engagement and eye contact. Use a script as a rehearsal tool, then speak from a condensed outline); Why do I forget things I just read (Most forgetting happens fast because passive reading creates weak retrieval cues. Converting the material into questions you answer yourself strengthens those cues); Suggest three productivity apps (Todoist for task management, RescueTime for tracking time, and Focus@Will for focus-enhancing music); Are online certificates respected by employers (They vary by field; certificates from accredited universities and recognized tech vendors carry more weight than generic completion badges, especially when paired with a portfolio).

summaries.title: Money questions
summaries.text: The user asked: How does compound interest work in savings (Interest earns interest over time, so a balance grows faster the longer it stays and the more often interest compounds); Quick take: is travel insurance necessary for a domestic trip (Not always, but it can help with cancellations, lost luggage, and medical costs abroad or far from home); What score counts as good (Scores of 670 to 739 are generally considered good, with 740 and above very good to exceptional); Is 3% inflation bad (It's above the typical 2% target but not alarming; moderate inflation is normal in growing economies); Compare marginal and effective tax rates (The marginal rate applies to the last dollar earned, while the effective rate is total tax divided by total income); Compare health insurance and critical illness insurance (Health insurance pays for medical treatments, while critical illness insurance pays a lump sum if you're diagnosed with a specified serious condition).

summaries.title: Devices and software
summaries.text: The user asked: How do chatbots actually work (They match patterns in your text against learned language models and generate the most likely useful response. Most modern ones use large neural networks trained on huge text corpora rather than hand-written rules); How does SPF protect against email spoofing (SPF allows domain owners to specify which servers are authorized to send email on their behalf, helping receiving servers detect forged sender addresses); Give me three causes of slow Wi-Fi speeds (Common causes are distance or wall obstruction, channel congestion from neighbors, and outdated firmware or an old router. Interference from microwaves and too many devices also contribute); Write a strong random password example (Here's one: v7Kq#mR2xL!p9TzW — 16 characters mixing cases, digits, and symbols); Write a short message asking colleagues to join a video call ("Hi all, please join the video call at 10:00 using the link below. Thanks!"); How do I mark an email as spam in Gmail (Select the email, then click the report spam button (exclamation mark icon) in the toolbar).

summaries.title: Tool runs: tests, disk, files, servers
summaries.text: The user asked: give me a one-liner to run tests and stop at first failure (Use `pytest -x` to stop the test run at the first failure); Show me a git log command with a one-line summary per commit (Run git log --oneline, which prints each commit's short hash and subject line. Add --graph --decorate for branch structure and ref names); What's an MTU and how do I test it (MTU is the largest packet size a link carries without fragmentation. Test with `ping -M do -s 1472 host` and lower the size until it succeeds); How do I check for open ports on a remote host (Use `nmap -p 1-1000 host` for a scan, or `nc -zv host port` for a single port. Only scan systems you're authorized to test); Can deleted files be recovered from sync (Only within the service's trash retention window, often 30 days; after that the deletion propagates everywhere); Quick one: what's a path (A path is the address string showing where a file or folder sits in the directory tree).

summaries.title: Travel questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Check what documents a budget traveler needs for crossing borders in Southeast Asia (Requirements vary by nationality, so verify visa-on-arrival eligibility and passport validity of at least six months for each country); Give me a one-line fact about the Terracotta Army (The Terracotta Army is a collection of thousands of life-size clay soldiers buried to guard the tomb of China's first emperor); Explain the difference between a couchette and a sleeper on European night trains (A couchette is a shared compartment with a bunk bed and minimal bedding, while a sleeper is a private compartment with a real bed, linens, and often a washbasin); Check whether car seats are required in taxis in most countries (Rules vary widely: many countries exempt taxis, but reputable family travel services recommend booking vehicles with child seats in advance); Suggest ways to stay safe during a natural disaster while traveling (Follow local evacuation orders, register with your embassy, keep your phone charged, and store emergency contacts offline); What's the weather like in Korea in October (October in Korea is mild and dry, with highs around 20°C and cool evenings, ideal for sightseeing).

summaries.title: Writing help
summaries.text: The user asked: How do I make 'send me the file now' sound more polite ('Could you please send me the file when you have a moment?' softens the demand while keeping it clear); Explain the difference between 'por' and 'para' in Spanish ('Por' often indicates cause, exchange, or duration, while 'para' indicates purpose, destination, or deadline); Write "good morning" in Italian and tell me if it's formal ("Buongiorno" works for both formal and neutral greetings; "buondì" is more casual); What's the Russian word for 'friend' (The Russian word for 'friend' is 'drug' (друг)); Should I include a photo on my CV (In the US and UK, no—it invites bias concerns. In parts of Europe and Asia it's often expected, so check local norms); Rewrite: 'You're wrong about the deadline.' ('I think there may be a misunderstanding about the deadline — could we double-check it?' keeps it collaborative).

summaries.title: أسئلة متفرقة
summaries.text: سأل المستخدم: وش أحسن بهار للكبسة؟ (دارسين وهيل وليمون أسود وقرنفل، والخلطة تختلف شوي من بيت لبيت.)؛ أبي وصفة شاي بالحليب والزعفران (اغلِ الشاي مع الحليب والسكر، وحط خيوط زعفران قبل التقديم بدقيقة عشان الريحة.)؛ هل أفضل أحط التوفير في حساب منفصل؟ (إيه، حساب منفصل يقلل فرصة إنك تصرفه بدون تفكير، ويخليك تشوف المبلغ يزيد بشكل واضح.)؛ كيف أختار موقع مناسب لمحل صغير؟ (شوف حركة الناس والمواقف وقرب المنافسين والزبائن المستهدفين. الموقع الغالي ما ينفع إذا ما يجيب زبائن.)؛ ليش القهوة التركية تطلع فيها رغوة زيادة؟ (لأنها مطحونة ناعم جدًا وتُغلى على نار هادية، فالرغوة تطلع بسرعة.)؛ كيف أحافظ على زبائني القدامى؟ (تواصل معهم بين فترة وفترة وقدم لهم عروض أو مزايا. الزبون الراضي يرجع ويجيب غيره.)

summaries.title: Programming questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Explain grid-template-areas with a quick example (Name cells in a grid-template-areas block like "header header" then assign items with grid-area: header to place them in those named regions); Explain a same-origin policy violation briefly (A page on one origin trying to read a response from a different scheme, host, or port is blocked, which is why CSRF tricks the browser into sending rather than reading); Can a dictionary have duplicate keys in Python (No, keys must be unique; assigning to an existing key overwrites its value); How to update an object in useState without mutation (Spread the previous object: `setUser(prev => ({...prev, name: 'new'}))`, which creates a new reference React can detect); Can you explain what a self-join is (A self-join joins a table to itself, typically using aliases to compare rows within the same table, such as finding employees who share a manager); Is a graph with no cycles called a tree (Not necessarily; a tree is a connected acyclic graph, while a disconnected acyclic graph is a forest).

summaries.title: Cooking questions
summaries.text: The user asked: How long can cooked rice stay in the fridge before it's unsafe (Cooked rice keeps about 3 to 4 days in the fridge at 40°F or below; reheat it until steaming hot); Can I eat potatoes that turned green (Green skin means solanine has formed; cut away green areas and any sprouts, or discard if a lot is green); Give me three classic French desserts and one line on each (Crème brûlée is a custard with a torched sugar crust, tarte Tatin is an upside-down caramelized apple tart, and profiteroles are choux buns filled with cream and topped with chocolate sauce); Check whether a glass cutting board is a good choice (No—glass is hard on edges and dulls knives quickly; wood or plastic boards are gentler and safer); Compare shawarma and doner kebab (Shawarma typically uses marinated chicken or beef sliced from a vertical spit and served in flatbread, while doner is similar but often served on a plate with rice or bread in Turkish style); Check if this is safe: leaving stew out overnight to cool (No, that's unsafe; food should be refrigerated within two hours to avoid bacterial growth, so chill it promptly in shallow containers).

summaries.title: General knowledge questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Where does 'checkmate' come from (It derives from Persian 'shah mat', meaning 'the king is dead' or 'the king is helpless', via Arabic and Old French); Summarize the studio system era briefly (From the 1920s to the 1950s, major Hollywood studios controlled production, distribution, and exhibition through long-term contracts and owned theater chains); How fast do tornado winds get (The strongest tornadoes can exceed 300 mph, though most peak well below that, typically under 110 mph for weaker ones); What caused the collapse of the Bronze Age civilizations (The Bronze Age collapse around 1200 BCE was likely caused by multiple factors, including invasions, droughts, and internal rebellions); Explain what a false friend is in language learning (It's a word that looks similar across two languages but means something different, like Spanish 'embarazada' meaning pregnant, not embarrassed); Summarize the impact of the transistor in one sentence (The transistor replaced bulky vacuum tubes and made modern computers, phones, and electronics possible).

summaries.title: Health and fitness questions
summaries.text: The user asked: What does sleep deprivation do to the body (It impairs attention and memory, raises stress hormones, and over time increases risks of obesity, diabetes, and cardiovascular disease); When should someone see a doctor for flu symptoms (Seek care for trouble breathing, chest pain, persistent high fever, or worsening after initial improvement); Give me a quick five-move stretching routine for the shoulders (Try arm circles, cross-body pulls, doorway chest openers, overhead reaches, and shoulder shrugs, each for 20 to 30 seconds); Do naps help or hurt (Short naps of 10 to 20 minutes boost alertness without grogginess, but long or late-afternoon naps can make nighttime sleep harder); Why do screens cause eye strain (Prolonged screen use reduces blinking and forces constant focusing, leading to fatigue. This causes dryness and muscle tiredness); Check if this breathing pattern is correct: inhale 5 seconds, exhale 5 seconds (That's correct: equal inhale and exhale at 5 seconds each promotes relaxation and balance).

summaries.title: Hobbies and sport
summaries.text: The user asked: What's the difference between focal length and field of view (Focal length is an optical property of the lens, while field of view is the angular extent it captures, which also depends on sensor size); Which is older, playing cards or chess (Chess is older—it originated in India around the 6th century, while playing cards reached Europe around the 14th century); What's the best knot for tying a hook to braided line (Use a Palomar knot: double the line through the eye, tie a loose overhand, pass the loop over the hook, and wet it before tightening); Recommend a book that explains economics to beginners (*The Undercover Economist* by Tim Harford explains core economic ideas through everyday examples without heavy math); Is a polarizing filter useful for landscapes (Yes, it cuts glare and deepens skies, especially at 90 degrees from the sun. It can't be fully replicated in editing); Write a packing checklist for a two-night canoe camping trip (Pack a dry bag with shelter, sleeping bag, stove and fuel, water filter, headlamp, first aid kit, and food in a hangable sack).

summaries.title: Home and garden questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Write a short care label instruction for a silk blouse (Hand wash cold with mild detergent, do not wring, and dry flat away from direct sunlight); Give me three ideas for a small bedroom (Use a platform bed with under-bed storage, mount lights on the wall, and pick a mirror to bounce daylight); Write a short routine for cleaning a bathroom in under 20 minutes (Spray cleaner on the sink, tub, and toilet, then scrub the toilet while it sits. Wipe surfaces, clean the mirror, and finish with the floor); How do I fix a squeaky door hinge (Remove the hinge pin, wipe it clean, and apply a thin coat of lithium grease or petroleum jelly before refitting); Check this idea: spraying soapy water on plants kills all pests (Insecticidal soap works on soft-bodied pests like aphids and whiteflies but can burn leaves and misses hard-shelled insects. Test on a small area first and avoid direct sun); Why does my drill bit keep wobbling (Usually the bit isn't seated fully in the chuck or the chuck jaws are worn; reseat it and tighten all three jaws evenly).

summaries.title: Learning and study
summaries.text: The user asked: What's the Cornell note-taking method (It divides a page into cues, notes, and a summary column. You write notes on the right, key questions on the left, and summarize at the bottom); Give me a quick template for meeting notes (Use four headings: Attendees, Decisions, Action items with owners, and Open questions; fill each during the meeting rather than afterward); Write a two-line summary of the forgetting curve (Memory decays rapidly after learning unless reviewed. Each well-timed review flattens the curve and slows future forgetting); Suggest a game to practice letter sounds (Try a sound hunt: call out a sound and have the child find objects around the room starting with that sound).

summaries.title: Money questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Convert 250 US dollars into British pounds (At about 0.79 pounds per dollar, that's roughly 198 British pounds); What's the difference between secured and unsecured loans (A secured loan is backed by collateral like a car, while an unsecured loan relies only on the borrower's creditworthiness); Is tax avoidance legal (Yes, tax avoidance is legal use of tax rules to minimize liability, unlike evasion which is illegal); Explain the difference between coinsurance and copay (Coinsurance is a percentage of costs you pay after meeting a deductible, while a copay is a fixed amount you pay for a specific service); Explain the pay-yourself-first method briefly (You transfer savings and investments immediately when income arrives, then budget the remainder for spending); Rewrite this plainly: the loan carries a 5.2% nominal rate compounded monthly (The loan charges 5.2% a year, with interest added each month).

summaries.title: Devices and software
summaries.text: The user asked: Explain how a large language model works, simply (It predicts the next token from patterns learned across huge text datasets, building sentences one piece at a time); Why are password managers recommended (They generate and store unique strong passwords for every account, so you only need to remember one master passphrase and avoid reuse); How can I blur my background in Google Meet (Before joining, click the effects icon in the preview and choose Blur or a virtual background. During a call, open the three-dot menu and select Apply visual effects); Why did my call drop when I walked to another room (Switching rooms likely moved the device to a weaker Wi-Fi signal or a different network. Staying near the router or using a wired connection prevents most drops); Give an example of a use case for archive storage (Storing old legal documents or historical records that must be retained but are rarely accessed is a typical archive storage use case); How much does it roughly cost per page to print in black and white (Inkjet black-and-white runs about 3 to 5 cents per page, while laser toner typically costs 1 to 2 cents per page).

summaries.title: Tool runs: tests, disk, files, servers
summaries.text: The user asked: What's the best way to check if a website is down for everyone or just me (Use a third-party service like Down For Everyone Or Just Me or check via an external monitoring tool like UptimeRobot); What happens when a file is moved to the recycle bin (It's held temporarily and can be restored until the bin is emptied, at which point space is freed); Write a one-line command to check if a host is reachable (`ping -c 4 host` sends four echo requests and reports loss and latency. On Windows use `ping -n 4 host`); Why do some calendar invites show tentative status (Tentative status means an invitee hasn't confirmed attendance, so the event appears with a distinct marker until they accept or decline); Explain why a build might pass locally but fail in CI (Common causes include different dependency versions, missing environment variables, case-sensitive file paths, or timing differences in CI); List common reasons a service fails to start after reboot (Common reasons include the service not being enabled, missing dependencies, incorrect permissions, or configuration errors; check systemctl status <service> and logs in /var/log).

summaries.title: Travel questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Does flying east or west cause worse jet lag (Flying east typically causes worse jet lag because it requires advancing your body clock, which is harder than delaying it); What's the liquid limit for carry-on bags on flights within the EU (Containers must hold no more than 100 ml each, and they all need to fit in one transparent resealable bag of about 1 litre); Give me three tips for sleeping well on an overnight train (Book a lower bunk, bring earplugs and an eye mask, and pack a small pillow or neck support for the seated options); Check whether a 24-inch suitcase typically fits carry-on rules (Usually no—24-inch cases often exceed the 22-inch height limit for carry-on. They generally need to be checked unless the airline allows larger cabin bags); Compare the Japan Rail Pass and buying individual Shinkansen tickets (The Pass pays off mainly on long multi-city routes; point-to-point tickets are cheaper for a single Tokyo–Kyoto–Osaka loop); What's the difference between black diamond and double black diamond ski runs (Black diamond runs are steep and difficult, while double black diamonds are extreme, often ungroomed, and may include cliffs or mandatory air).

summaries.title: Writing help
summaries.text: The user asked: Fix the punctuation: I bought apples oranges and bananas (Add commas to separate the items: 'I bought apples, oranges, and bananas.'); What makes a haiku different from other short poems (Haiku usually has three lines in a 5-7-5 syllable pattern and focuses on a single moment in nature, often with a seasonal word); What are the counterarguments mentioned in this piece (Critics argue the policy raises compliance costs for small firms and that the projected savings rely on optimistic assumptions about adoption rates); Compare chronological and functional CV formats (Chronological lists roles in reverse date order and is easiest for recruiters to follow; functional groups skills and hides dates, which can raise suspicion. Use functional only for career changers with sparse recent history); Explain the argument in this op-ed briefly (The author contends that congestion pricing works only if transit alternatives are in place before the charge begins); Create a title for a guide about gardening for beginners ('The Beginner's Guide to Gardening: Grow Your First Garden with Confidence' is inviting and clear).

summaries.title: أسئلة متفرقة
summaries.text: سأل المستخدم: منو أشهر شاعر عربي في العصر العباسي؟ (المتنبي يعتبر الأشهر، وبعده أبو نواس وأبو تمام.)؛ شلون أجهز سفرة إفطار بسيطة؟ (ابدأ بالتمر والماء والشوربة، وزيد مقبلات خفيفة وسلطة، ويكفي للأهل.)؛ هل بكرة بيتغير الطقس؟ (متوقع انخفاض بسيط في الحرارة مع رياح شمالية خفيفة.)؛ أبي صيغة إيميل اعتذار عن تأخير الرد (اكتب: أعتذر عن تأخري بالرد، وكان عندي ظرف، وشاكر لك تفهمك.)؛ اذكر لي مهرجانات سياحية في السعودية هذا الشتاء (فيه مهرجان شتاء طنطورة في العلا وموسم الرياض، وتقدر تتأكد من مواعيدها الرسمية.)؛ منو فاز بكأس العالم آخر مرة؟ (الأرجنتين فازت على فرنسا بالركلات الترجيحيه في نهائي ٢٠٢٢.)

summaries.title: Programming questions
summaries.text: The user asked: What's the difference between best, average, and worst case (Best case is the minimum work over inputs, worst case the maximum, and average case the expected work over an input distribution); Quick: what's the time complexity of inserting into a balanced BST (Insertion into a balanced binary search tree takes O(log n) time in the worst case); Write a parameterized query example for Python and SQLite (Use cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?", (user_id,)) so the value is bound, never concatenated into the SQL string); Which isolation level prevents non-repeatable reads but allows phantoms (Repeatable Read prevents non-repeatable reads but typically still allows phantom reads); What error does this cause: two mutable borrows of the same value at once (It fails with E0499: you cannot have more than one mutable borrow of a value in the same scope); Write a JSON error response body for a 422 validation failure (Something like {"error":"validation_failed","fields":{"email":"invalid format"}} conveys the problem clearly).

summaries.title: Cooking questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Check whether canned beans need to be cooked before eating (No, canned beans are already cooked and safe to eat cold or warmed through); What's a quick breakfast I could make in under five minutes (Scrambled eggs on toast takes about four minutes, or Greek yogurt with granola and honey is even faster); Which has more sugar, milk chocolate or white chocolate (White chocolate typically has more sugar by weight, since it contains no cocoa solids and is mostly cocoa butter, sugar, and milk); Is it safe to refreeze thawed chicken (Yes, if it was thawed in the fridge, but quality drops and it should be cooked before refreezing); How long should I simmer a chicken curry (Simmer gently for about 20 to 30 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and tender. Longer simmering deepens the flavor but can dry out lean cuts); Write a short recipe for aglio e olio (Sauté sliced garlic in olive oil, toss with cooked spaghetti, and finish with parsley and red pepper flakes).

summaries.title: General knowledge questions
summaries.text: The user asked: How fast can a cheetah run (Cheetahs can reach about 60–70 mph in short sprints, usually lasting only 20–30 seconds); Give me one everyday example of resonance (Pushing a swing at just its natural rhythm builds large motion, which is resonance matching your pushes to its frequency); Quick one: who played Ilsa in Casablanca (Ingrid Bergman played Ilsa Lund in Casablanca); How many squares are on a standard chessboard counting all sizes (There are 204 squares: 64 of size 1, 49 of size 2, and so on down to 1 of size 8); How many novels did Jane Austen publish in her lifetime (Six novels were published, four of them anonymously during her lifetime); Explain the French New Wave in two sentences (It was a late-1950s French movement of young critics-turned-directors like Godard and Truffaut who shot on location with lightweight cameras. They favored personal style and jump cuts over polished studio continuity).

summaries.title: Health and fitness questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Is a multivitamin necessary for most adults (No—most adults meeting dietary needs don't require one, though specific groups may benefit); Describe how to help a person in shock (Lay them down, raise their legs if no injury prevents it, keep them warm, and call for emergency help); How do you help someone with heatstroke (Move them to a cool place, remove excess clothing, cool them with water and fanning, and call emergency services immediately); Can you explain the role of electrolytes in hydration (Electrolytes like sodium and potassium help balance fluids and maintain nerve and muscle function); Write a short warm-up routine before a tempo run (Jog 10 minutes easy, then do 4 x 20-second strides with full recovery. Finish with a minute of easy jogging before starting the tempo); Compare CPR for adults and infants (Adults get two-handed compressions at the nipple line; infants get two fingers just below the nipple line, both at 100–120 per minute).

summaries.title: Hobbies and sport
summaries.text: The user asked: How is blackjack scored (Number cards count face value, face cards count 10, and aces count 1 or 11; the goal is to get as close to 21 as possible without going over); Check this: if a defender passes the ball back to the goalkeeper and the keeper picks it up, is that a foul (Yes, if the goalkeeper handles a deliberate back-pass from a teammate's foot, the opposing team gets an indirect free kick); Explain the difference between SSDs and HDDs for game loading times (SSDs load games much faster because they have no moving parts, while HDDs are slower due to mechanical read heads); How do I listen to audiobooks for free (Many public libraries offer free audiobook loans through apps like Libby or Hoopla. You can also find free public-domain audiobooks on LibriVox); What are the rules for castling in chess (Castling involves the king and a rook moving simultaneously: the king moves two squares toward the rook, and the rook jumps to the square the king crossed. It's only allowed if neither piece has moved, the king isn't in check, and the squares between them are empty and not under attack); What is the circle of fifths (It's a diagram showing the relationship between keys, helping with chord progressions and key signatures).

summaries.title: Home and garden questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Why do towels get scratchy over time (Detergent residue and fabric softener buildup stiffen the loops, so wash with less detergent and skip softener); What is biophilic design (Biophilic design brings natural elements like plants, daylight, wood, and water features into interiors to support wellbeing); When should I repot a rootbound plant (Repot when roots circle the pot or grow out the drainage holes, ideally in spring just before active growth begins); Can you check if this is the right screw for wood (I can't see the screw, but for wood you want coarse threads and a smooth shank. Drywall screws are too brittle for structural wood joints); Give me a quick way to declutter before packing (Sort each room into keep, donate, sell, and discard piles, and be ruthless about duplicates. Clearing before packing reduces volume, cost, and unpacking time); Is vinegar a real ant deterrent (Vinegar wipes out the pheromone trails ants follow, so it disrupts routes temporarily. It doesn't kill colonies, so pair it with bait for lasting control).

summaries.title: Learning and study
summaries.text: The user asked: Give a one-week plan for memorizing vocabulary (Review new words daily with recall, then at days 3, 7, and 14, mixing old and new words each session); What are some good ways to take notes from a textbook (Use the Cornell method: split the page into notes, cues, and a summary. Paraphrase in your own words rather than copying sentences); How do I stop procrastinating before a big test (Start with a tiny task, like opening your notes for two minutes. Momentum usually carries you into real work); What are decodable books (Decodable books use words that follow the phonics patterns a child has already learned, so they can sound out most words); Explain the difference between Spanish 'ser' and 'estar' ('Ser' covers identity and inherent traits, while 'estar' covers states, locations, and conditions. So 'es alto' means tall by nature, but 'está cansado' means currently tired); Compare cramming and spaced study (Cramming helps short-term recall but fades fast. Spaced study distributes reviews over days and produces much stronger long-term retention).

summaries.title: Money questions
summaries.text: The user asked: What is the bid-ask spread in forex (It's the gap between the price at which a dealer buys and sells a currency, and it's how dealers earn their margin); Check whether a total market index fund includes small companies (Yes, a total market index fund typically includes large, mid, and small-cap companies weighted by market value); How should irregular income be budgeted (Base the budget on the lowest expected monthly income and route surplus months into a buffer fund that covers shortfalls); Is the 70/20/10 rule good (It allocates 70% to living costs, 20% to savings, and 10% to debt or giving; it's flexible but light on debt repayment); Check whether the Australian dollar is rising against the yen (It has been edging higher, with one Australian dollar buying around 97 yen recently); Does inflation hurt everyone equally (No, it tends to hit lower-income households and those on fixed incomes hardest, while borrowers may benefit).

summaries.title: Devices and software
summaries.text: The user asked: What's the difference between an AI assistant and a chatbot (A chatbot usually handles narrow scripted conversations, while an AI assistant can reason across many topics and tasks. The line is blurry because modern chatbots increasingly use general AI models); My scans look completely black, what's likely wrong (Usually the lamp or exposure settings are at fault; check that the scanner lid is closed and the brightness setting isn't set too low); Compare COUNT and COUNTA briefly (COUNT counts only numeric cells, while COUNTA counts every non-empty cell, including text); What is cloud storage, exactly (It's data kept on remote servers you reach over the internet, rather than on your own device. Providers like AWS, Google, and Dropbox manage the hardware); What should I do first if a password gets exposed in a breach (Change that password immediately, and change it anywhere else it was reused, then enable 2FA on those accounts); Explain tokenization simply (Tokenization splits text into small chunks, often words or word pieces, that a model processes as numbers. "Unbelievable" might become "un" + "believ" + "able.").

summaries.title: Tool runs: tests, disk, files, servers
summaries.text: The user asked: Why does my test suite pass locally but fail in CI (Common causes are different OS or dependency versions, timezone settings, and tests that depend on files or services not present in CI); Name the parts of a calendar event (A typical event includes a title, start and end time, time zone, location, attendees, description, and recurrence settings); Set a one-time alert for two hours from now (I can't access your device's reminder app, but the alert should be set for two hours from the current time); Suggest a way to automate service checks across multiple servers (Use a configuration management tool like Ansible to run health check scripts across all servers, or set up a monitoring system like Zabbix with agents on each host); What does git status actually show (It shows the working tree state: staged changes, unstaged modifications, and untracked files. It also names the current branch and any upstream divergence); Is high cached memory a problem (No, cached memory is reclaimable file cache and generally good. Only worry if 'available' memory is low and swap usage is climbing).

summaries.title: Travel questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Write a one-sentence plaque label for Stonehenge ("A Neolithic circle of sarsen and bluestone megaliths raised around 2500 BCE, aligned to the solstices."); Check whether travel insurance covers pandemics (Many policies exclude pandemics, though some newer plans include limited medical coverage; read the exclusions section carefully); Check whether Rocky Mountain National Park requires timed-entry permits (Yes, RMNP has used timed-entry permits in recent summer seasons, so verify current rules on the NPS site before going); What's the best way to get from Tokyo to Kyoto (The Shinkansen takes about 2 hours 15 minutes; the Nozomi is fastest); How heavy can a checked bag be before airlines charge extra (On most major airlines the free limit is 23 kg per checked bag; beyond that overweight fees usually apply); What's the oldest museum still open to the public (The Capitoline Museums in Rome, founded in 1471 when Pope Sixtus IV donated bronze statues to the city).

summaries.title: Writing help
summaries.text: The user asked: Write a one-line toast for a team celebration ("To the late nights, the wins, and the people who made them happen. Cheers."); Can you check if "Ich habe Hunger" is correct German (Yes, it's correct and means "I am hungry," literally "I have hunger."); Should I write 'alot' or 'a lot' (Always write "a lot" as two words; "alot" is not standard English. It means a large amount or very much); Give a headline for a product launch of a smartwatch ('Introducing the Ultimate Smartwatch: Style, Health Tracking, and Connectivity on Your Wrist' highlights key features); Check this headline for grammar: 'Company announce new product line' (It should be 'Company announces new product line' — the singular subject takes a singular verb).

summaries.title: أسئلة متفرقة
summaries.text: سأل المستخدم: شنو يعني الذاكرة العشوائية RAM؟ (هي الذاكرة اللي تساعد الجوال يشتغل بسلاسة مع التطبيقات المفتوحة، كل ما زادت كان أفضل.)؛ شنو أحسن نوع شاحن باور بانك؟ (اختار Anker أو Baseus بسعة 10000-20000 مللي أمبير ودعم شحن سريع، وتأكد من شهادة الأمان.)؛ وش أول معلقة من المعلقات السبع؟ (المعلقة الأولى لامرئ القيس، ومطلعها: "قفا نبكِ من ذكرى حبيبٍ ومنزلِ".)؛ شنو معنى كلمة استفهام في النحو؟ (الاستفهام أسلوب تسأل به، مثل: وين رايح؟ وليش تأخرت؟)؛ وش الفرق بين التمرين الهوائي واللاهوائي؟ (الهوائي زي المشي والجري للقلب، واللاهوائي زي الحديد للعضلات والقوة.)؛ شكثر مدة الشوط الواحد؟ (أربعين وخمس دقايق، مع وقت بدل ضايع يزيد حسب التوقفات.)

summaries.title: Programming questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Compare \w and [a-zA-Z0-9_] (They're equivalent in most flavors, though \w may also include Unicode letters depending on settings); How do I find rows in one table not present in another (Use a LEFT JOIN with a NULL check or a NOT EXISTS subquery, e.g., SELECT * FROM A LEFT JOIN B ON A.id = B.a_id WHERE B.a_id IS NULL;); What does useMemo actually do (useMemo caches a computed value between renders and recomputes only when its dependencies change, avoiding expensive recalculation); What does a flame graph actually show (It shows sampled stack traces where width represents time spent, so wide frames indicate functions consuming the most CPU); What's the risk of rebasing a shared branch (It rewrites commit hashes, which breaks other people's clones and can cause duplicated or lost work for anyone who based commits on it); Write a bash one-liner to track a process's memory over time (`while true; do ps -o rss= -p $PID; sleep 5; done` logs RSS every five seconds. Plot it to see upward trends against workload markers).

summaries.title: Cooking questions
summaries.text: The user asked: What can replace fresh herbs in a fast recipe (Dried herbs work at about one-third the amount, or use a pinch of dried oregano or basil); Explain the difference between meal prep and batch cooking (Meal prep portions complete meals in advance; batch cooking makes large quantities of components to combine later); Which knife should I use to cut a loaf of crusty bread (A serrated bread knife, ideally 8–10 inches long. The serrations saw through hard crust without crushing the soft interior); Give me a 15-minute pasta recipe (Cook spaghetti while you sauté garlic in olive oil, then toss with grated Parmesan and black pepper. Reserve a splash of pasta water to loosen the sauce); How do you make fresh pasta dough (Mix 00 flour and eggs (about 100g flour per egg), knead until smooth, and rest before rolling); How do I know when dough has proofed enough (Poke it gently with a floured finger: a slow, partial spring-back means it's ready, while an immediate full rebound means underproofed. Very slack, deflating dough is overproofed).

summaries.title: General knowledge questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Give me three threats to sea turtles (Plastic ingestion, fishing nets, and loss of nesting beaches are major threats); Name one problem with the design argument (It infers a designer from apparent purpose, but apparent design can arise from natural selection without any intentional designer); When did jazz originate (Jazz emerged in New Orleans in the early 20th century, around 1900-1920, blending blues, ragtime, and brass band traditions); Tell me about the Rosetta Stone (It is a 196 BCE decree inscribed in hieroglyphs, demotic, and Greek, whose discovery in 1799 allowed Champollion to decipher Egyptian hieroglyphs); Give me an example of a syllogism (All mammals are warm-blooded; all dogs are mammals; therefore all dogs are warm-blooded); What's the principle of sufficient reason (It holds that everything that exists or happens has a reason or cause explaining why it is so rather than otherwise).

summaries.title: Health and fitness questions
summaries.text: The user asked: What to do for a seizure (Keep the area clear, cushion the head, don't restrain the person or put anything in their mouth, and time the seizure); How do I know if it's a cold or allergies (Allergies cause itchy eyes and clear mucus without fever, while colds often bring fever and body aches); Does vitamin C prevent colds (Regular vitamin C doesn't prevent colds in most people, though it may slightly shorten one); What's the 4-7-8 breathing technique (The 4-7-8 technique involves inhaling for 4 seconds, holding for 7, and exhaling for 8, which promotes relaxation); Check this claim: do we need eight hours exactly (No, eight hours is a rough average; individual needs vary, and quality and consistency matter more than hitting an exact number); What's the difference between threshold and VO2 max intervals (Threshold intervals are longer (e.g., 10–20 min) at a hard but sustainable pace, while VO2 max intervals are shorter (3–5 min) at near-maximal effort).

summaries.title: Hobbies and sport
summaries.text: The user asked: Which tennis shot is used to return a lob over the opponent's head (That's an overhead smash, hit downward with a serving-like motion to put the lob away); How do I stop knitted edges from curling (Add a border of garter stitch, seed stitch, or ribbing along the edges. Blocking finished pieces also helps relax the curl); How should a rook be placed in the middlegame (Put rooks on open or semi-open files and behind passed pawns, where they exert the most pressure); Write a short caption for a photo of fog over a lake ("Morning held its breath over the water." It fits the quiet, low-contrast mood of fog); Write a short explanation of how penalty shootouts work (Each team takes five penalties alternately, and the team with more goals after five rounds wins. If still tied, it goes to sudden death, one kick each until one team scores and the other misses); Explain the shot clock rule in basketball (A team must attempt a shot that hits the rim within 24 seconds (NBA) or 30 seconds (college) of gaining possession, or it loses the ball).

summaries.title: Home and garden questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Why do cockroaches keep showing up in the kitchen at night (Cockroaches are nocturnal and seek moisture and food crumbs, so sealing cracks and storing food tightly discourages them); Turn this into a short checklist: draught-proofing a room (Check doors, windows, skirting boards, and letterboxes. Seal gaps with brushes, foam strips, or caulk where appropriate); Is it cheaper to move midweek or on a weekend (Midweek moves are usually cheaper because demand is lower. Fridays and month-ends are the most expensive and hardest slots to book); How do I get coffee stains out of a white cotton shirt (Blot the stain, then soak it in cold water with a little dish soap before washing. Avoid hot water, which can set the stain); Is a sectional good for a narrow room (A sectional can work in a narrow room if it's a small L-shape placed along the walls, but avoid deep sectionals that block traffic flow); Why do towels get stiff after washing (Stiff towels often result from detergent buildup or hard water minerals; washing with less detergent and adding vinegar to the rinse can soften them).

summaries.title: Learning and study
