summaries.text: The user asked: Is it bad to read the same book over and over (No, repeated reading builds fluency and confidence, so it is genuinely useful for young readers); What's the best way to memorize the periodic table (Group elements by family and practice with spaced repetition; mnemonics for the first 20 help too); Is highlighting a good study method (It's usually weak on its own; it marks content but doesn't force retrieval, so pair it with self-quizzing); Explain spaced repetition in one sentence (Spaced repetition is reviewing material at gradually increasing intervals so each review happens just before you'd forget it); Write a one-line description of a data analytics certificate for a portfolio (Completed a data analytics certificate covering SQL, spreadsheets, and dashboard building with a capstone project); What's a good way to take notes that actually help memory (Use question-and-answer or Cornell-style notes: record key ideas as prompts you can quiz yourself on later. Notes become study material rather than a transcript).

summaries.title: Money questions
summaries.text: The user asked: What's the difference between term life and whole life insurance (Term life covers a fixed period and pays only if death occurs within it; whole life lasts a lifetime and builds cash value); Why do exchange rates change so often (Rates shift with supply and demand, driven by interest rates, inflation, trade flows and market expectations); Should emergency funds be invested in the stock market (Generally no—stocks can drop sharply, and emergency money should stay stable and accessible); Why do governments levy taxes (Governments levy taxes to fund public services such as infrastructure, defense, education, and healthcare); Write a short invoice reminder email for an overdue payment (Subject: Friendly reminder, invoice [#] due [date]. Body: Just following up on invoice [#] for [amount], now past due. Please confirm payment status or let us know if you need a copy); Give an example of a hard currency (The US dollar and Swiss franc are classic hard currencies, widely held and stable).

summaries.title: Devices and software
summaries.text: The user asked: Should I reboot my router regularly (Occasional reboots, such as monthly or after firmware updates, can clear memory issues, but frequent reboots usually signal a deeper problem); How do I count how many cells contain text (Use =COUNTIF(A1:A100,"*"), which counts non-empty text cells in the range); Why do spam emails often have weird spelling (Filters match common words, so spammers misspell them to slip through. The garbled text also tricks readers into opening the message out of curiosity); How do I mute everyone in a call (As host, open the Participants panel and choose Mute All. You can allow attendees to unmute themselves if needed); Is it worth upgrading to Wi-Fi 6E (It helps if you have many devices or congested airwaves and clients that support 6 GHz. Otherwise Wi-Fi 6 gear often delivers most of the benefit for less money); What does DKIM do (DKIM adds a digital signature to emails, allowing receiving servers to verify that the message was sent by the claimed domain and hasn't been altered).

summaries.title: Tool runs: tests, disk, files, servers
summaries.text: The user asked: Why do some folders show a lock icon (A lock icon usually indicates restricted permissions, meaning only certain users or accounts can access that folder); Write a short checklist for setting up backups on a laptop (Pick what to protect, choose two destinations (one offsite), schedule automatic runs, encrypt the copies, and test a restore quarterly); How can I see which files changed in the last commit (Use `git show --stat HEAD` for a summary or `git show --name-only HEAD` for just filenames); Write a script to check multiple servers' ping times (Use a loop: for host in server1 server2; do ping -c 1 $host | grep 'time='; done); What does HTTP 503 mean (HTTP 503 means Service Unavailable, indicating the server is temporarily unable to handle the request, often due to overload or maintenance).

summaries.title: Travel questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Why do flights from Europe to the US take longer than the return trip (Jet streams blow west-to-east, so eastbound flights get a tailwind boost while westbound flights fight headwinds); How long does the drive from Amman to Petra take (The drive is roughly 3 to 3.5 hours via the Desert Highway); Are hostel reviews reliable (Read recent reviews and look for patterns about cleanliness and noise rather than one-off complaints); Which is easier to navigate without Japanese: Tokyo or Seoul without Korean (Seoul is generally easier due to Hangul signage and widespread English on transit, though Tokyo's rail signage is also strong); Is tap water safe to drink in Korea (Yes, tap water in South Korea is generally safe to drink, though many locals prefer filtered or bottled water); Does deodorant count as a liquid at security (Yes, spray and gel deodorants count as liquids and must follow the 100 ml container rule).

summaries.title: Writing help
summaries.text: The user asked: Make this friendlier: 'Attend the meeting or send a delegate.' ('If you're unable to attend, feel free to send someone in your place' sounds more accommodating); How do I make this sound less aggressive: 'Send the report now' (Try 'Could you please send the report as soon as possible?' — the modal and 'please' soften the demand); Give me a tagline under five words for a meditation app ("Pause. Breathe. Begin."); Can you check this caption for typos: 'Your gonna love this new flavor' (Yes, it should be 'You're gonna love this new flavor' since 'your' is possessive); How long should a social media caption be (Aim for under 125 characters for punchy posts, or 138 to 150 characters before Instagram truncates with 'more.'); Quick idea: a detective who can only solve cold cases (Their gift works through decay, so fresh evidence reads as noise; they must wait for a case to age before the truth sharpens).

summaries.title: أسئلة متفرقة
summaries.text: سأل المستخدم: كيف أفرمت الآيفون بدون ما أفقد الصور؟ (سوِّ نسخة احتياطية على iCloud أو الكمبيوتر قبل الفرمتة، وبعدها تقدر ترجع الصور بسهولة.)؛ كيف أسوي لقيمات مقرمشة؟ (خلّي العجينة ترتاح زين وحط الزعفران والهيل، واقليها بزيت حار وقلّبها بسرعة.)؛ عطني معلومة عن نادي ريال مدريد. (هو الأكثر تتويجاً بدوري أبطال أوروبا، ومقره في إسبانيا.)؛ ليش نرفع الفاعل وننصب المفعول؟ (هذا نظام العربية الأصلي، الفاعل دايم مرفوع والمفعول منصوب عشان تعرف من يسوي الفعل ومن يتأثر فيه.)؛ هل يحتاج جوازي فيزا عشان أروح جورجيا؟ (لا، مواطني الخليج ما يحتاجون فيزا لجورجيا ويقدرون يدخلون بدونها.)؛ أعطني أسئلة تدريبية عن موضوع معين. (قول لي الموضوع وأنا أجهز لك أسئلة متنوعة بمستويات صعوبة مختلفة.)

summaries.title: Programming questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Compare `String` and `&str` briefly (`String` is an owned, growable heap buffer; `&str` is a borrowed view into UTF-8 bytes owned elsewhere); How do I reset all state when a prop changes (Give the component a key prop tied to the value so React remounts it, or store the previous prop and reset state in render or an effect); How do I match a literal dot (Escape it with a backslash: \); Why is the event loop important for non-blocking I/O (The event loop allows I/O operations to run asynchronously, so the main thread isn't blocked, improving performance and responsiveness); What's the difference between \b and \B (\b matches a word boundary, while \B matches a position that is not a word boundary); How to remove duplicate rows from a table (Use a CTE with ROW_NUMBER() partitioned by the duplicate columns and delete rows where the row number is greater than 1).

summaries.title: Cooking questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Give me three classic French desserts (Crème brûlée, tarte Tatin, and profiteroles are three well-known ones); Compare gelato and ice cream (Gelato uses more milk and less cream, is churned slower with less air, and is served warmer, making it denser and softer than ice cream); Fast dinner ideas using only pantry staples (Lentil soup, pasta with garlic and olive oil, or rice and beans all work from shelf-stable basics); What's the main ingredient in mutabbal (The main ingredient in mutabbal is roasted eggplant, mixed with tahini, yogurt, lemon, and garlic); Quick check: is chocolate toxic to dogs (Yes, chocolate contains theobromine, which dogs cannot metabolize well, and dark chocolate is the most dangerous per ounce); How long is deli meat good after opening (Refrigerated deli meat keeps about 3–5 days after opening).

summaries.title: General knowledge questions
summaries.text: The user asked: What's the difference between an atom and a molecule (An atom is a single element's smallest unit, while a molecule is two or more atoms bonded together); Quick one: what makes blood red (Hemoglobin, the oxygen-carrying protein in red blood cells, contains iron that gives blood its red color); Find the flaw: all horses are the same color, proved by induction (The base case n=1 holds, but the inductive step from 1 to 2 fails because the overlapping group of one horse is empty); What does 'a priori' mean (A priori knowledge is justified independently of experience, as in mathematics or pure logic); How did the Bronze Age collapse happen (Around 1200 BCE, invasions by Sea Peoples, drought, earthquakes, and collapsing trade networks brought down several eastern Mediterranean kingdoms within a few decades); Does dissolving sugar in water create a new substance (No, it's a physical change; the sugar molecules disperse but remain chemically unchanged).

summaries.title: Health and fitness questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Compare vitamin D2 and D3 (D3 raises blood levels more effectively than D2, though both can prevent deficiency); Best way to prevent knee pain from running (Build mileage gradually, strengthen hips and glutes, and replace worn shoes. If pain persists, reduce load and consult a professional); Write a short reminder I can post at my desk about blinking ("Blink often, look far away, and rest your eyes every 20 minutes." Keep it at eye level so it's easy to see); How much pressure for a nosebleed (Pinch the soft part of the nose firmly and lean forward for 10-15 minutes without checking); Give me three tips for jet lag (Shift bedtime gradually before travel, get bright morning light at the destination, and avoid alcohol on the flight; light exposure matters more than melatonin).

summaries.title: Hobbies and sport
summaries.text: The user asked: Is the Switch 2 backward compatible (Nintendo confirmed the Switch 2 plays physical and digital Switch games, though some titles may have compatibility caveats); How do I spot a fork tactic (Look for enemy pieces lined up on knight-reachable squares or on the same rank, file, or diagonal, especially when your knight is near their king and queen); Compare digital and acoustic pianos for a beginner (Digital pianos offer volume control, headphone practice, and stable tuning; acoustic pianos give richer resonance and touch response but need tuning and space); How can I prevent my sewing machine from skipping stitches (Change the needle, rethread the machine, and check the tension and bobbin to ensure proper stitch formation); What is the goal of the game Catan (The goal of Catan is to be the first player to reach 10 victory points by building settlements, cities, and roads, and by achieving certain bonuses); Compare castling kingside vs queenside (Kingside castling is safer and faster, while queenside castling creates a more aggressive setup but leaves the king nearer the center).

summaries.title: Home and garden questions
summaries.text: The user asked: What does the triangle symbol on a care tag mean (A triangle means bleaching is allowed; a crossed triangle means do not bleach); What's the best way to patch a hole in drywall (Use a self-adhesive mesh patch, cover with joint compound, and sand smooth after drying. For larger holes, cut a plug from scrap drywall); How should I wash a down jacket (Wash it on a gentle cycle with a down-specific detergent, then tumble dry low with clean tennis balls to restore loft); How do I declutter a closet in one afternoon (Work in four passes: trash, donate, relocate, and keep. Empty one shelf at a time so the space stays usable); Best way to remove a stripped screw (Try a rubber band between bit and head, or cut a slot with a rotary tool and use a flathead; as a last resort drill it out); What's the fastest way to clean burnt food off a pan (Simmer water with baking soda in the pan for ten minutes, then scrape with a wooden spoon. Most burnt residue will lift easily).

summaries.title: Learning and study
summaries.text: The user asked: Fix this sentence: 'Yo soy muy hambre.' (It should be 'Tengo mucha hambre' — hunger uses 'tener' in Spanish, not 'ser'); Explain the Feynman technique for notes (Write the concept as if teaching it to a beginner, identify gaps, then simplify and use analogies. This deepens understanding); Why do some kids struggle with reading (Difficulties can come from phonological awareness gaps, decoding issues, language delay, or vision and attention factors, so targeted assessment helps); Suggest a color-coding scheme for handwritten notes (Use one color for headings, one for key terms, one for examples, and one for questions to self; limit it to four so the page stays readable).

summaries.title: Money questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Give me three reasons to hold bonds (Bonds provide steady income, reduce overall portfolio volatility, and often cushion losses when stocks fall); Explain bonds to a beginner (A bond is a loan to a government or company that pays interest over time and returns the principal at maturity); How do central banks target inflation (They set a target, often 2%, and adjust interest rates and money supply to steer actual inflation toward it); Name three factors that affect currency supply and demand (Interest rates, inflation and trade balances are three major drivers of currency supply and demand); Why do central banks raising rates make loans more expensive (Higher central bank rates raise lenders' funding costs, which they pass on as higher rates to borrowers); What is an insurance deductible (A deductible is the amount you pay out of pocket before your insurance coverage begins to pay for a claim).

summaries.title: Devices and software
summaries.text: The user asked: How do I split 'John Smith' into first and last name (Use =LEFT(A1,FIND(" ",A1)-1) for the first name and =MID(A1,FIND(" ",A1)+1,99) for the last); Write a two-line rule for filtering newsletters ("If the List-Unsubscribe header exists and the sender is not in contacts, move to Newsletters." That keeps bulk mail out of the main inbox while preserving it for later reading); Explain how Bayesian spam filtering works (Bayesian filtering analyzes the words and patterns in emails, comparing them to known spam and legitimate emails, and assigns a probability score to classify new messages); Write a short checklist for securing a home router (Change the admin password, update firmware, use WPA2/WPA3, disable WPS and remote admin, and set a strong Wi-Fi password. Optionally create a guest network for visitors and IoT devices); What is the difference between cloud storage and cloud backup (Cloud storage is for active file access and collaboration, while cloud backup is for preserving data copies for recovery. Backup often includes versioning and retention policies); Check this: is 1366x768 a common laptop resolution (Yes, 1366x768 is a very common budget laptop resolution, also called HD).

summaries.title: Tool runs: tests, disk, files, servers
summaries.text: The user asked: what's a flaky test (A flaky test passes or fails inconsistently on the same code, often due to timing, randomness, or shared state); How do I verify DNS resolution for a domain (Use dig example.com or nslookup example.com to query DNS records and verify resolution); How can I debug a test that fails only sometimes (Log timestamps and random seeds, run it repeatedly in a loop, and isolate shared state or async timing that may cause the inconsistency); How do I test a restore without risking live data (Restore into an isolated folder or spare drive, verify checksums and file counts, and only then consider replacing the originals); What does the load average number actually measure (It's the average number of processes runnable or waiting on I/O over 1, 5, and 15 minutes. It counts demand, not CPU percentage, so a 4 on 4 cores means full saturation); Write a short shell command to clean and rebuild a Maven project (Run `mvn clean install` to clean previous outputs and rebuild the project with tests).

summaries.title: Travel questions
summaries.text: The user asked: Can you explain the difference between a tram and a light rail (Trams usually run on streets with traffic, while light rail operates on dedicated tracks and has higher capacity and speeds); Give me a quick list of must-see sights in Rome (The Colosseum, Vatican Museums, Pantheon, Trevi Fountain, and Roman Forum are the top essentials); Explain the 3-2-1 rule for jet lag (The 3-2-1 rule suggests avoiding caffeine 3 hours before bedtime, alcohol 2 hours before, and screens 1 hour before to reduce jet lag); Compare medical evacuation coverage across typical policy tiers (Budget tiers often cap evacuation near $50,000–$100,000, while premium tiers commonly reach $500,000 or more. Confirm whether transport goes to the nearest facility or home); Tell me the best area to stay in Berlin for sightseeing (Mitte puts you near the Brandenburg Gate, Museum Island, and Unter den Linden. Kreuzberg is cheaper and livelier, with good U-Bahn links); Can I take a lighter on a plane (One disposable lighter is usually allowed on your person but not in checked bags, and rules vary by country).

summaries.title: Writing help
summaries.text: The user asked: Give me a polite opener for a follow-up email ('I hope this finds you well — I wanted to gently follow up on my earlier message' works as a warm opening); How can I tailor my CV to a job description (Tailor your CV by matching keywords from the job description in your skills and experience sections, and by highlighting achievements most relevant to the role); Write 'Happy birthday' in Italian ('Happy birthday' in Italian is 'Buon compleanno'); What's the best way to tailor a CV to a job posting (Mirror the posting's key terms in your skills and bullet points, and reorder sections so the most relevant experience appears first. Use the exact wording for tools and certifications where honest); Pull out the three most important numbers from this piece (It cites 1.5°C of warming, a $2 trillion annual cost, and 600 million people living in low-lying coastal zones); Is "Just Do It" a slogan or a tagline (It's generally treated as Nike's tagline, since it has endured for decades as a brand-level signature. Slogans are more campaign-specific).
